text:
1.March 15, 2024 — CFP MOU is agreed to-21 months before Jenn Cohen said she was “surprised” by it and used it as an excuse to scuttle negotiations. The FBS conferences agreed to the CFP framework beginning in 2026. Contemporary reporting specifically noted that ND had protections in the agreement.
2. July 24, 2024 — Riley publicly raises the possibility of sacrificing the ND rivalry. At USC’s first Big Ten Media Day, Riley said he would love to continue the series but added: “Now if you get in a position where you got to make a decision on what’s best for SC to help us win a national championship vs. keeping that, shoot, then you got to look at it.” He also noted that other schools had “sacrifice[d] rivalry games.” 
3. February 14, 2025 — Jenn Cohen makes continuation of the series conditional. Cohen called USC–ND “such an important series” and said, “In an ideal world, we’re going to keep playing each other,” but immediately cited BigX travel and unanswered questions about CFP access, seeding and selection, saying USC would continue evaluating “what’s best” for its program. 
4. May 2025 — ND publicly commits to continuing; USC offered only to extend the rivalry only through 2026, with its willingness to commit beyond that hinging substantially on the future CFP format and the number of automatic BigX bids. MF, by contrast, said: “I want to play them every single year. When? I don’t care … Start of the season, middle of the season, end of the season.” 
5. May 20, 2025 — national criticism intensifies; SI’s Pat Forde wrote that throwing away USC–ND for an easier schedule would be “a crime against football.”
6. July 24, 2025 — Riley says he wants the game, but again conditions it on USC’s competitive interests.He again tied the rivalry’s future and timing to CFP structure and USC’s perceived competitive disadvantage. 
7. Summer–October 2025 — USC moves toward a multiyear compromise and the schools nearly reach agreement. USC amended its original short-term proposal to accommodate ND’s demand for a multiyear deal. By the October meeting in South Bend, the schools were close to an agreement, and USC was warming to continuing the traditional scheduling arrangement through 27. 
8. November 14, 2025 — Cohen explicitly wrote that USC wanted nonconference games at home “in the Coliseum as early as possible every year,” called scheduling one of USC’s few controllable “strategic levers,” and argued that making USC’s CFP road more difficult than its Big Ten peers “does not align with our goal to win championships.” 
9. December 2025 — USC reverses its compromise. Reporting revealed that under the 2024 MOU, ND would be guaranteed a CFP berth beginning in 26 if ranked in the top 12 under a 12-team format. The LA Times reported that USC officials claimed they “were not aware” of that provision and regarded it as a “material advantage.” Cohen then reversed course and told ND that the 2026 game would have to be played in Week Zero — or not at all. 
10. December 22, 2025 — USC–ND is officially put on hiatus. The Times reported that USC nevertheless intended to seek another opponent for Week Zero; because USC itself did not qualify for the ordinary Hawaii/international-game exception, it would generally need an opponent possessing such an exemption. 
11. December 22–23, 2025 — Keyshawn Johnson blasts his alma mater. The former USC All-American wrote: “This is ridiculous! Just say we scared. I’ll accept that at least it’s the truth.” He added: “We running from teams now? We running from Notre Dame?”, questioned why USC would cancel its biggest rivalry, and criticized both the athletic department and Riley for not understanding what it means to be a Trojan. 
12. December 23, 2025 — Nicole Auerbach’s reporting directly contradicts USC’s “not aware” explanation. Auerbach reported that all 18 BigX schools received the full CFP MOU language in March 2024, which was unanimously supported by all current and incoming members including USC.

text:
Key Themes

The oil shock has metastasized into a full macro repricing event. WTI above $90 and Brent approaching $95 aren't just energy stories: they're forcing a global rates reckoning now synchronizing sovereign selloffs from Tokyo to London, pushing Japan's 10-year to levels unseen since 1996 and the UK gilt to its highest since 2008, while compressing the Fed's September optionality with hike probabilities north of 65%. What makes this particularly dangerous for risk assets is the feedback loop: surging yields at the long end aren't just a valuation headwind, they're closing off the foreign bid for Treasuries at precisely the moment U.S. duration supply is heaviest, and with Warsh showing zero inclination to coordinate with Bessent, the pain trade in bonds has no political circuit-breaker. For futures traders, the acute risk is that momentum unwinds are now self-reinforcing. Mizuho flagging systematic de-risking breaking below the July lows suggests the move isn't done, while the 5% level on the 10-year acts as a psychological tripwire for equities that could force the next leg lower in a seasonally unfriendly tape already dealing with midterm uncertainty.

Market Snapshot

Pre-market futures are pricing a contained reaction (SPX -0.2%, NDX -0.5%) despite oil above $90 and 30-year yields back at pre-intervention levels, suggesting the equity market is leaning on record corporate cash balances, $1.1T YTD inflows, and DELL's AI server beat as offsetting factors. The notable Evercore ISI datapoint, 115 S&P 500 stocks now negatively correlated to the index and matching dot-com levels, suggests institutional investors have already begun rotating defensively rather than waiting for a sentiment break. That's a healthier technical posture than a 2000-style momentum crowding.

Macro

JPMorgan's Q3 GDP tracking at 2.75%, nudging toward the 3% PMI signal, is the key counterpoint to the stagflation narrative: consumer spending revised up 1pp, equipment investment on track for another 10%-plus quarter, and corporate profit growth robust enough that Feroli is flagging sub-4% unemployment as a plausible outcome. This is not a slowing economy rationalizing Fed patience. It is a resilient one that validates Warsh's hawkishness and makes the rates market's repricing of September a fundamentally sound response rather than a fear trade.

Placing the current bond selloff in historical context: the 17bp cumulative 20-day yield rise and 4.2% peak-to-trough loss are orders of magnitude below 2022's 62bp and 23% drawdown, reflecting a materially different starting point. Yields are rising from levels that already offer income cushion, and the structural demand destruction that comes from zero-yield duration is absent. The incremental headwinds, elevated sovereign issuance, AI capital competition, and diminished foreign buyer participation, are real but manageable, and for income-oriented institutional allocators the setup is becoming increasingly interesting at these levels without yet being a screaming buy.

The second U.S. strike in three days targeting Iranian radar and mine-laying infrastructure, met with drone and missile retaliation against U.S. regional bases, represents a material escalation in the Hormuz conflict rather than contained tit-for-tat. The civilian casualty narrative will intensify diplomatic pressure but shows no sign of forcing near-term de-escalation. Markets should treat the conflict as entering a prolonged attritional phase, with crude supply risk remaining a persistent rather than episodic input to the rates and inflation outlook.

Options flow is confirming directional conviction in the rate selloff: a $6.5M position targeting 30-year yields at 5.7% by November, alongside new risk in 10-year (4.85%) and 5-year (4.6%) structures, signals sophisticated players are paying up for tail protection rather than fading the move. That's a notable shift from speculative to defensive positioning in rates vol that validates the duration pain as a durable regime, not a one-day event.

JPMorgan's Peters frames the 10-year approaching 4.8% and the 30-year at 19-year highs as a genuine equity headwind, with the 5% psychological level on Treasuries representing a potential trigger for a 5-8% S&P correction, elevated but characterized as technically healthy rather than structurally damaging given the breadth of Q2's 30% earnings growth across financials, industrials, and utilities. The core bull case remains a capex-driven earnings supercycle, but September seasonality, midterm event risk, and the fading tailwind of earnings season make the risk/reward asymmetric for near-term equity longs.

Corporate

The after-hours earnings tape is a useful read on current risk tolerance: DELL's 9% surge on raised AI server guidance confirms the market continues to aggressively reward AI infrastructure capex exposure, while MDB's 14% drop despite a guidance raise and broad analyst positivity suggests the bar for software multiples is now punishing any deceleration in growth vectors like Atlas, however modest. CRDO's 9% decline after a beat on a 44%-run stock reflects the same dynamic. In this rates environment, execution must be flawless and guidance must clear an elevated bar.

Chevron's $7B five-year commitment to Venezuela's Carabobo fields represents the most significant oil major capital deployment into the country post-Maduro and is structurally meaningful as a medium-term supply story, but the timeline for material production is multi-year, offering no near-term relief to a Hormuz-constrained market. The U.S. government's simultaneous 35% stake acquisition in NABEP signals Washington is treating Venezuelan oil as a strategic energy security asset, which could complicate the market's read on how aggressively supply will be managed.

Commodity

Copper's 1.3% retreat from record-close levels encapsulates the macro conflict precisely: LME spot spreads remain over $100 above the three-month contract, confirming genuinely tight physical supply, yet the macro overlay, oil-driven inflation expectations forcing Fed tightening and crimping demand, is capping upside and dominating price action. Until the Iran/Hormuz uncertainty clears and the rates trajectory stabilizes, copper's strong fundamentals will remain hostage to macro sentiment rather than supply/demand.

Gold's $400 correction from overbought extremes (RSI 73 to 46) has mechanically reset the technical setup, but the metal is back in no-man's land rather than at a compelling entry. The gold/DXY inverse relationship remains intact, suggesting the prior move was positioning-driven excess rather than a breakdown of the debasement thesis. Without a clear directional catalyst in dollar or rates, the next tradeable edge awaits a decisive break of $4,300/50-day support or a reclaim of prior highs.

The 10% surge in 1-month Brent over the past week has become the single dominant macro variable across asset classes, with the Iran war premium now fully repriced into December '26 contracts at prior conflict highs, indicating the market is treating supply disruption as structural rather than transient. Polymarket pricing only a 30% probability of even one week of normalized Hormuz flow by year-end, combined with the imminent exhaustion of SPR drawdowns and recovering Chinese import demand, argues the oil bid is durable and the summer's cross-asset euphoria may now face a sustained headwind.

Flows and Positioning

Mizuho's momentum basket data is the most actionable positioning signal of the morning: a full round-trip below the July lows, through the levels associated with the Situational Awareness unwind, confirms that systematic de-risking has become self-fulfilling, with CTA forced selling creating a feedback loop that no longer requires a fundamental catalyst. This is a technical liquidity event layered on top of the macro deterioration, and until the momentum unwind exhausts itself, tactical buyers should be cautious about catching the equity dip.

Yesterday's market action was textbook stagflation: the WTI +5.2%/$90.22 and Brent +4.6%/$94.65 surge driven by renewed U.S.-Iran hostilities collided with Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole posture to reprice the September hike probability from roughly 40% to roughly 67%, a threshold that historically binds Fed action. The equity damage was broad (NYSE decliners 2.8:1, semis -2.1%, transports -2.5%, Russell -1.2%) but the real pain was in duration: the 10-year at its highest since January 2025, the 30-year at a 19-year high, and critically the 2-5y sector sold off in lockstep with the long end, confirming markets are pricing a genuine near-term tightening rather than a term-premium story. The move is unambiguously global: JGB 10s at 3% for the first time since 1996, Bunds at 3.35% (2011 high), Gilts at 5.25% (2008 high), each of which diminishes foreign appetite for Treasuries at precisely the moment the U.S. faces heavy duration supply. Until Warsh pivots or equities deteriorate sufficiently to force a K-blind Fed's hand, there is no structural catalyst for bond bulls.

Key Events

Today brings ADP and ISM Services, each of which will directly shape the probability distribution for a September Fed hike currently sitting around two-thirds. Broadcom reports after today's close and will be a key read on NQ versus RTY relative performance into tomorrow. Friday brings non-farm payrolls. Malibu Boats (MBUU) Rides A Saxdor Wave Into A Choppier Market https://t.co/4V1M4MWjMr 

On August 27, Malibu Boats (NASDAQ:MBUU) posted the kind of quarter that makes a rough industry stretch look like a distant memory. Fourth-quarter net sales jumped 42.7% to $295.5 million and adjusted EBITDA climbed 72.7% to $33.9 million, powered by the freshly acquired Saxdor brand and real strength in the legacy fleet. But the same earnings call that produced those headline numbers also carried warnings about a soft boat buyer and a bumpy road ahead. Both stories are true at once, and untangling them is the point. 

Marzetti's (MZTI) Record Streak Hits a Wall With Outbreak and Guidance Cut 

A Premium Brand Delivering Ahead Of Schedule 
 
The Saxdor acquisition is already paying for itself. The Finnish adventure day boat brand contributed $61.2 million in quarterly sales, beating management's own $57 million to $59 million guidance, and its boats sold for an average of $340,000 apiece versus $184,000 for the legacy fleet. That is a meaningfully richer price tag flowing straight into the top line. Just as notable, the legacy business grew on its own, with net sales up 13.2% and unit growth in both the Cobalt and Saltwater Fishing segments, evidence that this is not simply an acquisition masking a struggling core. 
 
Management also credited centralized sourcing and procurement for roughly half of the quarter's margin gains, a sign the MBI Advantage cost framework is doing real work rather than sitting on a slide deck. Looking ahead, the company guided fiscal 2027 net sales to $1.08 billion to $1.12 billion and adjusted EBITDA to $101 million to $109 million, backed by a July refinancing that pushed debt maturities out to 2031 and a fresh $70 million buyback authorization. Net leverage sits at roughly 1.2 times, well under the company's 2.5 times ceiling, even after paying for Saxdor. 
 
A Soft Buyer And A Front-Loaded Investment Year 
 
The same call that celebrated Saxdor's early performance also flagged where it fell short. The segment's adjusted EBITDA margin landed below the 10% to 11% range management had guided to, a result of added headcount ahead of volume and higher input costs, an investment the company is still waiting to see returned. Full-year gross margin slipped 180 basis points to 16%, and GAAP net income for the year cratered 88.8% to just $1.7 million, largely on acquisition and integration costs. Management was direct that fiscal 2027's first-half margins will trail the second half as Saxdor's domestic production ramps in Florida. 
 
More broadly, CFO David Black said the marine market is expected to be flat to down next year, and CEO Steve Menneto pointed to continued pressure on the payment-sensitive buyer as a key missing piece for a real industry recovery. Retail registrations were still down about 3% in the most recent quarter, an improvement from prior months but a decline nonetheless, and the fiberglass segments Malibu competes in remain more pressured than the broader powerboat market. 

Market Sentiment Versus Saxdor 

Hedge fund ownership rose from 13 funds to 23 quarter over quarter, which points to institutions building rather than trimming positions. Short interest sits at 6.98% of float, high enough to reflect a genuine skeptical camp but far from a crowded short. As of August 31, the stock trades at a forward P/E of just 11.34, a modest multiple that does not appear to be pricing in much of the growth management is guiding to. 

Conclusion 

Malibu's quarter shows a company genuinely growing through a soft cycle rather than around it, with Saxdor adding scale and price while the legacy brands hold their own. The tension is between that execution and an industry backdrop management itself called flat to down, with margins already set to lag in the first half of fiscal 2027. For the bulls, the case rests on Saxdor's margin catching up as domestic production ramps.

Adobe (ADBE) Bets Big On Saudi Arabia While Wall Street Hesitates https://t.co/iuBHkJM5f4 

On August 31, Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE) committed more than $4 billion to giving away its AI tools. The company will offer 12 months of free access to its Firefly Standard subscription and Adobe Express Premium features to more than 27 million eligible citizens and residents in Saudi Arabia, expanding its partnership with the country's Ministry of Communications and Information Technology and the government-backed AI firm Humain. The deal includes a new image generation model tuned for Saudi culture, letting users create images from Arabic-language prompts. It is a striking bet for a stock that trades like the market expects its growth to stall. 

Adobe (ADBE) Bets Big On Saudi Arabia While Wall Street Hesitates 

A Business Where AI Is Adding, Not Subtracting 
 
That confidence has some backing. Adobe's AI-first products, the newer tools built around generative features, saw their annualized recurring revenue triple year over year to more than $500 million, evidence that artificial intelligence is adding to Adobe's business rather than just threatening it. The Saudi Arabia expansion extends that momentum internationally, giving Firefly and Express a built-in user base of millions who might otherwise never try Adobe's software, in a region where Humain and the country's sovereign wealth fund are pouring money into localized AI development. 
 
The core business is not showing cracks either. Adobe's most recent quarter delivered $6.62 billion in revenue, up 13% year over year and a company record, extending two years of consistent low double-digit growth. Subscriptions make up virtually all of that revenue, and Adobe closed the quarter holding $27.1 billion of annualized recurring revenue, plus another $22.3 billion in contracted revenue still to be recognized, a backlog that gives management visibility most software companies would envy. Net margin for fiscal 2025 came in near 30%, and free cash flow neared $9.9 billion for the year, funding both new deals like the Semrush acquisition and buybacks that retired about 2% of shares outstanding in just three months. 
 
A Valuation That Still Smells Doubt 
 
Yet the stock's roughly 10 times forward earnings multiple says the market is not convinced the good times continue. The fear is straightforward: generative AI now lets anyone produce images and design work without needing Photoshop expertise, a skill that used to be the whole point of buying Adobe's software. Adobe faces that pressure not just from AI-focused startups but from Microsoft, and any regulatory shift like the European Union's AI Act could raise compliance costs and complicate how Adobe trains its own models. 

There are cracks worth watching inside the numbers too. Total annualized recurring revenue growth is tracking near 10% for the fiscal year, well below the pace of reported revenue, and a good chunk of that comes from the roughly $480 million Semrush added rather than organic demand. Adobe also wrote down about $70 million in goodwill tied to its publishing and advertising business last quarter, and it is navigating leadership turnover at the top: the chief financial officer departed in June, replaced on an interim basis, while longtime CEO Shantanu Narayen has said he will step aside once the board finds a successor. 

What The Market Is Signaling 

Hedge fund enthusiasm has cooled recently. The number of funds holding Adobe fell from 86 to 81 in the most recent quarter, suggesting some institutional investors are trimming rather than adding. Short interest sits at 5.06% of the float, enough to indicate a real bear camp has formed around the stock. Adobe's forward price-to-earnings ratio of 10.57, as of August 31, remains low for a company still growing revenue in the double digits. 

Where The Evidence Leaves Investors 

Adobe is making a multibillion-dollar wager that AI expands its business rather than replaces it, and the Saudi Arabia deal is the clearest example yet of that strategy in action. The tension sits between a market multiple already pricing in decline and a recurring revenue engine that keeps setting records. Bulls are counting on free users in Saudi Arabia and elsewhere eventually converting into paying Firefly and Express subscribers.

News Flashback

Early 2026

Jan-March

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" and Current State (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

Early 2026

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" and Current State (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

text:
Good morning from Virginia. 🇺🇸

September 2, 1901. The Minnesota State Fair. A late-summer Monday, grandstand packed with perhaps ten thousand people who had come for prize livestock, machinery, and the chance to see the Vice President of the United States.

Theodore Roosevelt was forty-two, restless even in office, a man who still looked as if he might vault a fence rather than walk around it. He had been governor of New York, Rough Rider, police commissioner, assistant secretary of the Navy. The vice presidency was supposed to have quieted him. It had not.

He spoke that morning on “National Duties.” He talked of pioneers—the men and women one generation back who had cut farms from timber and prairie and built the state those fairgoers now inhabited. He talked of work, of character, of a nation that could not live on ease. Then, almost in passing, he offered a line he had first written privately the year before and now gave to a crowd for the first time:

“Speak softly and carry a big stick — you will go far.”

He did not thunder it. He explained it. Bluster without strength was contemptible. Soft words without power behind them were useless. Courtesy toward other nations was required. So was the capacity to make those words good. The big stick was not a club to be swung for sport. It was the quiet fact of strength that made peace possible.

The local papers liked the speech. They noted the laughter and applause. They did not, for the most part, single out the proverb. It would take time for the phrase to become the man.

Four days later, in Buffalo, an anarchist shot William McKinley. For a week the President seemed to rally. Roosevelt, told the danger had passed, went into the Adirondacks. On the night of the thirteenth the word came that McKinley was dying. Roosevelt came down off Mount Marcy in the dark, reached a station at dawn, and learned the President was already gone. At 2:15 in the morning of September 14, McKinley died. That same day, in a borrowed parlor on Delaware Avenue in Buffalo, Theodore Roosevelt took the oath. Twelve days after the fairground speech, he was President of the United States—the youngest ever to hold the office.

History does not often arrange its ironies so cleanly. A man stands before a state fair and tells a nation how power ought to be carried: quietly, and with something real behind the quiet. Then the office itself is thrust into his hands before the month is out. What followed—the Navy, the Canal, the conservation of land, the insistence that the United States speak with a civil tongue and keep a fleet in being—was the working out of that afternoon in Minnesota.

The proverb was his. The moment was America’s.

Quick Read 

Minnesota's Mayo Clinic network draws medically complex retirees despite a $2,759 higher per-capita tax burden than Florida's zero-income-tax environment. 

Florida's tax edge is shrinking as coastal insurance premiums, flood coverage, and post-Surfside condo assessments add thousands annually to retiree carrying costs. 

Healthcare spending has surged to $3.83 trillion annualized nationally, nearly matching housing costs, with retirees absorbing a disproportionate share of that burden.

Sometime in the mid-sixties, retirement math changes in a way most people don't see coming. At fifty, the focus is on taxes and tee times. At sixty-five, the real questions shift to who handles the cardiac event, the hip replacement, the cancer scare, and the parent-level dementia risk that starts creeping in. That is exactly why the Minnesota versus Florida debate keeps coming up, and why the answer is not as simple as comparing state tax tables. Here is what it actually takes to make the Minnesota case work, and where that case tends to fall apart. 
 
Testing the Migration Premise Before Anything Else 
 
The clean version of the headline, retirees fleeing Florida for Minnesota, is not supported by the state population data. Florida's resident population was 23,462.52 thousand as of January 1, 2025, while Minnesota's was 5,830.40 thousand on the same date. Florida is still the larger and faster-growing retirement destination in absolute terms. What is real is a quieter counter-current: a subset of retirees, particularly those with complex or anticipated medical needs, who weigh Minnesota's healthcare depth against Florida's tax advantage and choose the north. The argument is a case for Minnesota on medical grounds, not a mass exodus.

Jacob Boomsma / iStock via Getty Images 

Why the Healthcare Argument Carries Real Weight 
 
Minnesota's healthcare footprint is unusual for a state of its size. The Mayo Clinic in Rochester anchors a network of academic medical centers, and the Twin Cities carry a density of specialists, teaching hospitals, and integrated systems that most Sun Belt metros cannot match on a per-capita basis. For a retiree whose seventies and eighties are likely to be shaped by cardiology, oncology, orthopedics, or neurology, that proximity has measurable value. 

National consumer spending data underscores why this matters: in July 2026, health care spending ran at $3,830.8 billion annualized, only modestly below housing at $3,979.8 billion, and it has climbed from $3,432.2 billion in January 2025. Healthcare is now a housing-sized line item in the national budget, and retirees carry a disproportionate share, with premium surcharges and coverage gaps quietly adding thousands more on top of the sticker price (we mapped the ones that catch retirees off guard, from IRMAA to Part D, in a free Medicare guide). 

Tax and Weather Counterweights You Cannot Wave Away 

Minnesota is not exactly known as a low-tax haven. On an income-adjusted basis, the state and local tax burden came to $7,869 per capita in the 2024 Tax Foundation data, compared with $5,110 in Florida. Minnesota taxes ordinary retirement account withdrawals at state rates, offers a Social Security subtraction that phases out once you cross middle-income thresholds, and levies a property tax that only gets partially softened by senior deferral options. Florida, by contrast, has no state income tax and no estate tax. 

Then there is winter, which is not an abstraction. Heating a house through a real season, maintaining a roof and driveway through freeze-thaw cycles, and dealing with the seasonal fall and cardiac risks that push some retirees south all carry real costs. The cost-of-living index reflects some of this. Minnesota came in at 98.621 against a national benchmark of 100, while Florida sat at 103.414, making Minnesota cheaper overall, but that gap does not include the tax line. 

Florida Offset That Quietly Narrows the Gap 

Florida's headline tax advantage has been eroded by insurance and structural inspection realities. Homeowners' premiums in coastal counties, flood coverage where required, and post-Surfside condo special assessments have added thousands of dollars per year to carrying costs in exactly the retiree corridors that used to look cheapest. The tax savings are real, but insurance and assessment costs that did not exist at this scale a decade ago are partially consuming them. 

Number, Withdrawal Rate, and Verdict 

The comparison is easier to see in plain dollars. Take the BLS average household spending of $78,535 in 2024 as a starting baseline, index it forward with the 2027 Social Security COLA tracking around 3.1%, and layer in state income tax on withdrawals for the Minnesota case. Subtract the combined Social Security for a couple claiming near full retirement age, and the remaining spending gap has to be funded from a portfolio at a sustainable withdrawal rate. Florida's version of the same budget lands lower on the spend line because withdrawals are not taxed at the state level, which translates into a smaller required portfolio before adding back insurance and assessments. 

The picture is narrower than the headline suggests. Minnesota fits the retiree whose dominant late-life risk is medical complexity, who values proximity to a Mayo-caliber system, and who can absorb a higher tax bill on withdrawals. Florida fits the retiree whose dominant risk is outliving savings, who is healthy at 65, and who will trade specialist depth for a lower structural cost of living. The trade-off comes down to which risk the retiree is actually solving for.

text:
Good morning from Virginia. 🇺🇸

September 2, 1864. Before first light the city was already lost, though the streets did not yet know it.

All that summer Atlanta had been the great prize of the West—the rail crossing, the foundries, the rolling mills, the shops that turned out rifles and saddles and shell for two Confederate armies. Joseph Johnston had given ground from Dalton to the Chattahoochee with a miserably careful hand. Jefferson Davis, impatient for a blow, put John Bell Hood in his place. Hood struck, and struck again—Peachtree Creek, the fields east of the city, Ezra Church—and the Army of Tennessee paid in young men it could not spare. Then came the siege, the shells falling into cellars and churchyards, the last railroad still open to Macon.

Sherman did not smash the gates. He slipped away south with most of his army and laid his hand on the Macon & Western at Jonesboro. On the last day of August, William Hardee threw two corps at men already dug in and was thrown back. Hood, reading the move wrong, pulled a corps toward the city as if Sherman meant to storm it. On September 1 the Federals broke Hardee’s line. The last iron road was cut.

That night Hood ordered the army out. What could not be hauled was destroyed. Eighty-one cars of powder and stores were fired. The magazines went up. Cotton burned. The explosions rolled across the dark country and were heard seven miles off by Union men still watching the Chattahoochee bridges. Refugees clung to the columns heading for Lovejoy’s Station. The Gate City emptied itself by torchlight.

Morning of the second. Mayor James Calhoun rode out Marietta Street under a white flag with a few citizens beside him. There was no Confederate general left to treat with. He met the first blue infantry and said, with the spare dignity of a man who had nothing else to offer, that the fortune of war had placed Atlanta in their hands, and that he asked protection for the women, the old, the children, and private property. The Twentieth Corps came in with flags and bands. The workshops were silent. The rails led nowhere that could still feed an army.

Sherman would telegraph Washington the next day that Atlanta was ours, and fairly won. In the North the words landed like rain after drought. Men who had grown sick of the war found they could endure it a little longer. Lincoln’s election, which had seemed to hang by a thread, steadied. From the Southern side the same news meant something colder: the industrial heart of Georgia gone, the West broken as a theater, Lee still holding the Petersburg lines while the country behind him began to come apart.

Hood’s army was not destroyed that morning. It would march north and spend itself at Franklin and Nashville. But the city that had been the South’s workshop and pride in the West was occupied without a fight in its streets, and the sound that announced it had been the South’s own magazines tearing the night open.

text:
Legend of the Seas: Royal Caribbean’s Newest Mega Ship
https://t.co/q8AE2r6Hz1
Royal Caribbean's Legend of the Seas is the third vessel in the groundbreaking Icon Class and is widely recognized as one of the world's largest cruise ships. Building on the success of Icon of the Seas and Star of the Seas, Legend combines family-focused neighborhoods, record-setting attractions, extensive dining options, and some of the most innovative accommodations at sea.
Ship Specifications
Specification Legend of the SeasClass Icon Class
Gross Tonnage Approximately 248,663 GT
Length 1,197 ft (364.8 m)
Passenger Capacity 5,610 guests (double occupancy)
Maximum Capacity Up to about 7,600 guests
Crew Approximately 2,350
Decks 20 total (18 guest decks)
Propulsion LNG-powered (Liquefied Natural Gas)
Launch and Deployment
Legend of the Seas entered service during the summer of 2026, with its maiden season sailing the Western Mediterranean before repositioning to Florida for Caribbean cruises.
Main Itineraries
Summer
7-night Western Mediterranean cruises
Barcelona, Spain departures
Rome (Civitavecchia), Italy departures
Ports including Naples, Palma de Mallorca, Marseille, Florence/Pisa (La Spezia)
Winter
Southern Caribbean cruises
Western Caribbean cruises
Departures from Fort Lauderdale
Many itineraries include Perfect Day at CocoCay, Royal Caribbean's private island.
The Eight Neighborhoods
One of the defining traits of the Icon Class is its neighborhood concept.
1. AquaDome
A transformational glass-enclosed district featuring:
AquaTheater shows
Restaurants and bars
Panoramic ocean views
2. Thrill Island
Home to:
Category 6, the largest waterpark at sea
Crown's Edge aerial adventure
Surf simulators
Rock-climbing experiences
3. Chill Island
Focused on:
Multiple resort-style pools
Swim-up bars
Relaxation spaces
4. Surfside
Designed specifically for families with young children:
Splash areas
Family dining
Carousel
Family-friendly entertainment
5. The Hideaway
Adults-focused area featuring:
Infinity pool
DJ entertainment
Beach club atmosphere
6. Royal Promenade
The ship's main indoor boulevard:
Shopping
Cafés
Lounges
Live entertainment
7. Central Park
An open-air garden neighborhood with:
Thousands of live plants
Fine dining
Quiet walking spaces
8. Suite Neighborhood
An exclusive multi-deck enclave for suite guests with:
Private sun decks
Restaurants
Lounge access
Staterooms and Suites
Legend offers more than 2,800 staterooms in dozens of categories.
Family-Friendly Cabins
For a family of four, the most popular categories are:
Interior Family Stateroom
Ocean View Family Stateroom
Balcony Stateroom
Infinite Balcony Stateroom
Surfside Family View Balcony
These typically accommodate 4 to 5 guests.
Suites
For larger families or luxury travelers:
Junior Suite
Larger living area
Balcony
Sleeps up to 4
Sunset Suite
Larger aft-facing balcony
Premium views
Grand Suite
Separate sitting area
Concierge privileges
Owner's Suite
Larger balconies
Premium benefits
Ultimate Family Townhouse
One of the most famous suite categories in the fleet:
Multi-level layout
Private entrance to Surfside
Slides and entertainment features
Accommodates larger families
Royal Loft Suite
Among the most luxurious accommodations at sea with expansive living areas and concierge service.
Dining and Restaurants
Legend features approximately 28 dining venues, among the highest counts in the cruise industry.
Complimentary Dining
Main Dining Room
Windjammer Marketplace
AquaDome Market
Surfside Eatery
Café Promenade
Sorrento's Pizza
Specialty Dining
Chops Grille
Giovanni's Italian Kitchen
Izumi Sushi
Empire/Hollywood-style Supper Club concepts
Royal Railway: Legend Station
Hooked Seafood
Celebration Table experiences
Legend introduces some exclusive dining concepts not found on earlier Icon-class ships, including Royal Railway: Legend Station and Hollywoodland Supper Club.
Entertainment
Entertainment is one area where Royal Caribbean consistently leads the industry.
AquaTheater
High-diving
Acrobatics
Water shows
Absolute Zero
Large ice arena
Professional skating productions
Broadway-style Production Shows
Full-scale theatrical performances
Live Music
Dueling Pianos
Jazz clubs
Lounges
Family Attractions
Largest waterpark at sea
Mini golf
Arcade experiences
Adventure Ocean youth programs
Relaxation Areas
Guests looking for a quieter vacation can enjoy:
Seven swimming pools
Multiple whirlpools
The Hideaway infinity pool
Vitality Spa
Adults-only retreats
Central Park
Suite sun decks
What Makes Royal Caribbean Different?
Compared with Carnival, Norwegian, MSC, Princess, and Celebrity, Royal Caribbean differentiates itself through:
Scale
Royal Caribbean operates the world's largest cruise ships.
Neighborhood Concept
No other mainstream line uses the neighborhood model to the same extent.
Adventure Activities
Surf simulators
Zipline-style attractions
Crown's Edge
Largest waterpark at sea
Family Focus
The line is often considered one of the strongest choices for multi-generational families due to extensive kids, teen, and adult programming.
Private Destinations
Perfect Day at CocoCay is widely viewed as one of the best private island experiences among major cruise lines.
When Should a Family of 4 Book?
For this type of ship, booking early is extremely important.
Best practice:
12 to 18 months ahead for standard balcony cabins.
18 to 24 months ahead for suites.
24+ months ahead for Ultimate Family Townhouse or Royal Loft categories.
The lowest fares and best cabin selection generally appear when itineraries are first released.
Approximate Pricing for a Family of 4
Prices vary greatly by season and itinerary, but typical ranges are:
Cabin Type 7-Night Cruise for Family of 4Interior $3,500 to $6,000
Ocean View $4,000 to $7,000
Balcony $5,500 to $9,000
Junior Suite $8,000 to $14,000
Grand Suite $12,000 to $20,000+
Owner's Suite $18,000 to $35,000+
Ultimate Family Townhouse $40,000 to $100,000+
These are broad estimates based on current Icon-class pricing patterns and can vary substantially by sailing date, demand, and promotions.
Bottom Line
Legend of the Seas represents the latest evolution of Royal Caribbean's Icon Class: a 248,663-ton LNG-powered megaship carrying over 5,600 passengers and more than 2,300 crew. With eight neighborhoods, nearly 30 dining venues, extensive family accommodations, and some of the most ambitious entertainment and water attractions at sea, it is designed to be a destination in itself rather than simply transportation between ports.

text:
The Top Commercial Freighter Aircraft of the Last 30 Years
Air cargo moves roughly 60-70 million metric tons of freight annually worldwide while carrying goods worth trillions of dollars. During the past 30 years, a handful of widebody freighters have dominated global logistics, e-commerce, pharmaceuticals, aerospace transport, and express-package delivery.
The most successful freighters have not necessarily been the largest. Success is usually measured by a combination of payload, operating economics, fleet size, reliability, and customer adoption.
Top 5 Commercial Freighter Aircraft
Aircraft Entry into Service Years in Service (2026) Max PayloadBoeing 747-8F 2011 ~15 years 134-137 tonnes
Boeing 777F 2009 ~17 years 102-107 tonnes
Boeing 767-300F 1995 ~31 years 57 tonnes
MD-11F 1991 ~35 years ~92 tonnes
Airbus A330-200F 2010 ~16 years ~70 tonnes
Largest Customers
FedEx Express
The world's largest cargo airline. It transports roughly 18 billion cargo tonne-kilometers (CTKs) annually.
Primary fleet:
Boeing 777F
Boeing 767F
MD-11F
UPS Airlines
Transports approximately 15 billion CTKs annually.
Primary fleet:
Boeing 747-8F
Boeing 767F
MD-11F
Qatar Airways Cargo
About 15.2 billion CTKs annually.
Atlas Air
World's largest operator of 747 freighters. Roughly 11.5 billion CTKs annually.
DHL Aviation
Handles approximately 2.5 million tonnes of cargo annually.
Purchase Price
Actual transaction prices are usually 30-60% below list price.
Aircraft Approximate New Purchase PriceBoeing 747-8F US$419 million
Boeing 777F US$352 million
Boeing 767-300F US$220 million
Airbus A330-200F US$235 million
Airbus A350F (upcoming) Estimated US$340-370 million based on recent industry pricing and orders
Which Is the Most Versatile?
Boeing 767-300F
The 767F is widely regarded as the most versatile because:
Operates from shorter runways
Fits medium-volume routes
Lower operating cost
Compatible with many regional airports
Excellent reliability
Popular for express parcel networks
It is often called the "Swiss Army knife" of cargo aviation.
Which Is the Most Durable?
Boeing 747 Freighter Family
The 747F has demonstrated exceptional structural longevity.
Advantages:
Extremely strong airframe
Nose-loading door
Proven on long-haul, heavy-lift routes
Many aircraft remain productive after 25-35 years
The 747 platform remains the benchmark for heavy freight durability.
Which Is the Most Efficient?
Boeing 777F
Industry experts generally consider the 777F the most efficient large freighter currently in service.
Benefits:
Two engines instead of four
Lower fuel burn
Long range
Lower maintenance costs
The aircraft became the dominant long-haul cargo platform largely because of these economics.
Future winner:
Airbus A350F and Boeing 777-8F are expected to surpass today's 777F efficiency.
Longest Range Fully Loaded
Aircraft Range with Max PayloadBoeing 777F ~9,200 km (4,970 nm)
Boeing 747-8F ~7,630-8,000 km
Airbus A350F (planned) ~8,700 km (4,700 nm)
Boeing 767F ~6,100 km
Among aircraft currently in service, the 777F flies the farthest with a full payload.
Typical Turnaround Time
Aircraft Typical Cargo Turnaround767F 1.5-2 hours
777F 2-3 hours
A330F 2-3 hours
MD-11F 2-3 hours
747-8F 3-4 hours
Express-carrier hubs can achieve faster times through highly automated loading systems.
Can All International Airports Accommodate These Aircraft?
No.
Boeing 747-8F
Requires:
Long runways (typically 3,000 m+)
Strong pavement
High-capacity cargo facilities
Boeing 777F
Can access more airports but still requires major cargo infrastructure.
Boeing 767F and A330F
Can use a much larger number of international airports.
Antonov An-124
Only a limited number of airports can routinely accommodate it due to weight, pavement strength, and loading requirements.
Passenger-to-Freighter Modifications
When an airliner becomes a freighter, engineers typically add:
Floor Reinforcement
Cargo produces highly concentrated loads.
Main Deck Cargo Door
Large side-loading door added.
Smoke Detection Systems
Enhanced fire detection and suppression.
Fuselage Strengthening
Additional structural members.
Cargo Handling Systems
Rollers, locks, and pallet guides.
Window Removal
Passenger windows are plugged and reinforced.
Weight Optimization
Seats, galleys, lavatories, and cabin systems removed.
These conversions can extend useful life by 15-20 years.
What Share of Freight Moves in Combi Aircraft?
True "combi" aircraft (passengers plus freight on the main deck) now account for only a small share of global air cargo.
Estimated:
Less than 5% of worldwide air freight
Most cargo now travels either:
dedicated freighters, or
in the lower-deck holds ("belly cargo") of passenger airliners
Many older combi fleets have been retired because dedicated freighters and long-range twinjets are more economical.
Top Combi Aircraft Types
Historically the most important:
Aircraft StatusBoeing 747-400 Combi Most successful combi ever built
Boeing 747-200 Combi Retired from most fleets
Boeing 737-700C Active in specialized markets
Boeing 737-400 Combi Limited use
ATR 72 Combi Common in regional and remote operations
Additional notable types:
Boeing 757 Combi
Airbus A321P2F (mixed cargo/passenger configurations in some operators)
Dash 8 Combi
BAe 146QT/QC quick-change aircraft
Bottom Line
If one aircraft best represents air freight success over the last 30 years, it is the Boeing 777F. It has become the industry's standard large freighter because it balances payload, range, reliability, and fuel efficiency better than any previous cargo aircraft.
If maximum capacity and oversized cargo capability are the priority, the Boeing 747-8F remains unmatched among production commercial freighters thanks to its nose-loading design and payload exceeding 134 tonnes.

text:
Dear Tesla Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for September 3 https://t.co/cbO9HAKb7s 

EV Charging 6 by Sophia Jonas via Unsplash 

Tesla (TSLA) CEO Elon Musk has never been shy about pursuing ambitious ideas, and Tesla itself helped create the electric vehicle (EV) market that exists today. Now, investors have another Musk-backed vision to watch: the Cybercab and Tesla's broader push toward autonomous transportation. 
 
The EV giant is scheduled to host its Cybercab event in Austin on Thursday, Sept. 3, promoting it with a poster reading "Exclusive Access: Cybercab." The invite-only gathering is for the top scorers in Tesla's Robotaxi rider sweepstakes, while everyone else is expected to follow the launch through a livestream.  
 
More News from Barchart 
 
Reeling back, Tesla unveiled the Cybercab concept at the 'We, Robot' event in October 2024 at Warner Bros. Studios in Los Angeles, and pilot production reportedly began at Gigafactory Texas in February 2026. Meanwhile, Tesla launched its Austin Robotaxi service with modified Model Y vehicles running FSD with safety monitors, later removing monitors on some routes. 
 
That service has now logged more than 380,000 unsupervised miles without a notable incident, according to Tesla's disclosures. Therefore, the Sept. 3 event could mark the next major step of bringing dedicated Cybercab hardware into an autonomous service already operating in the real world. 
 
It would also offer a clearer look at the quick pace in which Tesla can turn its autonomous-driving ambitions into a scalable business, making the company's execution from here particularly important for the stock. 
 
About Tesla Stock  
 
The Austin, Texas-based Tesla designs, manufactures, leases, and sells EVs and energy products worldwide. With a market cap of $1.38 trillion, its portfolio spans electric cars, Superchargers, solar systems, Powerwall and Megapack batteries, and related services.  
 
Beyond hardware, Tesla develops autonomous-driving systems, artificial intelligence (AI), vehicle software, and battery technologies. Even so, its stock performance has been uneven, reflecting investor worries about slowing growth, fierce competition, margin pressure, and elevated spending on AI and autonomous-driving projects.  
 
In the last 52 weeks, Tesla's shares are up 6.48%, yet its year-to-date (YTD) performance shows an 18.1% decline. However, the picture improved during the last month, when the stock gained 18.37%. Investor optimism around robotaxis, Cybercab development, improving deliveries, and the electric Semi helped fuel the recent monthly rebound. 

https://t.co/7RFrR4tPLe 

From a valuation perspective, TSLA stock is trading at 196.74 times forward adjusted price-to-earnings and 12.99 times sales. Both measures remain above industry averages and their own five-year average multiples, indicating that investors continue to assign the company a premium valuation relative to many of its peers across the sector. 

A Closer Look at Tesla's Q2 Earnings 

On July 22, Tesla unveiled its Q2 FY2026 earnings results, with revenue rising 25.5% year-over-year (YOY) to $28.24 billion and surpassing analyst estimates of $25.71 billion. However, adjusted EPS dipped 17.5% from the year-ago value to $0.33, and also fell short of the Street's $0.51 forecast. 

Looking beneath the headline figures, Tesla's core automotive business generated $20.52 billion in revenue, a 23.1% increase from a year ago. Its energy business, covering solar and battery energy storage systems, posted $3.14 billion, up 12.5% YOY. Services and other revenue surged 50.4% to $4.58 billion. 

Yet, costs moved considerably faster than sales as Tesla increased spending on AI and other research and development initiatives. Operating expenses rose 47.3% from the previous year's quarter to $4.35 billion in Q2, pushing the operating margin down sharply to 1.4% from 4.1% a year ago. 

Operationally, Musk continued steering Tesla beyond conventional vehicle sales, emphasizing its driverless Robotaxi service, increasing Cybercab production, and converting older Fremont, California, factory lines for Optimus humanoid robots. He also promised an AI-powered machine that could serve as a babysitter, factory worker, or world-class surgeon. 

Financially, free cash flow swung negative, recording a $1.1 billion deficit versus $146 million a year ago. Capital expenditures soared 142% to $5.79 billion from $2.39 billion in the same quarter last year, while management said capex would exceed $25 billion this year.  

On the other hand, analysts expect Q3 FY2026 EPS to fall 29.7% YOY to $0.26. Full-year FY2026 EPS is estimated to decline 19.3% YOY to $0.88. Meanwhile, FY2027 EPS is projected to grow 56.8% from the previous year to $1.38. 

What Do Analysts Expect for Tesla Stock? 

Wall Street remains bullish on Tesla, with its stock carrying an overall "Moderate Buy" rating. Of the 42 analysts covering the name, 15 recommend "Strong Buy," two favor "Moderate Buy," 20 advise investors to "Hold," and five issue a "Strong Sell" call. 

Price targets have moved higher as well, adding another layer of optimism to the outlook. The average price target is $397.60, implying an upside of 8.7% from current levels. Meanwhile, the Street-High target of $600 points to a potential gain of 64%.

text:
Beyond Mykonos and Santorini: Why Naxos, Paros, and Rhodes Are Greece’s Rising Luxury Island Trio
For years, travelers dreaming of the Greek islands gravitated almost automatically toward Santorini and Mykonos. Today, however, a growing number of discerning travelers are looking beyond the usual hotspots in search of authenticity, exceptional cuisine, rich history, and luxury without the overwhelming crowds. Increasingly, that search is leading them to Naxos, Paros, and Rhodes.
Together, these three islands offer a compelling blend of Cycladic charm, elegant hospitality, ancient heritage, and sophisticated culinary experiences. For couples seeking a week of island-hopping, they represent one of the most rewarding journeys in the Mediterranean.
Naxos: The Soul of the Cyclades
As the largest island in the Cyclades, Naxos offers a more authentic and relaxed atmosphere than many of its famous neighbors. The island combines spectacular beaches, fertile farmland, mountain villages, and significant archaeological sites. It was an important center of ancient Cycladic civilization and remains deeply connected to traditional Greek culture.
The People
Naxians are known for their warmth, hospitality, and strong connection to local traditions. Unlike islands dominated solely by tourism, Naxos still has thriving agricultural communities, allowing visitors to experience everyday Greek island life.
The Cuisine
Naxos is considered one of Greece's culinary treasures. Local specialties include:
Naxian graviera cheese
Slow-roasted lamb and goat
Fresh seafood
Potatoes that are famous throughout Greece
Kitron, a citrus-based local liqueur
Many luxury travelers are drawn to farm-to-table experiences, vineyard visits, and traditional tavernas that remain family-owned.
Cultural Highlights
The iconic Portara, the massive marble gateway overlooking Naxos Town
Venetian castles and architecture
Byzantine churches
Mountain villages such as Apeiranthos and Filoti
Mount Zas, linked in mythology to Zeus
Paros: The Chic Cycladic Favorite
If Naxos is the soul of the Cyclades, Paros is its stylish younger sibling. The island has quietly evolved into one of Greece's most fashionable destinations, attracting travelers who appreciate boutique luxury, sophisticated dining, and vibrant harbor towns without the intensity of Mykonos.
The People
Parians have embraced tourism while preserving their traditional island identity. Visitors encounter a blend of fishermen, artisans, entrepreneurs, and restaurateurs who have helped shape Paros into a refined yet welcoming destination.
The Cuisine
Paros has emerged as one of Greece's strongest dining destinations, featuring:
Fresh octopus and seafood
Sun-dried fish specialties
Local wines
Cycladic cheeses
Modern Greek fine dining
Naoussa Harbor, in particular, has become a hotspot for upscale restaurants and sunset cocktails.
Cultural Highlights
Paros carries a rich heritage stretching back to antiquity. The island was famous for its prized white marble, which was used in many masterpieces of classical Greek sculpture.
Visitors enjoy:
Whitewashed villages
Historic Parikia
The picturesque harbor of Naoussa
Byzantine churches
Traditional fishing communities
Rhodes: Greece's Medieval Jewel
Located in the Dodecanese rather than the Cyclades, Rhodes offers an entirely different dimension of Greek island travel. Here, visitors discover a remarkable mix of Greek, Byzantine, Ottoman, and Crusader influences.
The People
Rhodes has long been an international crossroads. Its residents are known for their cosmopolitan outlook, influenced by centuries of trade and cultural exchange.
The Cuisine
Rhodes' cuisine reflects both Aegean and Eastern Mediterranean traditions:
Fresh seafood
Honey-infused desserts
Stuffed vine leaves
Locally produced olive oils
Traditional meze spreads
Rhodian wines
The island's culinary scene ranges from family-run tavernas to luxury resort dining.
Cultural Highlights
The centerpiece of Rhodes is its extraordinary UNESCO-listed Medieval Old Town, one of the best-preserved medieval cities in Europe.
Highlights include:
Palace of the Grand Master
Street of the Knights
Ancient Lindos
Magnificent beaches
Ancient Greek and Byzantine monuments
For history enthusiasts, few Mediterranean islands can compete with Rhodes.
Why Luxury Travelers Are Paying Attention
Several factors explain why these islands are attracting affluent travelers:
1. Authenticity Without Sacrificing Comfort
Luxury today increasingly means meaningful experiences rather than simply lavish accommodations. These islands deliver both.
2. Lower Crowds Than Iconic Greek Hotspots
While tourism is growing, visitors often find a more relaxed atmosphere than on Santorini or Mykonos.
3. Strong Culinary Identity
Each island offers distinct regional specialties and growing fine-dining scenes.
4. Boutique Luxury
Travelers increasingly favor stylish small hotels, private villas, and personalized experiences over large resorts.
5. Exceptional Diversity
Within one trip, visitors can experience:
Cycladic island life
Mountain villages
Ancient ruins
Medieval cities
World-class beaches
Ideal 7-Day Luxury Island-Hopping Itinerary for a Couple
Days 1-3: Paros
Base: Naoussa
Activities:
Sunset strolls through Naoussa Harbor
Catamaran cruise around Antiparos
Fine dining overlooking the sea
Explore Parikia's historic center
Beach club day at Kolymbithres
Recommended Luxury Stay
$500-$1,000 per night
Days 4-5: Naxos
Base: Naxos Town or Plaka Beach
Activities:
Visit the Portara at sunset
Private food and wine tour
Explore mountain villages
Beach relaxation at Plaka
Farm-to-table dining experiences
Recommended Luxury Stay
$400-$900 per night
Days 6-7: Rhodes
Base: Rhodes Old Town or Lindos
Activities:
Private walking tour of the Medieval City
Sunset dinner in Lindos
Yacht excursion along the eastern coast
Explore ancient archaeological sites
Recommended Luxury Stay
$600-$1,500 per night
Approximate Luxury Cost for One Week (Couple)
Category Estimated CostLuxury Hotels $4,000-$7,000
Domestic Flights & Ferries $500-$1,000
Fine Dining $1,000-$1,800
Private Tours & Excursions $1,000-$2,500
Transfers & Miscellaneous $500-$1,000
Total $7,000-$13,000+
For travelers opting for premium suites, private yacht charters, and Michelin-level dining, costs can easily exceed $15,000 for the week.
The Bottom Line
Naxos, Paros, and Rhodes represent a new generation of Greek luxury destinations. They offer what many sophisticated travelers increasingly seek: authentic culture, exceptional food, beautiful accommodations, fascinating history, and a sense of discovery that some of Greece's most famous islands have begun to lose. The result is a Greek island journey that feels both refined and genuinely connected to the country's rich heritage.

text:
Tesla Is Raising Cybertruck Prices in the U.S. by $5,000. What This Means for TSLA Stock. https://t.co/ikgKiA5cnV 

Tesla Cybertruck by Tada Images via Shutterstock 

Tesla (TSLA) is raising the price of its Cybertruck in the United States, putting a fresh spotlight on the electric vehicle (EV) maker's effort to balance demand with profitability. The company increased the starting prices for both the Dual Motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) and the Premium AWD Cybertruck by $5,000.  
 
These price increases stand out because they reverse Tesla's earlier reliance on price cuts to sustain vehicle demand. In its latest reported quarter, Tesla generated $28.24 billion in revenue, up 26% year-over-year (YOY). 
 
More News from Barchart 
 
The focus arrives as the global EV market continues to expand. Its market value is projected to grow from $1.15 trillion in 2025 to $1.86 trillion by 2035, supported by emissions policies, government incentives, lower battery costs, broader charging networks, and longer driving ranges. 
 
Tesla may see little direct earnings impact from Cybertruck alone. Still, the decision could provide a useful signal about the company's confidence in the truck's premium positioning. Can the $5,000 price increases support Tesla's margin recovery, or will the move make the Cybertruck a harder sell in an increasingly competitive EV market? Let's dive in.  
 
About Tesla Stock 
 
Tesla is an Austin, Texas-based EV and clean energy company. The firm designs, manufactures, and sells electric vehicles, battery storage systems, solar energy products, charging equipment, and software services, while developing autonomous driving (AD) technology, robotics, and artificial intelligence (AI) computing infrastructure. 
 
TSLA stock ended Aug. 28 at $348.75 per share. Currently, the stock is down by 19% since the start of the year but up almost 6% over the last 52 weeks.   

https://t.co/7RFrR4tPLe 

With a $1.38 trillion market capitalization, Tesla trades at 393 times trailing earnings and 14.7 times sales. That is sharply above the sector medians for both multiples. 
 
Released on July 22, Tesla's second-quarter 2026 report showed revenue of $28.24 billion, topping the $26.71 billion consensus estimate and representing 26% YOY growth. However, non-GAAP EPS came in at $0.33, missing the $0.54 analyst estimate. 
 
Gross margin was 16.8%, down from 17.2% in the prior-year quarter, while operating margin fell to 1.4% from 4.1%. Net income reached $1.11 billion. 

Meanwhile, net cash provided by operating activities climbed 85% YOY to $4.69 billion, providing an important offset to the weaker earnings result. Free cash flow also fell to -$1.1 billion, representing a YOY deterioration. 

Tesla produced 451,758 vehicles and delivered 480,126 vehicles during the quarter. That delivery volume exceeded production by 28,368 units, helping the company's revenue beat.  

Tesla's Cybertruck Pricing Shifts 

Tesla has moved quickly between price points as it works to position the Cybertruck in the U.S. pickup market. Earlier this year, in February, the company launched a lower-priced Cybertruck at $59,990. The company also reduced the Cyberbeast price by $15,000, from $114,990 to $99,990. These changes expanded the lineup's reach and were intended to support delivery growth. 

The most recent price adjustment takes the strategy in the opposite direction. Tesla raised the Dual Motor AWD price to $74,990 from $69,990 and also increased the Premium AWD price to $84,990 from $79,990. These $5,000 increases amount to a 7.1% price hike for the Dual Motor AWD and 6.3% hike for the Premium AWD, although the Cyberbeast remains priced at $99,990. 

This narrower gap can steer buyers toward higher-priced configurations. It also increases Tesla's revenue on every Cybertruck delivered.  

However, the benefit depends on whether the company can preserve order volume at the new prices. A higher sticker price without added range, features, or capability gives buyers less obvious incremental value. 

The repricing also arrives as Tesla handles wider operational considerations. China's State Administration for Market Regulation recently ordered the recall of about 2.98 million China-made and imported Tesla EVs. 

Chinese authorities plan to prohibit hidden door handles in 2027. The policy follows incidents in which electronic handles failed after collisions, preventing occupants from exiting or rescuers from entering. 

Together, the Cybertruck repricing and China recall place greater importance on Tesla's ability to execute across its product portfolio while protecting demand, managing safety compliance, and improving vehicle-level profitability.  

Wall Street's Long-Term Case 

The next quarterly report will show whether higher pricing has helped, with Tesla scheduled to report Q3 results on Oct. 28. Analysts expect EPS of $0.26 for the September quarter, but that estimate trails the $0.37 seen in the prior-year period, pointing to a 30% YOY decline in earnings. 

RBC Capital analyst Tom Narayan offered a more bullish assessment on July 7. Narayan reiterated an "Outperform" rating and raised his TSLA stock price target to $500 from $475, representing 36% potential upside from current levels. His call reflects continued confidence in Tesla's long-term prospects despite near-term earnings pressure. 

Bank of America also maintains a bullish view, recently rating TSLA stock as a "Buy" with a $460 price target, which represents 25% potential upside from here. The firm's thesis hinges on Tesla's ability to scale its technology efficiently and establish a leading position in robotaxis. 

The broader outlook on Wall Street remains constructive. Based on 42 analysts with coverage, TSLA stock has a consensus "Moderate Buy" rating and an average price target of $397.60, suggesting potential upside of 8% from current levels. 

https://t.co/7RFrR4tPLe 

https://t.co/7RFrR4tPLe 

Conclusion 

Tesla's Cybertruck price increases offer a modest positive for TSLA stock because the move could improve revenue per vehicle and support automotive margins. Still, the benefit depends on whether buyers remain willing to pay $74,990 or more. Higher pricing alone will not offset weaker earnings expectations or resolve execution issues in China and AI hardware. The most likely outcome is a limited near-term margin lift, with TSLA stock's direction still tied to deliveries, profitability, and robotaxi progress.

Dak Prescott (QB, DAL): 2026 outlook

Dak Prescott enters his eleventh season in the league as a firmly established veteran quarterback. Stability is the defining trait of his outlook, backed by two seasons of consistent usage in the same offensive system and a strong 95.1 percent snap share from last year. The Dallas offense continues to lean heavily on his arm. Projections point toward a high volume of work with 34.55 pass attempts per game supported by a market-implied team total of 25.5 points per game. That volume provides a secure weekly floor.

Efficiency remains a strong suit. Prescott posted a plus-five percent completion percentage over expected mark, proving he routinely delivers accurate throws independent of scheme alone. Recent games highlight his heavy involvement in the passing attack, topping 30 pass attempts in four of his last five outings to close out the previous year, including a 47-attempt game against Detroit and a 37-attempt performance against Washington. While rushing output is minimal and mostly consists of a few scrambles per game, his value relies almost entirely on efficient passing volume and high-scoring team context.

Risk comes primarily from the lack of a rushing floor, which can occasionally leave his scoring dependent on multi-touchdown passing performances. Furthermore, 7.4 percent of team targets are newly vacated in the offense, which could subtly alter how the passing tree distributes looks early in the year. The schedule offers a slight edge overall with an opponent strength index of 1.027 against his position, but relying heavily on pocket efficiency without a high volume of rushing scores means he needs the passing game to click immediately to sustain his ceiling.

What to watch:
• Monitor how the passing game absorbs the newly vacated 7.4 percent target share early in the season.
• Expect heavy pass volume with a projected 34.55 attempts per game driving his floor.
• Watch his completion percentage over expected to maintain the elite efficiency mark of plus-five percent.
• Recognize the lack of rushing equity, as his fantasy scoring relies heavily on passing efficiency and touchdowns.

🇪🇸 THE END OF SOCIALIST SPAIN IS COMING — A 10-POINT PLAN FOR A FREE SPAIN @ppopular
Spain can become one of Europe’s great success stories again: prosperous, secure, Atlanticist, pro-European and confident. My vision is not isolation, nationalism or nostalgia. It is a Free Spain firmly anchored in Europe, NATO and the democratic West.
My 10-point programme:
1. FLAT TAX 15%
Replace excessive complexity with a simple, competitive 15% flat tax. Reward work, investment, entrepreneurship and growth. Spain should become one of Europe’s best places to build a company and create jobs.
2. RECOGNISE KOSOVO 🇽🇰
Spain should finally recognise the Republic of Kosovo. Support Kosovo’s membership in the Council of Europe, NATO and the European Union. A European Spain should support a European Kosovo.
3. UKRAINE VICTORY 🇺🇦
No appeasement of Russian aggression. Spain must support Ukraine politically, economically and militarily until a just and sustainable peace is secured. Ukraine belongs in NATO and the EU.
4. STAND WITH ISRAEL 🇮🇱
Spain should rebuild a strong strategic partnership with Israel based on security cooperation, trade, technology and democratic partnership while supporting diplomacy and civilian protection throughout the region.
5. RENEW THE ALLIANCE WITH THE USA 🇺🇸
Spain needs a powerful transatlantic partnership with the United States. Madrid and Washington should cooperate more closely on NATO, defence, energy, technology, investment and global security.
6. STRONG NATO SPAIN
Spain must become a serious European defence power. Modern armed forces, stronger deterrence and adequate defence investment are essential. A strong Spain means a stronger NATO.
7. BUILD HOMES — NOT BUREAUCRACY 🏠
Spain’s housing shortage will not be solved by slogans. Free land for development, accelerate permits, encourage construction and give investors, landlords and tenants legal certainty. Build, build, build.
8. ENERGY FREEDOM ⚡
Keep nuclear power. Expand renewables, grids, storage and European interconnections. Spain should offer its citizens and industries abundant, reliable and affordable energy.
9. RULE OF LAW & CLEAN GOVERNMENT ⚖️
Independent courts. Transparent public procurement. Zero tolerance for corruption. Equal citizenship and respect for Spain’s constitutional institutions must stand above partisan interests.
10. SPAIN LEADS EUROPE 🇪🇺
Spain should lead a stronger European Union: competitive Single Market, strong Euro, enlargement, defence cooperation, transatlantic partnership and economic reform. Europe needs Spain at the centre of its future.
