text:
The Fox News story is authentic. The two deaths happened, were confirmed by state health departments, and are independently reported by local and national outlets. No credible sources dispute the core facts.
What the article claims vs. what is confirmed
Fox News (Melissa Rudy, Sept. 1, 2026) reported that a North Carolina teenager died from Naegleria fowleri (the “brain-eating amoeba”) shortly after an 8-year-old girl in Louisiana died of the same rare infection. That matches the record.
North Carolina case

NCDHHS announced Aug. 27, 2026 that a central North Carolina teen was critically ill with primary amebic meningoencephalitis (PAM) caused by Naegleria fowleri.
NCDHHS later confirmed the teen died Aug. 31, 2026 and issued condolences while withholding further identifiers to protect the family. Multiple outlets (WRAL, Charlotte Observer, USA Today, Newsweek, ABC11) received the same confirmation.
The family identified him on a GoFundMe as Moises Ponce Mendoza. His mother, Monica Mendoza, wrote that severe headaches began the illness; he was seen at a Burlington hospital Aug. 21, sent home, then taken to UNC Hospitals the next day, placed in a coma, and treated for the amoeba. NCDHHS itself did not name him.

Louisiana case

Lillian Smart, 8, of Ruston, died Aug. 22, 2026 (the day after her birthday). The family posted that brain injuries were too severe to recover from.
Louisiana Department of Health announced a confirmed Naegleria fowleri case Aug. 19, most likely acquired swimming in Lake Claiborne. The family and local reporting connected that case to Lillian. Gov. Jeff Landry publicly offered condolences.

The “just days after” framing is a bit compressed (LA death Aug. 22, NC death Aug. 31), but both cases occurred in the same late-summer window when these infections typically appear.
Sources that agree
Official and mainstream reporting is consistent:

NCDHHS press release and follow-up statements to reporters
WRAL, News & Observer / Charlotte Observer, ABC11, WBTV, Queen City News
USA Today, Newsweek, HuffPost, CBS
Louisiana Department of Health announcement plus family statements and local coverage (Shreveport Times, https://t.co/NIEG3JlqwJ, WDSU)

CDC background on the organism also matches what Fox and the state agencies described: infection only when contaminated warm freshwater is forced up the nose (not by swallowing), rapid progression after nonspecific early symptoms, and very high fatality. Typical U.S. incidence is fewer than 10 cases a year; historical tallies are on the order of ~167–180 U.S. cases since the mid-20th century with only a handful of survivors.

He did not dabble in the Ardern gay-race-communist nation destroying project. He ran the shop floor: Education, COVID Response, Public Service, Leader of the House, then the ten-month caretaker premiership after the brand collapsed & she ran away like a cowardly dog.

The contempt he attracts is not mystery psychology. It is the residue of a government that preached kindness while building a money printing compliance state, & of the loyal lieutenant who still will not admit what that state was.

The career politician in a flakey sausage-roll costume

Christopher John Hipkins, born 5/09/1978 in the Hutt Valley, is the most complete parliamentary lifer Labour has produced since the Clark nursery. Head boy. Victoria U students’ association president. Arrested at a 1997 Parliament protest (charges dropped, apology later—the origin myth).

Then the building & never out of it: adviser to Trevor Mallard & Helen Clark, Industry Training Federation, into Rimutaka in 2008 at 30, whip, education spokesperson, cabinet from day one of the 2017 government. “Boy from the Hutt” is the brand. Diet Coke & sausage rolls are the props. The biography is Wellington institutional all the way down.

The personal file is the same pattern as the political: proximity to power, then a public reset when the arrangement stops being useful. Married Jade at Premier House in 2020 with Grant Robertson as best man—the court wedding. Separated 2022. By the 2023 concession speech he was thanking “Toni with an i,” a former staffer, now fiancée. He is praised for not using his children as props. Fine. That is the social offence. New Zealanders can tolerate a posh National CEO. They have more trouble with a professional politician who sells himself as the pie-warm everyman while his entire adult life has been caucus, ministry, & the next portfolio.

The nickname stuck because it is schoolboyish.

The contempt stuck because the schoolboy grew up inside the state in Wokeington & never developed an interest outside it.

COVID: the operational face of the kindness tyranny

Ardern supplied the kindness sermon. Hipkins supplied the timetable. Interim Health Minister after David Clark’s lockdown tourism, then Minister for COVID-19 Response from November 2020–June 2022. Masks on transport, pre-departure tests, border rules, Auckland’s long winter, the daily 1pm understudy who became the face of “the team of five million.” He still says the first eighteen months were “nailed.” The exit, he now admits, was not. The specific stains are operational, which is why they attach to him rather than to the poster. The Northland lockdown after two women crossed the Auckland boundary: Hipkins fronted the line that they had used “false information.” OIA material later showed a clerical error, & the gang/sex-worker colouring that had circulated was garbage. He treated the correction as a footnote. Charlotte Bellis, pregnant in Afghanistan, had to threaten legal action before the record was fixed.

That is not a tragic miscommunication. It is a minister who reached for a villain when the system had stuffed up.

Then the afterlife. He & Ardern declined to appear at the later public hearings of the COVID Royal Commission, citing precedent & the risk of abuse, while offering written evidence & a private interview.

For a man who spent two years telling the country to trust the podium, cowardly refusing the public dock is the tell. The project required obedience in real time & privacy in retrospect.

text:
The safety of the Bab el-Mandeb is not a geopolitical favor to be granted, a charity case for the international community, or a burden to be outsourced to distant navies. It is a fundamental, non-negotiable sovereign duty of the bordering littoral states anchored in international law, dictated by geographic reality, and demanded by operational necessity.
The primary responsibility for securing this vital maritime corridor rests exclusively with the nations that share its shores. Foreign naval fleets, regardless of their advanced technology or overwhelming firepower, are transient visitors in these waters. They lack permanent jurisdictional authority, possess no deep-rooted regional intelligence networks, and bear no enduring accountability to the local populations whose security and daily livelihoods are inextricably tied to the strait's safety. Similarly, non-coastal states however invested they may be in global trade have zero sovereign standing to assume this duty.
Critically, the solution cannot be unilateral action by a single coastal state. The Bab el-Mandeb is a shared waterway, bordered by nations with interconnected yet distinct security challenges. Fragmented, uncoordinated efforts will inevitably create blind spots that hostile actors will exploit. This is precisely why strong, institutionalized collaboration among the coastal governments is the absolute prerequisite for lasting security.
Foreign powers should offer technical training, intelligence sharing, and logistical backing only upon explicit request and under the strategic direction of the littoral states. The ultimate objective is to foster a self-reliant, locally driven maritime security architecture that operates effectively with or without international escorts. The safety of the Bab el-Mandeb must be secured by its rightful guardians, for their own sovereignty and for the stability of global commerce alike.

text:
SPECIES-SPECIFIC 'COCKTAILS' DEPEND ON HABITAT AND DIET

Although the fish share the same Mediterranean waters, the contamination profile varies significantly depending on the species' habitat and feeding habits :

Mackerel: This fish feeds both at the surface and on the seabed, which explains the broad spectrum of contaminants found, including plasticizers, industrial compounds, and pesticides .

Red Mullet: As a bottom-dweller that sifts through sediment, red mullet is more exposed to coastal pollution, showing higher concentrations of plasticizers and pharmaceuticals .

Hake: As the top predator in the study, hake registered a lower volume of contaminants but a higher presence of persistent industrial substances, which are difficult to degrade .

NO IMMEDIATE HEALTH RISK, BUT A CALL FOR BETTER MONITORING

The UCO has emphasized that detecting contaminants in fish does not automatically mean their consumption poses a health risk . However, the findings highlight a critical gap in food safety knowledge. As the researchers noted, limiting controls to known contaminants offers an incomplete picture of what fish actually accumulate, especially when the transformation products—the metabolites—are not being monitored .

The study underscores the need to advance scientific understanding of these substances to obtain a more realistic picture of marine pollution and the potential risks of human exposure through seafood consumption .

text:
The Mimic Octopus (Thaumoctopus mimicus) wasn’t officially described until 1998. It was first documented in the coastal waters of Sulawesi, Indonesia, in areas better known for sand and silt than flashy coral reefs.
It’s not a particularly large animal. Most of its 60-centimetre length is made up of long, narrow arms that ripple across the sand. Its natural colours are muted, usually pale brown to blend in with the seabed. 

What sets this species apart, though, is what it does with its body. Unlike most octopuses that stick to background-blending camouflage, the mimic octopus takes on the actual forms and movements of other marine species.

The Mimic Octopus impersonates other animals to improve its chances of survival. Most of the time, it uses mimicry to scare off predators. In some cases, it may also use it to sneak closer to prey. This kind of mimicry works well in the mimic’s natural habitat. Sandy bottoms and silty slopes don’t offer much cover. So instead of hiding, the octopus pretends to be something dangerous.

It spreads its arms wide and moves slowly to resemble the spiny, venomous lionfish. The effect is enough to keep most predators at a distance.

It hides six arms in a hole and stretches two others in opposite directions, waving them to mimic a banded sea snake. This species is known for being venomous, so predators usually avoid it.

 It flattens its body and glides along the seabed, arms trailing behind. The movement and shape closely resemble a harmless flatfish, helping it blend in while moving.

Rather than solely for defense, the mimic octopus employs mimicry both defensively and aggressively, deterring predators and sometimes deceiving prey by adopting forms and movements that encourage close approach. The mimic octopus often chooses which animal to copy based on the threat it faces. It’s a smart way to stay one step ahead in a wide-open ocean.

If you want to see a Mimic Octopus in the wild, the Lembeh Strait should be your go-to spot. Located in North Sulawesi, Lembeh Strait sits in the very region where the species was first documented. It’s now considered the best spot in the world for reliable sightings while going on a muck dive. The dark volcanic seabed here is perfect for mimicry. For photographers and critter fans, nowhere else comes close.

When identifying a Mimic Octopus, focus on posture and movement. If the animal appears to be deliberately acting like something else rather than simply hiding, you are likely witnessing one of the ocean’s most remarkable survival strategies.

text:
I believe faith, repentance, and baptism place us on the strait and narrow path, with baptism being the gate. We are then given the gift of the Holy Ghost, whose sanctifying power purifies and transforms us. 

Think about that exchange: we offer ourselves as devoted disciples of Jesus Christ, and God offers us the gift of a member of the Godhead as our constant companion.

The other saving ordinances—including the temple endowment and sealing—do not purchase salvation or add merit to Christ’s Atonement. They deepen our covenant relationship with God. Through them, we make sacred commitments to Him, receive His promises, and learn to live a life increasingly patterned after Christ.

That is really what the covenant path is about: becoming, through Christ, what God desires us to become.

After all, what would heaven be if liars continued lying, thieves continued stealing, the hateful continued hating, and everyone simply carried their fallen character into eternity? God is not merely relocating us to a nicer place. He is transforming us into people who can live in His presence.

So over time, through Christ, we develop godly attributes: charity, humility, forgiveness, patience, long-suffering, holiness, and love. These are qualities Christ Himself perfectly embodies. If these are qualities you aspire to, congratulations- you're becoming like God too! 

And we certainly do not accomplish this flawlessly.

We stumble. We repent. We learn. We change. We rely upon Christ's grace again and again.

His grace does not merely forgive us when we fall short. His grace enables us to become something we could never become on our own.

In that sense, we fail our way toward a higher plane—not because failure saves us, but because every time we fall, Christ invites us to get back up, repent, follow Him, and continue being transformed by His grace.

The ordinances don’t replace Jesus. The covenants don’t compete with Jesus. The commandments don’t purchase what Jesus did.

They are all part of coming unto Christ and allowing Him to make us more like Him.

That is why I don’t see grace and obedience as competitors. Obedience is not an alternative to grace. It is part of what a life transformed by grace looks like.

If one person made a solemn promise to you to be faithful, loyal, and committed to your relationship, while another person refused to make any such commitment, which relationship would naturally become deeper?

That is what baptismal and temple covenants do. They don't purchase God's love or earn His grace. They establish a committed relationship with Him. We bind ourselves to God through promises, and God binds Himself to us through His promises.

The covenant doesn't earn the relationship. It defines and deepens it.

Isn’t it interesting that Scripture portrays Christ as the Bridegroom and His people as the bride?

Marriage is fundamentally a covenant relationship.

Perhaps Scripture uses marriage imagery precisely because salvation is more than receiving a gift and walking away. Christ is inviting us into a covenant relationship with Him.

text:
Comparative Eschatology

Many of the world’s major religions share a hope that history (or a cosmic cycle) is moving toward a future era of peace, justice, righteousness, and human flourishing. This “golden age” idea appears in linear traditions that expect a once-and-for-all climax and in cyclical traditions that expect a return of an earlier, better age. The details differ sharply: some expect a divine warrior or messiah who violently ends evil; others expect a teacher or a period of gradual moral improvement; some see a temporary earthly kingdom followed by judgment and a new creation; others see an endless perfected world or the start of another cycle.

Here is a comparison of the most developed versions.

Zoroastrianism: Frashokereti — the world made wonderful
Zoroastrianism offers one of the earliest fully developed linear eschatologies. History lasts 12,000 years. At the end the savior figure Saoshyant (the “Benefactor,” born of Zoroaster’s preserved seed) appears. The dead are resurrected in their bodies. All humanity walks through a river of molten metal that feels like warm milk to the righteous and purifies the wicked. Evil (Ahriman) is annihilated forever. Creation is renovated—*frashokereti*, “making wonderful”—becoming ageless, deathless, and perfect. Mountains are leveled, a single language and nation emerge, and time itself ends. The emphasis is restoration of the original good creation rather than its destruction.

Judaism: the Messianic Age and Olam Ha-Ba
Jewish tradition looks forward to the *Yemot ha-Mashiach* (Days of the Messiah), a future era of universal peace, the ingathering of the Jewish exiles, rebuilding of the Temple in Jerusalem, and the nations recognizing the God of Israel. Swords are beaten into plowshares; knowledge of God fills the earth. The Messiah is a human descendant of David, a wise and just king, not a divine being. After (or overlapping with) this age comes *Olam Ha-Ba*, the World to Come. Interpretations vary: some rabbis see it as a perfected physical world after resurrection; Maimonides treated the messianic era as still this-worldly (the only difference being the end of foreign domination) and reserved the ultimate reward for a purely spiritual afterlife.

Christianity: the Millennium and the New Heaven and New Earth
Christian views diverge on the “thousand years” of Revelation 20.

- Premillennialism (common among evangelicals and some early Church fathers): Christ returns first, binds Satan, and reigns physically on earth for 1,000 years with resurrected saints. This is an earthly golden age of peace and justice, after which Satan is released, a final rebellion occurs, and then come the Last Judgment and the New Heaven and New Earth.
- Amillennialism (Catholic, Orthodox, and many Protestant churches): the “millennium” is the present Church age; Christ’s reign is spiritual. The golden age proper is the eternal New Heaven and New Earth after his return and judgment.
- Postmillennialism: the Church gradually Christianizes the world, producing a long golden age; Christ returns afterward.

The final state (Revelation 21–22) is a renewed creation in which God dwells with humanity, death and tears are gone, and the New Jerusalem descends.

Islam: the Mahdi, Jesus, and a brief era of justice
Most Sunni and Shia traditions expect the Mahdi (“the Guided One”), a descendant of Muhammad, to appear when the world is filled with injustice. He will restore justice and rule for 7–9 years (some accounts say longer). Jesus (Isa) then descends, prays behind the Mahdi, kills the Dajjal (false messiah), and helps defeat Gog and Magog. A period of extraordinary peace, abundance, and Islamic rule follows—sometimes described as a golden age lasting 7 to 40 years. After it ends, faith declines and the Day of Resurrection and Judgment arrives. The golden age is therefore a temporary earthly interlude before the final accounting, not the eternal state.

Hinduism: Kalki and the return of Satya Yuga
Time is cyclical. We are in Kali Yuga, the darkest of four ages, which began in 3102 BCE and lasts 432,000 years. At its end Vishnu’s tenth avatar, Kalki, appears on a white horse with a blazing sword, destroys the wicked, and re-establishes *dharma*. A new Satya Yuga (Krita Yuga, the Golden Age of Truth) then begins: virtue is complete, people live long lives in harmony, and righteousness stands on all four “legs.” The cycle of four yugas then repeats. The golden age is therefore recurrent, not final; even after it, decline will eventually set in again.

Buddhism: the coming of Maitreya
Shakyamuni Buddha predicted that his teaching would decline and then that conditions would improve. When human lifespan has risen to 80,000 years and the world is prosperous and peaceful, Maitreya (the “Friendly One”), currently waiting in Tusita heaven, will be born, attain enlightenment under a naga tree, and hold three great assemblies that liberate countless beings. The period is one of flourishing Dharma rather than a permanent end of history; it occurs within the current eon that will still see many more Buddhas. Traditional timelines place it billions of years in the future.

Bahá’í Faith: the Golden Age of a united humanity
Bahá’ís see the present as the Formative Age of Bahá’u’lláh’s revelation. It will culminate in a Golden Age of world unity, a planetary civilization, the “Most Great Peace,” and the fulfillment of the messianic hopes of earlier religions. The emphasis is less on a single warrior-savior and more on the gradual unfolding of new social and spiritual principles already revealed. Humanity itself, guided by the new teachings, builds the golden age.

Other traditions
Sikhism mentions yugas and contains retellings of Kalki and Mahdi stories, but its core teaching focuses on righteous living in the present and union with Waheguru rather than a future earthly utopia. Daoist and Chinese millenarian movements have historically expected “Great Peace” after cataclysms, often with a messianic Laozi figure (Li Hong), but these ideas belong more to specific sects than to a shared orthodox doctrine.

Shared patterns and key differences
Almost every tradition pairs a time of moral and social collapse with the appearance of a restorer (Kalki, Maitreya, Messiah, Mahdi + Jesus, Saoshyant). Common features of the golden age itself include:
- universal peace and justice,
- prosperity and harmony with nature,
- widespread spiritual knowledge or virtue,
- often longer human lives.

The biggest contrasts are:
- Time: linear and once-for-all (Abrahamic + Zoroastrian) versus cyclical return (Hindu, and to a lesser extent Buddhist and Chinese).
- Duration: a short earthly interval (Islam), a thousand years (some Christians), an entire yuga lasting 1.7 million years (Hinduism), or an eternal renovated world (Zoroastrianism, Christian New Creation).
- Means: violent purification by a divine warrior versus teaching and gradual moral transformation.
- What follows: final judgment and a new creation, the start of another cycle, or the end of time itself.

These visions have inspired both quiet hope and, at times, militant movements that tried to force the golden age into existence. In most mainstream forms today they function more as a moral horizon—an image of what a just and flourishing human world could look like—than as a detailed timetable.

text:
From BORDER to  BALLOT BOX

BY DARRELL PITTS

The election-integrity problem does not begin at a polling place. 
It begins years earlier, when governments that were never designed to talk to one another began sharing the same person from one official file to the next.

On May 20, 1993, President Bill Clinton signed the National Voter Registration Act. When Motor Voter took effect in 1995, a driver’s-license transaction became a gateway into voter registration. 

A license proves identity and the right to drive. It does not prove citizenship. 

That distinction hardened after 2013, when California Gov. Jerry Brown signed AB 60, allowing qualifying undocumented residents to obtain licenses beginning January 1, 2015. 

New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo signed the Green Light Law in June 2019. 

New Jersey Gov. Phil Murphy followed in December. 

A real government card can now belong to someone who is not a citizen.

Oregon enacted modern automatic voter registration in 2015; 
California legislated it the same year. 
Eligible customers were no longer asked whether they wanted to register. 
The process ran unless they opted out. 

Computers do not know citizenship. They know what a field says. If the field is blank, wrong, outdated, or answered falsely, automation simply moves the error faster.

Pennsylvania Gov. Tom Wolf signed Act 77 on October 31, 2019, creating no-excuse mail voting. Once a name is on the roll, a ballot can leave a county office without the voter ever appearing at a precinct. 

In 2020, Pennsylvania Democrats returned about 1.7 million mail ballots against roughly 623,000 Republican returns. Mail voting is not proof of fraud. It is proof that an upstream eligibility mistake can become a counted paper without anyone looking the voter in the eye

From 2021 through 2024 the Biden administration expanded parole, 
asylum processing, 
CBP One, 
and CHNV. 
After the Afghanistan withdrawal, 
Operation Allies Welcome brought more than 76,000 Afghan parolees into the United States. 

That Afghan program was only one channel. 

Estimates of all Biden-era parole grants—border releases, 
CBP One port appointments, 
CHNV, 
Uniting for Ukraine, 
and the Afghan evacuees—run about 2.5 million people. 

Parole did not make them citizens or lawful permanent residents. 

It gave temporary permission to enter and remain. 

For those who then received work authorization, that status could produce a genuine Social Security number, an American address, and, where blue state law allowed, a driver’s license

—the documents that later meet Motor Voter at the DMV.

Parole is not citizenship. 
Neither is an Employment Authorization Document. Neither is a Social Security number issued through Enumeration Beyond Entry after USCIS approves work authorization. 

A job produces a paycheck. A lease produces an address. An address and qualifying status can produce a state ID. By the time that file reaches a DMV, almost every ordinary document looks American. 

Only one question still matters: citizen or not.

On September 19, 2023, Gov. Josh Shapiro flipped PennDOT from opt-in to automatic opt-out for eligible customers. 
“I authorized automatic voter registration,” he said. 

Within about two months he reported nearly 58,000 new or updated DMV registrations, a 70 percent jump over the comparable period two years earlier. 

Throughput rose at the exact junction where Pennsylvania must separate citizens from noncitizens.

Pennsylvania sped up the flow of people through the one office step that has to decide: this person is a citizen who may be offered voter registration, or this person is not.

Throughput is volume and speed—how many DMV customers get pushed into the voter-registration process in a given period. 

After Gov. Shapiro switched PennDOT from opt-in to automatic opt-out on September 19, 2023, far more license/ID transactions were run through that registration path. 

He later cited nearly 58,000 new or updated DMV registrations in about two months, a large jump from the same stretch two years earlier.

The junction is that PennDOT moment. 
A license center already handles citizens and qualifying noncitizens. 

Motor Voter / automatic registration is where those records can become voter applications. 

So the system has to keep the two groups apart there: citizen continues toward registration; 
noncitizen is supposed to be blocked.

The sentence is saying the state increased traffic through that checkpoint. 

More files moving faster makes the citizenship field more important, because a blank or wrong field at that exact handoff is how an ineligible person can be offered a registration application.

On April 17, 2026, Auditor General Timothy DeFoor released his review of Motor Voter activity from January through June 2024. 

More than 200,000 unique applications moved through PennDOT. 

Auditors pulled 58 for closer look and found one noncitizen who had been allowed to apply because a clerk left the noncitizen field blank. 

The person did not register and did not vote. 

DeFoor still called the error unacceptable. 

The audit did not inspect every record. 

It did not have to. 

It showed that a single omitted field can defeat an automated firewall.

That is the architecture, not a theory about every new arrival. 

A noncitizen can lawfully collect immigration papers, a work permit, an SSN, a paycheck, a lease, and a license. 

Federal law still forbids that person from voting in a federal election. 

The illegal act happens only if citizenship screening fails, a later review fails, a county accepts the registration, and a ballot is cast. 

Downstream systems can then perform perfectly. 
The county sees a registered voter. 
The mail ballot issues. 
The scanner counts paper. 
A risk-limiting audit confirms the machine counted what it was given. 

None of those steps answers the first question.

On August 31, 2026, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy shut down 110 commercial-driver schools tied to more than 5,000 English-proficiency failures and sent investigators into hundreds more training sites. 

States had issued genuine licenses on the strength of certifications that later collapsed. 

A real government card does not prove that every fact underneath it was true. 

Apply that lesson to citizenship and the point is obvious.

President Trump’s 2026 postal order tries to put unique Intelligent Mail barcodes on ballot envelopes so a ballot can be followed from issuance through the mail and back. 

That is useful against lost, duplicate, or untraceable envelopes. 

It cannot repair a roll that already contains the wrong person. 

A flawless barcode can track an ineligible ballot with perfect fidelity. 
Mail security is not citizenship security.

The SAVE Act attacks the earlier lock. 
It would amend Clinton’s 1993 law so federal registration requires documentary proof of citizenship—passport, 
naturalization papers, 
or specified combinations that actually speak to nationality rather than driving privilege. 

A license is not enough. 
An SSN is not enough. 
Twenty years of residency is not enough. 
The question becomes whether the applicant is an American before a record exists.

Compassion for lawful immigrants does not require treating citizenship as a data field that can be left blank. 

Banks reconcile accounts because people err and some people lie. 

Elections deserve the same discipline: prove citizenship before registration, reconcile the roll against authoritative status, track the envelope, audit the count. 

Miss the first lock and the other three can work exactly as designed while processing a vote that never should have been issued.

The border is where the person entered. 

The ballot box is where the question is finally settled, and by then it can already be too late.

text:
If you’re a builder your hvac contractor will charge you $5500 for a 3 ton brand new HVAC system including ducts….I really like this price honestly. 

If you’re a homeowner and your existing HVAC system fails and needs a replacement system the home owner will get charged around $16,500. 
Adding complete new duct work  in Arizona commonly adds $5,000-$10,500 more depending on home size and attic access so a true new system plus ducts frequently ends up in the $15,000-$22,000

There are contractors who offer payments plans 
0% if paid in full 12-18 months 

Fixed rate installment loans, yes there are loans for new hvac installations…
9.99% for 84 months 
12.99% for 120 months 
Credit dependent ranges 8%-20%

Assuming we have a principal of $18,000 with a 12.99% for 120 months then the homeowner would have paid a total of $32,240

Your best bet here is to get no 3 bids but 5 separate bids from different contractors that separately line up the system vs ducts.

text:
A woman from New York was driving through a remote part of Arizona when her car broke down. 

An American Indian on horseback came along and offered her a ride to a nearby town.

She climbed up behind him on the horse and they rode off. 

The ride was uneventful, except that every few minutes the Indian would let out a Ye-e-e-e-h-a-a-a-a!' so loud that it echoed from the surrounding hills and canyon walls.

When they arrived in town, he let her off at the local service station, yelled one final "Ye-e-e-e-h-a-a-a-a!' and rode off.

"What did you do to get that Indian so excited?" asked the service-station attendant. 

"Nothing," the woman answered "I merely sat behind him on the horse, put my arms around his waist, and held onto the saddle horn so I wouldn't fall off."

"Lady," the attendant said, "Indians don't use saddles."

text:
In 1988 Dolly Parton pulled every 7th and 8th grader in Sevier County into a room and told them to pick a buddy.
 
She made them sign a contract.. if BOTH graduate, she hands you both $500. One fails, nobody gets paid.
The county dropout rate went from 35% to 6%.
She handed out the checks herself.

In 1989 she offered $500 to every kid in the county who wanted to go to the local college. 
When Gatlinburg burned in 2016, she sent 900 families $1,000 a month for six months.
You've probably heard that part.
 
Here's the part you haven't: 
The fund raised more than expected, so she showed up in May and handed every one of those families another $5,000 on top.
 
Then she quietly put $3 million into the recovery group that handles the years after the news trucks leave.
She built her county an entire hospital.
 
She played a benefit concert in 2007, Dollywood and the Stampede matched it, and LeConte Medical Center opened in 2010 with a birthing unit and a women's center in it.
In 2022 she started covering 100% of tuition, books, and fees for Dollywood employees. 
Full-time, part-time, AND seasonal.
 
In 1991 she paid for a bald eagle sanctuary because the birds couldn't be released back into the wild, no press release.

And when Hurricane Helene came through here in Western North Carolina, she wrote a personal check for $1 million and her companies matched it. 

She started the Imagination Library because her daddy couldn't read or write. Before he passed, he told her it was the most important thing she ever did.
Rest in Peace, Dolly! 🙏

🚨 HOUSE VOTES 413–2 TO CENSURE REP. CHUCK EDWARDS

The House voted 413–2 Tuesday to censure Republican Congressman Chuck Edwards of North Carolina over his conduct toward two young female staffers.

Every Democrat and nearly every Republican supported the resolution. The only “no” votes came from Edwards and Republican Rep. Ralph Norman.

Edwards was required to stand in the well of the House while Speaker Mike Johnson publicly read the resolution. Censure is the House’s most severe punishment short of expulsion.

The Ethics Committee interviewed 16 people and reviewed approximately 1,500 pages of evidence.

One staffer was 19 when she first interned for Edwards and had not finished college when he hired her as his congressional scheduler. The second was in her early 20s. Both had worked for him in the North Carolina Senate before following him to Congress.

Edwards is 65.

According to the committee, Edwards provided the women with unusual personal attention and gifts, including:

• More than $1,000 in jewelry
• Designer purses, shoes and flowers
• A laptop and cellphone
• A KitchenAid mixer and robotic vacuum
• Vacations, hotel rooms and performance tickets
• Massages and spa treatments
• One-on-one dinners
• Two personalized handguns—one pink and one blue, engraved with their names

He also commented on their clothing, appearance and weight, calling them “pretty” and “breathtaking.” He sent one staffer approximately 30 kinds of ice cream after she declined a dinner invitation.

Edwards wrote poems for one woman and read one aloud at her going-away party while standing beside a slideshow of the two of them—and crying. Several employees testified that it made them uncomfortable.

Edwards paid for a New York trip that included a helicopter ride, dinner and Hamilton tickets. He took a staffer to casinos, bought her drinks and paid for her gambling. He performed yardwork at her home and skipped House votes to help decorate her Christmas tree.

One of the women was later promoted to deputy chief of staff. Several employees considered the promotion preferential and said Edwards’ treatment of the women damaged office morale. Edwards defended the promotion, calling her brilliant and the strongest candidate.

In November 2025, Edwards paid for flights, two Bellagio rooms and tickets to the Sphere for himself and a former staffer in Las Vegas. Flowers were waiting in her room.

She texted that the accompanying message made her uncomfortable and asked whether the trip was intended to be “anything it’s not.”

She later told investigators she had repeatedly declined the trip but eventually felt pressured because Edwards still had influence over her public-service career.

Edwards admitted he concealed his companion’s identity from his scheduler because it “would have looked suspicious.”

The committee found no evidence of sexual contact, an explicit proposition or an offer of employment benefits in exchange for sex.

That became Edwards’ defense.

In a 22-page letter, he argued the committee combined innocent acts and interpreted them “through the darkest possible lens.”

“A gift is not sexual misconduct,” he wrote. “A compliment is not sexual misconduct. Poetry is not sexual misconduct.”

Edwards described the relationships as platonic or father-daughter friendships. Before the vote, he apologized for making the women uncomfortable but maintained:

“Regret is not an admission of sexual harassment.”

The committee considered the overall pattern: the women’s ages, Edwards’ authority over their careers, the gifts, travel, preferential treatment and their ability to reject his attention without consequences.

It concluded that Edwards engaged in “persistent unprofessional and inappropriate conduct” that a reasonable person could interpret as romantic or sexual.

Both women eventually left his office. Edwards abandoned his reelection campaign two days after the report became public.

Potential use cases include:

The group is targeting a market launch in the first half of 2027 and intends to operate under frameworks including the U.S. GENIUS Act and EU MiCA where applicable.

Standard Bank is part of the 21-member group.
This is another sign that the stablecoin race is no longer simply crypto companies versus banks.
The banks themselves are now building stablecoins.

Digital assets received an important acknowledgement following the latest meeting of G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors in Asheville, North Carolina.

The official Chair’s Statement released on September 1 recognizes that digital financial innovation, including digital assets, can play a transformative role in supporting economic growth.

The statement also highlights the private sector as an important driver of that innovation.

At the same time, regulators emphasized the need to protect:
• Financial stability
• Trust in payment systems
• Monetary systems
• Cross-border financial integrity

The statement commits to advancing regulatory and supervisory frameworks that establish “clear pathways” for sound digital-finance and digital-asset innovation.
Stablecoins are also on the agenda, with the G20 awaiting further Financial Stability Board work concerning cross-border global stablecoin arrangements.
Important context:

This is a G20 Chair’s Statement, so it should not be interpreted as every G20 member endorsing identical crypto regulation.

Still, digital assets being framed around innovation and economic growth alongside regulation is significant.

Official U.S. Treasury statement:
https://t.co/0L9Rjgtau7

3. U.S. SEC MOVES TO MODERNIZE TRANSFER-AGENT RULES FOR THE BLOCKCHAIN ERA
Tokenized securities are forcing regulators to rethink infrastructure designed decades before blockchain existed.

The @SECGov has proposed a major modernization of the rules governing registered transfer agents.
Transfer agents play a critical role in securities markets by maintaining ownership records and processing changes in ownership.

The September 1 proposal explicitly considers the modern use of:
• Electronic communications
• Electronic recordkeeping
• Distributed ledgers
• Blockchain-based securities
• Tokenized share transfers

SEC Chairman Paul Atkins said the modernization would reflect current market operations, including the use of blockchain technology in securities offerings and transfers of shares.

This matters because tokenizing a stock is only part of the challenge. The legal ownership records, transfer-agent infrastructure, settlement systems and investor protections around that token also need to function in an onchain environment.
Public comments will remain open for 60 days after publication in the Federal Register.

Official SEC announcement:
https://t.co/slXn5PRMVO

6. RUSSIA’S NEW CRYPTO MARKET REGIME TAKES EFFECT
Russia’s new framework governing cryptocurrency transactions officially came into effect on September 1, 2026.
Under the framework announced by the Bank of Russia, both qualified and non-qualified investors can access cryptocurrencies through regulated intermediaries.

For non-qualified investors:
• A knowledge test is required
• Access is limited to selected highly liquid cryptocurrencies
• Purchases are capped at ₽300,000 per year through one intermediary

Qualified investors must also pass a test but can access a broader range of cryptocurrencies without the same monetary limit.

Russia is also creating regulated infrastructure around the market, including:
• Crypto exchanges
• Digital repositories
• Existing financial institutions acting as intermediaries

Digital repositories will maintain records of rights to crypto assets, while approved exchanges will facilitate transactions.

Whatever one's view of Russia’s broader crypto policy, this represents another major economy moving away from the simple “ban or ignore crypto” approach toward regulated market infrastructure.

An AI agent that can identify the information it needs, pay for that information using USDC, analyze it and produce a structured research report.

This is where agentic commerce gets interesting.
Instead of AI only consuming free internet information, agents can become actual economic actors capable of:

Weird how you never hear about any of this in the news...... TRUMP DOES THE UNTHINKABLE...
I've never heard anything negative about the man until he announced he was running for president.

• He's never even tried alcohol or tobacco. He doesn't do drugs. 

• His work ethic is beyond unparalleled as a hardworking businessman. 

• He's one of the most generous celebrities in the world with a heart filled with more gold than his $100 million New York penthouse.

Since the media has failed so miserably at reporting the truth about Trump, I decided to put together some of the acts of kindness he's committed over three decades which has gone virtually unnoticed or fallen on deaf ears. 

• In 1986, Trump prevented the foreclosure of Annabell Hill's family farm after her husband committed suicide. Trump personally phoned down to the auction to stop the sale of her home and offered the widow money. Trump decided to take action after he saw Hill's pleas for help in news reports. 

• In 1988, a commercial airline refused to fly Andrew Ten, a sick Orthodox Jewish child with a rare illness. The boy had to travel with an elaborate life-support system. Trump contacted the grief-stricken parents after hearing this and didn't hesitate to send his own plane to take the child from Los Angeles to New York so he could get his treatment. 

• In 1991, 200 Marines who served in Operation Desert Storm spent time at Camp Lejune in North Carolina before they were scheduled to return home to their families. However, the Marines were told that a mistake had been made and an aircraft would not be able to take them home on their scheduled departure date. When Trump got wind of this, he sent his plane to make two trips from North Carolina to Miami to safely return the Gulf War Marines to their loved ones. 

• In 1995, a motorist stopped to help Trump after the limo he was traveling in got a flat tire. Trump asked the Good Samaritan how he could repay him for his help. All the man asked for was a bouquet of flowers for his wife. A few weeks later Trump sent the flowers with a note that read: We've paid off your mortgage. 

• In 1996, Trump filed a lawsuit against the city of Palm Beach , Florida, accusing the town of discriminating against his Mar-a-Lago resort club because it allowed Jews and blacks. Abraham Foxman, who as the Anti-Defamation League Director at the time, said Trump put the light on Palm Beach not on the beauty and the glitter, but on its seamier side of discrimination. Foxman also noted that Trump's charge had a trickle-down effect because other clubs followed his lead and began admitting Jews and blacks. 

• In 2000, Maury Povich featured a little girl named Megan who struggled with Brittle Bone Disease on his show and Trump happened to be watching. Trump said the little girl's story and positive attitude touched his heart. So he contacted Maury and gifted the little girl and her family with a very generous check. 

• In 2008, after Jennifer Hudson's family members were tragically murdered in Chicago , Trump put the Oscar-winning actress and her family up at his Windy City hotel for free. In addition to that, Trump's security took extra measures to ensure Hudson and her family members were safe during such a difficult time. 

• In 2013, New York bus driver Darnell Barton spotted a woman close to the edge of a bridge staring at the traffic below as he drove by. He stopped the bus, got out and put his arm around the woman and saved her life by convincing her to not jump. When Trump heard about this story, he sent the hero bus driver a check simply because he believed his good deed deserved to be rewarded.

Pollinating California's almonds takes almost every commercial honeybee in the United States, and in the winter of 2025 the beekeepers lost 62 per cent of them on the way.

Step one. Clear the ground. California grows around 80 per cent of the world's almonds across 1.4 million acres, most of it planted within a generation over rangeland and mixed farmland. The orchard floor is sprayed to bare dirt. Nothing flowers there and nothing nests there, and for eleven months of the year it is one of the quietest places in American agriculture.

Step two. Find the water. An almond takes roughly 1.1 gallons, and the tree drinks every year of its 25 year life whether there is a drought on or not. Almonds account for close to a tenth of all agricultural water use in the state. When the surface allocation is cut, growers drill, and the valley floor has been sinking for decades.

Step three. Import pollinators, because you removed the ones that lived there. Almonds cannot pollinate themselves. An acre needs two colonies, so the bloom needs 2.8 million of them, which is virtually every managed hive in the country. There is no second option and no reserve.

Step four. Load them onto lorries in Florida, Texas and the Dakotas and drive them across a continent. It is the largest movement of livestock on earth and it exists to fertilise a nut. Stack them at densities no bee evolved for, so that every mite, virus and spore in American beekeeping is introduced to every other one, annually, on schedule.

Step five. Spray them while they work. Fungicides go on during bloom because the crop is worth too much to risk. The label says it is safe for bees. The beekeepers have been saying otherwise for twenty years.

Step six. Feed them syrup. A monoculture flowers for three weeks and then offers a colony nothing at all, so the industry keeps its livestock alive on sugar and protein patties for the other forty-nine.

Step seven. Count the dead. Beekeepers had come to accept losing 30 per cent a year. Then February 2025 arrived and commercial operators had lost an average of 62 per cent, some of them close to everything. 1.6 million colonies, $600 million, the worst losses ever recorded. Lorries pulled into Fresno with half the boxes already silent.

Step eight. Shake the trees. Mechanical shakers drop the crop onto the dirt and the valley disappears into dust for weeks, in a basin that already has the worst air in the United States.

Step nine. Feed the hulls to cattle. The waste goes into dairy rations, so the almond industry is quietly propped up by the animal almond milk was invented to replace.

Step ten. Blend two per cent of it with water, add a gum from Rajasthan, chalk for the calcium and a synthetic B12, and print a leaf on the carton.

The cow eats grass and pollinates nothing, because she does not need to. She is the ethical problem. The system that required every bee in America and killed two thirds of them getting there is the solution.

text:
New Georgia State clinic to help families retain property, fight heirs’ loss

A new law clinic at Georgia State University will offer free legal services to help families counter heirs’ property issues, which experts say are a leading cause of involuntary property loss and a barrier to the creation of generational wealth. The problem arises when the owner of a property does not appear on the title, which most commonly happens when someone inherits property from a relative who has passed away without leaving a will. Such property is often split between many different family members, but without clear documentation tying them to a property, families often have a difficult time holding onto their land or accessing services like disaster relief funds that require them to prove ownership of their house.

text:
If you’re an American looking for a destination that feels genuinely different from the usual international travel circuit, Rabaul in East New Britain should be on your list for one simple reason: nowhere else gives you such a powerful combination of World War II history, active volcanic landscapes, island culture, and raw Pacific scenery in one compact place.

Rabaul is not just another tropical destination. It is a place where history is still physically embedded in the land and ocean.

During World War II, Rabaul became one of Japan’s most important military bases in the South Pacific. Thousands of troops were stationed there, tunnels were carved into hillsides, aircraft operated from nearby airfields, and the surrounding waters became part of a much larger battle for control of the Pacific. For Americans, that history is not distant. It is connected directly to the sacrifices made by U.S. servicemen across the Pacific campaign.

Today, you can stand in places where that history happened.

You can explore old Japanese tunnels, coastal defenses, war relics and sites that once formed part of an enormous military network. Then, within the same journey, you can look across Simpson Harbour toward volcanic peaks that completely changed the city’s story decades later.

That is what makes Rabaul unique.

This is not a museum where history sits behind glass. The entire landscape tells the story.

Mount Tavurvur remains one of the most recognizable features of the area. The 1994 volcanic eruptions devastated large parts of old Rabaul, covering sections of the town in ash and forcing many businesses and residents to relocate toward Kokopo. Yet Rabaul survived.

That creates a travel experience with layers.

You are not only visiting a beautiful Pacific island. You are walking through a place shaped by war, rebuilt after destruction, surrounded by volcanoes, coral seas, traditional communities and some of the most dramatic scenery in Papua New Guinea.

For American travelers who enjoy history, military heritage, photography, adventure, diving or destinations with a real story behind them, Rabaul offers something completely different from Hawaii, Fiji or the Caribbean.

And that is exactly the point.

Papua New Guinea is not competing by being more familiar.

Its strength is that it still feels undiscovered.

A trip to Rabaul can include visits to war sites, volcanic viewpoints, local markets, cultural performances, island excursions, snorkeling, diving, dolphin watching, seafood, village experiences and time along the coast around Kokopo and the Gazelle Peninsula.

But the strongest reason to come is the feeling of standing somewhere that connects America’s Pacific history with one of the most extraordinary landscapes on Earth.

If you ever visit Papua New Guinea, do not just pass through Port Moresby.

Put Rabaul on the itinerary.

You may arrive because of the history.

You will probably leave remembering the people, the volcanoes, the ocean and the feeling that you discovered somewhere most Americans still know almost nothing about.

Register your interest here: https://t.co/uA0lzRPJAq

For travelers tired of predictable destinations, that rarity alone makes Rabaul worth crossing the Pacific to experience at least once personally.

We currently have TWO Category 4 hurricanes spinning across the Pacific at the same time — Karina and Lowell — and now Tropical Storm Marie is strengthening behind them.

Three tropical systems lined up across the Pacific at the same time.

text:
September 1, 1449. Mongol raiders captured the Emperor of China. Beijing's response was to crown a new emperor and inform them the old one was now worthless.

Two days ago I posted about the beggar who founded the Ming dynasty. This is his great great grandson losing everything in about three weeks.

The Zhengtong Emperor was 21 and completely controlled by a eunuch named Wang Zhen, who ran the court and loved military pageantry and had never fought anything. When the Oirat Mongol leader Esen raided the frontier, the emperor announced he would personally lead a punitive expedition. His Minister of War and the deputy minister, a man named Yu Qian, both told him plainly it was an unacceptable risk.

He went anyway. Roughly half a million men marched out of Beijing on August 4, hastily assembled, badly supplied, and commanded in practice by a palace eunuch.

It rained the whole way. Men starved to death on the road before anyone saw a Mongol. Wang Zhen refused to turn back until he reached Datong, took one look at the actual situation, declared the expedition a triumph, and ordered a retreat.

The retreat is where the army died. The Mongols destroyed the rearguard, then ambushed and annihilated the 40,000 cavalry sent to cover it.

On August 31 the army halted at a post station called Tumu. Six miles away sat Huailai, a walled town with water. Wang Zhen refused to move to it because his personal baggage train had not caught up yet. So the army spent the night on dry high ground with no water.

Esen had about 20,000 men against them. He surrounded the camp and offered to talk. Wang Zhen ordered the army to break formation and march for the river.

They were butchered in the open. Something like half the army died. Two dukes, two marquises, five counts and hundreds of senior officials were killed in a single afternoon. The Mongols captured tens of thousands of firearms. Wang Zhen was reportedly killed by one of his own officers during the collapse, which under the circumstances was probably the most popular event of the day.

And they took the emperor alive.

Esen thought he had just won China. He had the Son of Heaven sitting in a tent and assumed Beijing would pay anything.

Beijing's answer was Yu Qian, the man who had told them not to go. Made Minister of War on September 7. He refused to allow anyone to even discuss moving the capital, threatened to execute anyone who proposed it, stripped 80,000 troops off the frontier and put 220,000 defenders on the walls. Then the court simply crowned the captive emperor's brother, handed the prisoner the honorary title of emperor emeritus, and left Esen holding a hostage worth precisely nothing.

Esen attacked Beijing in October with 70,000 men, lasted five days, and went home. His confederation fell apart. He was murdered in 1455.

The captured emperor was eventually released, spent seven years under house arrest inside his own palace, then staged a coup and took his throne back.

One of the first things he did was have Yu Qian executed.

text:
Aside from my mom’s story my father’s is even more wild. This is a bit longer, but worth it (or maybe not)

My father served in Vietnam (drafted), was part of the Cambodian incursion. His platoon was part of what triggered the Kent state protests where a four students were killed by the national guard - Allison Krause (19), Jeffrey Miller (20), Sandra Lee Scheuer (20), and William Schroeder (19). This weighed heavily on my father. 

My father was autistic, and had an abusive upbringing. He fought in the Battle of Song Mao. Bronze Star recipient. Highest rated marksman in his company for years. I once saw him shoot a nickel and quarter in the direct center from god knows how far, it felt like a mile. He came home with severe PTSD, which they didn’t understand yet. 

A few years later dad marries my mom, has me, I’m born in April which is the same month Song Mao occurred. If you know about PTSD, then months/days/times can trigger flashbacks. After my 3rd bday my mom came home to find my dad trying to drown me in our bathtub while also beating my back black & blue. He was having a flashback and kept calling me “Charlie” (a derogatory name given to the enemy in Nam) Mom grabs me, runs out of the house, but not before my dad shouts “it’s my life’s purpose to kill that boy!” 

Dad sent to looney bin. Mom files for divorce. I go a few years not seeing him, she wasn’t sure it was safe. Finally reconnect. Have decent divorced dad contact, see him one weekend a month, but we always stayed at his mom's house, which always seemed…off. 

Then when I’m 15 he loses it at a car dealership while trying to get a free car with his military ID (that's not a thing). Cops are called, I’m driven home confused. Get home, mom tells me the truth about my dad. Which was scary to hear. I finally realized that she always made sure I had two quarters in my pocket whenever I saw him. It was in case I needed to make an emergency call on a pay phone (google it)…but she never told me that so I always used them to play arcade games. 

Dad disappears. I go 3 years with no contact till my senior year when he shows up barefoot at my high school asking to check me out. Thankfully my mom was smart enough to put him on the no list, and also to tell the school he was dangerous. They won't let him see me, he throws a fit, threatens to shoot up my school. I'm brought into a safe in the principals office and locked in it, while they evacuate the school under the guise of a bomb threat. School clears, police whisk me away. I never told any of my friends this story. I was embarrassed. Two days later we go to the gas station to get lunch, my dad is walking by, disheveled and bare foot, carrying a case of Coors, it's NOON. He looks so out of place my buddy driving goes "look at that fucking loser, probably lives in a box". I turn, see it's my dad, recoil, and just reply "yeah, what a fucking loser" meanwhile I'm fighting back tears, shaking, anxiety like never before.

Next day while I'm at school my dad breaks into our house, steals various pairs of shoes of mine (Air Yewtah's!) and grabs his military uniform for some reason. He leaves me with one pair of shoes, my least favorite. I find this ironic, and kinda hysterical. 

Disappears again for about 8 years. My aunt sees him homeless downtown. Offers to help him. They let him live with my grandma, he assaults her during a flashback, so they find a house for him which coincidentally was 1 mile from where I was living. I see this as a sign to reconnect. Side note; not everything is a sign. 

I visit his house, it's been 10 years. He's awkward. Won't talk. I start crying and leave. I wouldn't see my dad again for many more years.

Fast Forward many years and my father burnt his house down while having a flashback….coincidentally also in April. He narrowly avoids jail time for arson, because the smoke killed parts of his brain. He's given probation so long as he's in counseling and a living home. 

He's put in a retirement community, again, it's now a 1.5 minute drive from my new house. See it as a sign again, ask my aunt if I could visit him. My dad says no. I ask again off and on over the course of years. No. He doesn't want to see me. Then one day out of the blue my aunt calls saying he'll see me. I almost told her to tell him to fuck off. By now I was bitter and pissed, but I figured it was my one shot to tell him how I feel.  I should note that his sisters paid for this home, his side of the family had a bit of money. Money they never showed me in any way. 

Decide to man up and face the only real villain in my life, or so I thought. He's broken, a shell of the man I once knew. Before he was quiet, reserved, now he could barely form sentences, sounded like he had Down syndrome. I couldn't possibly berate, or be angry at him. 

We reconnect as best we can while eating at the Wendy's by his community. I started to enjoy watching him eat his chicken nuggets. He'd lay a napkin out on the table, then methodically arrange the nuggets in a row, and take one bite of each, move down the row, then take a 2nd bit. It was like watching a toddler. I had profound empathy for him, when all I ever use to have was hate and vitriol.

I later found out just how abused he was as a child. Something even my mom wasn't aware of. Turns out, his step dad tried to drown him in a bathtub too. It almost worked, and paramedics were called. In that moment I reallized that my dad trying to drown me was an experience he went through, and it wasn't about me at all.

I spent my life wondering if my dad loved me, or cared about me. He never showed, or said either. Then at his funeral my uncle, his brother, approached me with a story that shattered me. He told me that when my dad started getting bad mentally again, he was aware of it, and scared of what he might do. He went to my uncles house and gave him all of his guns. He didn't want to have them around, especially with me. He said his greatest fear was hurting me, and was taking precautions not to. He also said it's why he stayed away from me. Not because he didn't love me, but because HE DID. When my uncle handed me those guns I started crying like I never had before. I was holding the physical manifestation of my father's love. A shotgun, a bolt action rifle, and 9mm. 

My father was the villain in my life until a few years before he died. I was lucky enough to be there when he took his final breath. Something I would have never envisioned wanting to experience let alone being thankful for. 

I don't know if there's a moral here, but it taught me a great deal about making assumptions towards others. I spent decades thinking my father hated me, when in actuality he was doing the only thing in his limited power to keep me safe. 

Sometimes actions aren't what they appear to be. Maybe that's all the moral it needs?

Joe Kent acknowledges the American game in Syria.🛑🔥🚨🎯✅️

When viewed through the lens of Middle Eastern and global political history, this observation captures the essence of the strategy known in international relations as "proxy warfare."

It is nothing new for major powers to utilize local groups, militias, or regional actors on the ground to advance their strategic interests rather than incurring direct military and economic costs; however, the US is one of the actors that has employed this mechanism the longest and most systematically.
The key dimensions of this strategy are as follows:

Cost and Public Pressure: Direct military intervention as seen in the cases of Iraq and Afghanistan triggers significant backlash among the American public and incurs costs running into the trillions of dollars. Operating through "proxy" or subcontracted groups prevents the return of flag-draped coffins to the homeland and lowers operational costs.

Plausible Deniability: Should groups on the ground take specific actions or commit violations, Washington can avoid direct responsibility, thereby retaining flexibility at the negotiating table.

Regional Balancing: Instead of attempting to establish or govern states directly in crisis zones like Syria, Iraq, Yemen, or Libya, the US aims to keep regional actors under pressure by arming and training elements that align with its vision (or serve to counterbalance its rivals).
The Other Side of the Coin: Uncontrollable "Blowback"

However, the greatest weakness of this strategy for the US is that these subcontracted entities do not always remain loyal or may spiral out of control.  The Case of Afghanistan: The subsequent emergence of groups like Al-Qaeda and the Taliban from within the ranks of the Mujahideen, who were supported against the Soviets in the 1980s.
Syria and Iraq: Groups that were initially viewed as tactical allies on the ground or that exploited power vacuums eventually became primary sources of regional instability and terrorism themselves.
In conclusion, while policies pursued through proxy organizations may offer the US military and political flexibility in the short term, they create vast, uncontrollable zones of chaos in the long run a situation that ultimately hits the local populations the hardest.

text:
The White House recently declared that "Communism is the enemy of free people everywhere." This sentence is a masterpiece of ideological inversion. It does not seek to define freedom; it seeks to weaponize it. To analyze this claim, we must move beyond the surface-level rhetoric and apply the cold lens of Political Economy.
 The bourgeoisie speaks of "freedom" in a purely formal sense. They speak of the freedom of speech, the freedom to vote, and the freedom to enter into contracts. But for the proletariat, these are ghosts of freedoms. 
What is the "freedom of contract" for a worker who must accept any wage, however meager, or face starvation? What is the "freedom of speech" for those whose voices are drowned out by the roar of corporate-owned media? This is not freedom; it is the freedom to be exploited. In a society where the means of production are privately owned, the worker is "free" only in the sense that they are stripped of everything—including the means to survive independently—leaving them no choice but to sell their labor power as a commodity.
 We must ask: Who is the "we" that speaks for these "free people"? The White House is not a neutral arbiter of human rights; it is the administrative headquarters of the global capitalist class. 
When the state declares communism to be the enemy of freedom, what it is actually saying is: "The collective appropriation of the means of production is an enemy to our right to accumulate surplus value." The fear they project onto communism is not a fear for the liberty of the masses, but a fear for the stability of private property. They protect the "freedom" of the few to own the world by ensuring the "freedom" of the many to remain precarious.
 In the 21st century, this deception has reached its zenith. The bourgeoisie now offers us a new kind of "freedom": the freedom of the gig economy, the freedom of digital nomadism, and the freedom of consumer choice. 
But look closer. The "flexibility" of the Uber driver is merely the removal of social security; the "choice" between a dozen different streaming services is a distraction from the fact that our very attention has been commodified. We are trapped in a digital panopticon where algorithms dictate our desires and movements. This is the "freedom" the White House defends—a world where you are free to click, but not free to decide how the wealth created by your data is distributed.
 The bourgeoisie claims communism destroys freedom. On the contrary, capitalism destroys humanity and calls it freedom. 
True freedom—substantive freedom—is not the right to choose between two brands of soap or two political puppets. It is the liberation from the tyranny of necessity. It is the end of the division of labor that turns humans into appendages of a machine (or an algorithm). 
Communism is not the "enemy" of free people; it is the only historical project that aims to create the material conditionsunder which freedom becomes possible for all, not just those who hold the deed to the land or the keys to the server.

The claim that communism is the enemy of freedom is a veil thrown over the face of exploitation. The only way to answer this lie is to reclaim the word "freedom" from the halls of power and return it to the streets, the factories, and the digital hubs where value is actually created. 
Until the means of production are held in common, "freedom" will remain a luxury item available only to those who can afford to buy it.

text:
September 2 Saint Stephen, King of Hungary, Confessor: From the Liturgical Year of Dom Prosper Louis Pascal Guéranger, O.S.B., 1903
.
White Semidouble.
.
“Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness. The people with teeth of steel grinding the nations gives itself up as food to him, to whom was said: Kill and eat; the mouth of the Huns, formerly vomiting foam and rage, now distills the honey of charity. Such, O Christ, are thy miracles; such are thy works, O our God!” Thus does Baronius, on reaching in his history the year of Christ 1000, hail the arrival of the Hungarian deputies, who came to offer to the Roman Church the suzerainty of their land, and beseech the Vicar of Christ to confer the title of king upon their Duke Stephen.
.
We are carried back in thought a century earlier, when, led by Arpadus, the son of Almutz, under the banner of the hawk, the Magyars came down from the mountains of Transylvania into the plains watered by the Theiss and the Danube. Attila seemed to live again in these sons of his race, who poured like a torrent over Germany, Gaul and Italy. But the empire of the Huns over reconquered Pannonia was only to be lasting on condition of its ceasing to be the scourge of God, and becoming the rampart of his Church. In this world, while it is not yet time for eternal justice, the instruments of God’s anger are soon broken, unless they are amenable to love. Five centuries earlier, Attila in person was rushing like an overflowing river upon the capital of the world, when he was met by the Sovereign Pontiff. The Hungarian chronicles record the following message as having been then received from heaven by the universal devastator: “Hearken to the command of the Lord God, Jesus Christ. Thy pride shall not be suffered to enter into the holy city where lie the bodies of my Apostles. Return. Later on a descendent of thine will come to Rome with humility; and I will cause him there to receive a crown that shall last forever.” Attila thereupon recrossed the Alps, and had only just time to reach the Danube before he died. In the days of St. Stephen the heavenly promise was fulfilled. Let the reader not be astonished that we do not discuss its authenticity. Legendary or not, as to the forms with which national traditions have clothed it, there is nothing in this divine engagement that the historian need reject: it is in accordance with the rules of God’s Providence, which governs history. God never forgets a service; nor does apostolic gratefulness wear out with years: the debt of gratitude which Leo the Great contracted, Sylvester II paid at the appointed time. From that tomb respected by the plunderer, a virtue came forth, changing the avenger into an apostle. The crown, placed on the brow of Attila’s successor by Peter’s successor, was destined to be his as long as he should be preceded by the Cross, that other mark of honor conferred upon him. Like the Holy Empire, to which Hungary was to be later on united without however being absorbed by it, the Hungarian monarchy was founded upon Peter; for his sake it subsisted, and he alone, under God, was the safeguard of its future.
.
Let not the sad forebodings of the present hour make us forget the marvelous power shown on this feast by the Lamb the Ruler of the earth. Scarcely had the blood shed by the sons of Arpadus disappeared from the streets of the cities; scarcely had the smoke of burning ruins and the dust of crumbling walls been scattered; when their fierce energy, tempered like a choice blade in the waters of the sacred font, became the defense of Christianity in the East. A new sort of invasion began; the holiness sprung from Stephen put forth numerous branches, which, shedding their beautiful blossoms over the whole earth, filled all lands with perfumes for the Spouse.
.
Let us read the history of the apostolic king, as given in the Book of Holy Church.
.
Stephanus in Hungariam Christi fidem et regium nomen invexit. Regia corona a Romano Pontifice impetrata, ejusque jussu in regem inunctus, regnum Sedi apostolicæ obtulit. Varia pietatis domicilia Romæ Jerosolymis, Constantinopoli; in Hungaria archiepiscopatum Strigoniensem, episcopatus decem, admirabili religione et munificentia fundavit. Par in pauperes amor et liberalitas, quos veluti Christum ipsum complectens, neminem a se mærentem ac vacuum umquam dimisit; quin ad eorum inopiam sublevandam amplissimis facultatibus erogatis, domesticam quoque supellectilem eximia benignitate frequenter distribuit: suis insuper manibus lavare pauperum pedes, noctu solus et ignotus nosocomia frequentare, decumbentibus inservire, ac cetera caritatis officia exhibere consuevit: quarum virtutum merito illius dextera, resoluto cetero corpore, incorrupta permansit.
.
Stephen introduced into Hungary both the faith of Christ and the regal dignity. He obtained his royal crown from the Roman Pontiff; and having been, by his command, anointed king, offered his kingdom to the Apostolic See. He built several houses of charity at Rome, Jerusalem, and Constantinople: and with a wonderfully munificent spirit of religion, he founded the archiepiscopal See of Gran and ten other bishoprics. His love for the poor was equaled only by his generosity towards them; for, seeing in them Christ himself, he never sent anyone away sad or empty-handed. So great indeed was his charity that, to relieve their necessities, after expending large sums of money, he often bestowed upon them his household goods. It was his custom to wash the feet of the poor with his own hands, and to visit the hospitals at night, alone and unknown, serving the sick and showing them every charity. As a reward for these good deeds his right hand remained incorrupt after death, when the rest of his body had returned to dust.
.
Orandi studio noctes pene totas ducebat insomnes, atque in cœlestium rerum contemplatione defixus, interdum extra sensus raptus, sublimis in sera ferri visus fuit. Perduellium conspiratione, ac validorum hostium impetus, miro prorsus modo, non semel orationis præsidio evitavit. Susceptum ex Ghisella Bavarica, sancti Henrici imperatoris sorore, quam sibi matrimonio juxerat, Emericum filium tanta morum disciplina, talique pietate enutrivit, quantum ejus postea sanctitas declaravit. Regni vero negotia ita disposuit, ut accitis undique prudentissimis et sanctissimis viris, nihil umquam sine illorum consilio moliretur. Humillimis interim precibus in cinere et cilicio Deum deprecans, ut universum Hungariæ regnum, antequam e vita migraret, catholicum videre mereretur. Vere propter ingens dilatandæ fidei studium, illius gentis Apostolus nuncupatus, facta a Romano Pontifice ipsi, posterisque regibus præferendæ crucis potestate.
.
He was much given to prayer; and would spend almost entire nights without sleep, rapt in heavenly contemplation; at times he was seen ravished out of his senses, and raised in the air. By the help of prayer, he more than once escaped in a wonderful manner from treasonable conspiracies and from the attacks of powerful enemies. Having married Ghisella of Bavaria, sister of the emperor St. Henry, he had by her a son Emeric, whom he brought up in such regularity and piety as to form him into a saint. He summoned wise and holy men from all parts to aid him in the government of his kingdom, and undertook nothing without their advice. In sackcloth and ashes, he besought God with most humble prayer, that he might not depart this life without seeing the whole kingdom of Hungary Catholic. So great indeed was his zeal for the propagation of the Faith, that he was called the Apostle of his nation, and he received from the Roman Pontiff, both for himself and for his successors, the privilege of having the Cross borne before them.
.
Dei Genitricem, quam ardentissime venerabatur, amplissimo in ejus honorem constructo templo, Hungariæ Patronam instituit, ab eadem vicissim Virgine receptus in cœlum ipso suæ Assumptionis die, quem Hungari, e sancti regis instituto, Magnæ Dominæ diem appellant. Sacrum ejus corpus suavissimo fragrans odore, liquore cœlesti scatens, inter multa et varia miracula, Romani Pontificis jussu, nobiliorem in locum translatum est, atque honorificentius conditum. Ejus autem festum Innocentius Undecimus Pontifex Maximus quarto nonas septembris, ob insignem victoriam ab exercitu Leopoldi Primi Romanorum electi imperatoris et Hungariæ regis, eadem die in Budæ expugnatione, ope divina e Turcis reportatam, celebrandum instituit.
.
He had the most ardent devotion towards the Mother of God, in whose honor he built a magnificent church, solemnly declaring her patroness of Hungary. In return the Blessed Virgin received him into heaven on the very day of her Assumption, which the Hungarians, by the appointment of their holy king, call “the day of the Great Lady.” His sacred body, exhaling a most fragrant odor and distilling a heavenly liquor, was, by order of the Roman Pontiff, translated, amidst many and divers miracles, to a more worthy resting place, and buried with great honor. Pope Innocent IX commanded his feast to be celebrated on the fourth of the Nones of September; on which day, Leopold I emperor elect of the Romans and king of Hungary, had, by the divine assistance, gained a remarkable victory over the Turks at the siege of Buda.
.
Apostle and king, protect thy people, assist the Church, succor us all. At the close of that tenth century, when anarchy had penetrated even into the sanctuary, hope sprang up once more on the day whereon the Holy Spirit, the Creator and Renovator, chose thy race, in all its native vigor, to renew the youth of the world. Satan, who thought that the Papacy was humiliated once for all, trembled with rage when he saw new laborers coming to Peter, as to the only foundation on which it is possible to build. The proudest family that had ever caused the empire of Romulus to shake, asked of Rome the right to be counted among the nations of the West. How true it is that the gates of hell shall never prevail against the rock, against the Church founded thereon, against the holy city prepared on the top of mountains to draw all nations to itself. In vain had the storm stirred up the very mire of the torrents of the abyss: it was the hour when God lifted up his hand, as the prophet says, towards the far-off lands, and kings came, bringing to the ever holy Bride those unknown sons whom they themselves had educated for her.
.
No, the Lord confoundeth not them that wait for him. And therefore we will hope, even against hope, in the future of the noble nation established by thee upon the apostolic strength. A people justly proud of so many irreproachable heroes could not allow itself to be long led astray by a false liberty kept up by Jewish gold, and extolled by all the enemies of the country’s traditions. Martin watches together with thee over the land of his birth; and the sovereign of Hungary, the august Queen of heaven, will not suffer her loyal subject to the listen to the proposals of the infernal spirit.
