text:
AI is Trump’s Manhattan Project | Pippa Malmgren, UnHerd

What is science? This used to be a test question at school, but it is now a test question for society. Today, we are in the midst of a historic collision between scientific discovery and scientific dogma. In July, just as the White House issued “Science: A New Golden Age”, its sweeping new scientific roadmap, Congress was raking Dr Anthony Fauci over the coals. As America’s most visible scientific authority thanks to his role in the COVID pandemic, he became the personification of a troubling reality that, until recently, was heresy. Not only is traditional science alarmingly fallible, but it seems that some in the scientific establishment are willing to be deceptive rather than lose control of consensus, cash flows and power. As a New York Times headline put it: “We were badly misled.”

This has attracted the attention of President Trump and his Chief Scientific Advisor, Michael Kratsios, who comes from a private-sector background. They see an opportunity to wrest control of science from the bureaucracy — or perhaps even what MAGA loyalists might describe as the “priesthood” of experts who protect the science community at the expense of public well-being.

The travails of Dr Fauci, therefore, are part of a wider struggle. There is a broader, civilization-level conflict going on, one that was best articulated by Claude Lévi-Strauss in 1964 when he said: “The scientist is not a person who gives the right answers; he’s one who asks the right questions.”

Not long ago, anyone who said there was water on the moon was deemed a nutcase. Thanks to data gathered via India’s Chandrayaan-1 mission of 2008, and Nasa’s LCROSS mission of 2009, we know that there are some 600 billion kg of water ice in the moon’s polar regions — a discovery that bodes well for both manned and unmanned missions. In 2020, Nasa’s Stratospheric Observatory for Infrared Astronomy (SOFIA) confirmed the existence of water molecules in the sunlit regions as well.

The heretical discoveries range from space to the mundane matters of daily life. For instance, we used to think that ulcers were caused by spicy food and stress. Then, in 1979, Dr Robin Warren and Dr Barry Marshall, both Australian scientists, showed evidence that ulcers were caused by bacteria. The idea was heavily ridiculed, because almost every other scientist had accepted the dogma that no microorganism could possibly survive in human stomach acid. The opposition was so fierce that, for the sake of humanity, Marshall offered himself up as a rat lab by drinking broth made from a patient’s gastritis. First, he became violently ill from the H. pylori bacteria it contained, as he knew he would; then, he cured himself with antibiotics, proving that a peptic ulcer was the product of the bacterium. This discovery has saved millions from unnecessary surgeries and lifelong peptic ulcer disease. Today we know that the condition of the microbiome, the gut, is fundamental to our overall flourishing, and that our bodies are host to countless microorganisms capable of both inflicting profound illness and sustaining our happiness and health.

Science, in other words, is full of orthodoxies waiting to be overturned — which is exactly what Trump and Kratsios are aiming to do. The White House science strategy is a ruthless overhaul, upending traditional funding models and clearing out the legacy leadership that has long governed the scientific community: not only government bodies, but also institutions, such as universities, that are funded by the government. Naturally, many in the scientific establishment are horrified, given their animus for Trump and their hostility toward government meddling in science. But others are thrilled, because the new strategy released by the Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) is the most radical overhaul of the US federal research enterprise since the Second World War. It breaks the old guard’s control over who gets funding, what gets funded, and how science “should” progress.

Instead, it calls for funding individuals rather than institutions such as universities, no matter how garlanded. In other words, scientific investigators no longer need to be blessed by the scientific bureaucracy to qualify for funding. Marshall would have been funded a lot sooner had this approach been in place.

The OSTP is also gunning for the peer review system, via which scientific work is slowly and ceremoniously reviewed by other scientists. This approach is often inimical to radical new thinkers, but it has been maintained by universities for decades. Now individual agency reviewers can unilaterally advance unconventional and high-risk, high-reward proposals that traditional academic panels, mindful of existing scientific consensus, would probably reject. Federal money will now flow to “Focused Research Organizations”, which address well-defined problems over a deliberately short lifespan. (Note the contrast with the ancient and bloated university sector.) The roadmap will also enable faster delivery of grant money and, when appropriate, longer timeframes for researchers to get on with their work without having to apply for further funding. How much discovery has been blocked, even unconsciously, by an old guard whose livelihood and parent institutions benefited from scientific stasis?

But the government is not the only source of scientific funding. In fact, the private sector funds a significant proportion of university science. The question remains: how much of the science community has ignored ideas because of ego, or because their cash flows from sponsors would have been adversely affected by the new discovery? Peer reviewers are unlikely to admit that a new idea is right if it proves that their own life’s work is wrong. Some say the peer-review system is independent, but in the case of Fauci, who led the National Institutes of Health’s massive grant-giving process for 38 years, it seems scientists everywhere believed that publishing anything that ran counter to his views might well cause their funding to dry up.

Kratsios is also coming for the academic journals, another form of gatekeeper. From 1951, Robert Maxwell transformed the old peer-review system, which had been quaint and collaborative, into a multibillion-dollar commercial industry, starting with Pergamon Press. This forced journals and libraries to pay subscription fees to remain up to date. The academics, who had been doing this work for free, were now paid. Peer review prestige thus became commodified and monopolized, and the research itself became expensive to access. Kratsios, in response, is trying to cut the flow of taxpayer dollars to these journals.

As for Trump, he wants the credit for being the president who tore down those gates and the gatekeepers, and for enabling a new era of scientific discovery, one that will be led by free thinkers rather than bureaucrats. The OSTP is therefore pushing many scientists out of the National Science Foundation, the Food and Drug Administration, and the Centers for Disease Control. It is also limiting federal funds to the old academic institutions.

Central to the new strategy is the “Genesis Mission”, which is commonly described as the Manhattan Project of our generation. Just as the US, in the Second World War, sought to gain control of the atom and the atom bomb through the Manhattan Project, today the White House seeks to enable artificial intelligence to solve the greatest problems facing humanity, from health to energy. The core of the Genesis Mission is the “American Science and Security Platform”, which aims to consolidate the government’s massive supercomputing resources and its diverse research and experimental facilities. These facilities include the seventeen national labs, like Los Alamos National Laboratory and the Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory. These labs house immense bodies of work that their scientists have quietly accumulated over many decades.

We must remember that much of the research has been so highly classified that scientists could not share data within some of these labs, or across them, let alone with private researchers. The White House says this work is a public good paid for with taxpayer money and that all qualified scientists should be able to access it, especially since the old guard have either been wrong or are holding back innovations that would benefit the public.

The White House is also implying that the old-guard scientists have been using the “Classified” label as a “Keep Out” sign for too long. The Genesis Mission calls for all this data to be digitized, standardized, and made AI-ready so it can be shared and studied by both government and private scientists. By feeding many decades of extraordinarily valuable data to AI, the thinking goes, researchers can break open scientific silos and connect the dots between complex biological, chemical, and physical interactions.

In other words, the White House is saying America will go “open-source” in a controlled environment. The US won’t share everything with the world, but it will share it amongst a much broader pool of scientists. This modern Manhattan Project is designed to create an explosion in collaboration.

The most ambitious aspect of the strategy is to allow AI to run labs directly, testing new hypotheses, generating predictive models, and designing and executing new experiments. Science will thus no longer depend on the views or whims of individual scientists or gatekeepers. Science will become autonomous, self-driving, and continuously iterating, operating at a speed that it is impossible for human researchers to replicate.

The era of scientists pipetting chemicals or adjusting lasers or working directly with lab rats, then, is over. AI and robotics will automate both the decision-making and the physical actions. All this takes energy — and the US has some catching-up to do. A new nuclear power plant for example, used to require $30bn and thirty years of regulatory approvals. In May 2025, the White House gave small American nuclear firms the deadline of 4 July, 2026, America’s 250th anniversary, to “go critical” with small modular reactors using new technologies. Four firms made it. The US is now scaling up the nuclear energy needed to power the data centers and AI essential to the project of a Golden Age. Even now, AI is solving mathematical equations that were hitherto unsolvable — which will make for faster scientific progress. For example, nuclear fusion used to be perennially “50 years away”. It is advancing quickly now that AI and supercomputing are reshaping the boundaries of math and physics. The AlphaFold team won the Nobel prize in Chemistry for unlocking a decades-old puzzle of folding proteins, revolutionizing how scientists approach disease and drug discovery. Today the same AI-led transformation is happening across science.

The White House also seems determined to demonstrate that Dr Fauci was not the only scientist who prioritized cash flow and business interests over health outcomes. Back in April 2025, Kratsios made an intriguing claim while addressing a gathering of technologists. He said: “We are capable of so much more. Our technologies permit us to manipulate time and space. They leave distance annihilated, cause things to grow, and improve productivity.” It turns out that he was quoting President William McKinley in 1901. That was the era of electricity. What does “annihilating distance and manipulating time“ mean today? What clandestine research, observers wondered, was Kratsios referring to? It doesn’t seem to be a coincidence that, at the same time as the administration aggressively declassifies so much material across various agencies, it has also decided to nullify many government non-disclosure agreements — ensuring whistleblowers can come forward without risking their status, pensions, and possibly more.

We need to be prepared for what scientists call “ontological shocks”. These are the profound psychological or cognitive disturbances that can occur when a person or a society encounters new information that breaks their fundamental understanding of reality. All the talk in the AI community is that AI is about to revolutionize both maths and physics. This needn’t be scary: humanity’s worldview has collapsed many times before — be that in the Copernican Revolution, or when Darwin revealed his Theory of Evolution. And each of these collapses has been to our benefit. Of course, it will be different, more difficult this time: humanity has never had to contend with an intelligence that is so much greater than its own. No one knows what AI will optimize for. After all, we’ve programmed it for efficiency and profitability, but not for human connection. It’s been trained on the internet, a place that doesn’t represent the best of human intent or human thinking. Are we ready for the consequences of AI and the new approach to science that it will bring? It took three generations for humanity to adjust to Galileo’s worldview. Can we be sure to adjust any faster? Indeed, should we? Will new truths be more reliable than the old ones?

The White House, however, says humanity is entering a new “Golden Age”. Science is making extraordinary new discoveries almost daily, rendering old dogma obsolete. Many in the scientific establishment fear obsolescence. Sensing the barbarians at the gate, they fear a scientific dark age brought on by government intervention. But the old order had to end, as it always does — and given the advent of AI, superfast computation, and potentially explosive declassification, its destruction might not take long.

text:
Sam Darnold (QB, SEA): 2026 outlook

Sam Darnold enters his ninth NFL season firmly entrenched as the starter for Seattle, bringing a steady veteran presence to an offense that relies on efficiency rather than sheer volume. Last year, Darnold played in 17 games, logging 96 percent of the offensive snaps while averaging 28.06 opportunities per game and finishing the campaign with 235.4 total points. His passing volume sits in a conservative range. The offense operates at a negative pass rate over expected of 6.8 percent across 58.6 plays per game, though a market-implied team total of 24.5 points per game keeps the scoring environment respectable. Darnold brings almost no rushing floor to the table, and his red zone involvement was practically nonexistent last year at 0.12 red zone opportunities per game. That lack of goal-line utility places immense pressure on his passing efficiency to deliver weeks of strong production. Recent outings showcased both sides of this profile, ranging from a 22.3-point performance against Atlanta down to a quiet 6.1 points against Carolina. Two seasons of stable usage in the same system provide a high confidence baseline, but the scheme's run-leaning nature caps his ceiling. When the offense stalls near the goal line, Darnold loses out on the high-value touches that anchor top-tier fantasy quarterbacks. He remains a low-end option who needs clean efficiency and multi-touchdown passes to pay off, as his volume alone will rarely carry the weight.

What to watch:
• Monitor how the coaching staff handles play-calling in the red zone given his minimal rushing and scoring-area usage.
• Track the pass rate over expected to see if the offense opens up its aerial attack or stays conservative.
• Evaluate his dependency on clean pocket efficiency since rushing contributions offer a very thin floor.
• Watch for target distribution trends among receivers to ensure adequate volume translates into fantasy scoring.

text:
Broadcom ($AVGO ) Q3 FY2026: The Market Saw a $0.2B Miss. Hock Tan Saw the Birth of a New Hyperscaler Class.

The after-hours tape on September 2 told one story: AVGO dropped as much as 7% before trimming to ~3.5%. The headline trigger was a Q4 revenue guide of $34.8B versus the $35.03B LSEG consensus. A 0.7% miss.

But the conference call told a different one — one that fundamentally changes how to model the AI TAM. The gap between those two narratives is where the trade lives.

The Q3 scorecard, first. Revenue hit $29.6B, up 86% YoY, beating the $29.36B consensus. Adjusted EPS of $3.32 cleared the $3.24 estimate. AI semiconductor revenue: $16.7B, up 221% YoY and 54% sequentially. XPU shipments more than tripled YoY and now represent 73% of AI revenue. AI networking revenue grew more than 2.5x. Operating margin expanded to 67.9%, up 240bps YoY. Free cash flow hit a record $13.7B, or 46% of revenue.

All of that was in the rearview. The market's focus was forward.

The guidance that triggered the drop. Q4: $34.8B total revenue, $21.7B AI semiconductor revenue, 66% operating margin. The miss versus the $35.03B LSEG number is $230M — about two-thirds of one percent. StoneX analyst Cody Acree captured the market's mood: "The magnitude is not quite enough from a top and bottom line standpoint on the beat and raise when you have a company that is this levered to AI".

The guidance the market initially priced out. On the call, management laid out AI semiconductor revenue of ~$115B in FY2027 and ~$230B in FY2028. The FY2026 AI revenue forecast was raised to $58B (from $56B). For FY2028, EPS is expected to exceed $30. FactSet consensus for FY2028 AI revenue was $177B. The raise is $53B — or 230x the size of the Q4 guide miss.

The math is not complicated. The market applied a ~10x elasticity multiple (0.7% guide miss → ~7% stock drop) to the short-term number and effectively ignored a 30% upward revision to the three-year-out number.

But the real story is not in the numbers — it is in the structural shift Hock Tan articulated.

On the call, Tan made a point that fundamentally changes how to think about AI demand: AI labs are becoming hyperscalers in their own right.

"Now, these guys are going to be hyperscalers in their own right.""So what they do is they want first-party compute capacity, just as they create their own. They want to create silicon that is very cost-performance optimized, and they want to run their own data centers eventually. They want to run it as fast as they can.""Short term, you're right, they are using cloud services, third-party services, to deploy their models.""Long term, we see these guys to be no different from a hyperscaler, and they will run their own data centers and be first-party to offer AI, generative AI API access to models to the world.""So we see that happening. It's not speculation, it's actually happening, and we are in the midst of enabling that."

This is not a demand story that peaks with hyperscaler capex cycles. It is a permanent expansion of the number of entities that buy silicon at scale. The XPU customer set is no longer just Google, Meta, Microsoft, and Amazon — it includes Anthropic, OpenAI, and others building their own infrastructure.

Why this structural shift matters for the $230B target.

First, the ASIC replacement cycle. As inference workloads scale — and token economics become the binding constraint for AI application margins — the cost-per-token advantage of custom silicon becomes a competitive necessity. Broadcom holds ~70–85% of the custom ASIC design services market. That is not a cyclical tailwind; it is a structural shift in how AI compute gets purchased.

Second, customer deployment visibility. The call provided concrete numbers: Anthropic is on track for 5GW of TPU deployment in FY2027 with visibility into an incremental 10GW. OpenAI targets 5GW of chip deployment in FY2028, with production starting in late FY2026. Tan defended the Google partnership directly: "Our partnership with Google will continue to sustain because we have the strongest IP portfolio in semiconductor design, including industry leading SerDes chip-to-chip interconnect, leading-edge HBM and SRAM integration, and simply differentiated advanced packaging. Most of all, we have consistently delivered the fastest time to market for TPUs from product definition to production".

Third, the networking flywheel. Tan expects AI networking revenue to grow just as fast as XPUs over the next few years. Tomahawk 6, the world's first 102.4Tbps Ethernet switch chip with co-packaged optics, is already shipping in production volume. It supports scale-up clusters of 512 XPUs and two-tier scale-out networks of 100,000+ XPUs at 200Gbps/link. If XPU revenue scales from $58B to $230B, networking revenue scales in lockstep.

The supply constraint is the ceiling, not the risk. Management stated explicitly that demand exceeds the FY2027 outlook. The binding constraints are land, power, data-center readiness, leading-edge wafers, substrates, and HBM memory. Tan was explicit: "We can ship significantly more. [The] question on our mind sometimes is: Are they going to be — even as we ship the chips — going to be deployed on a timely basis? And that's always very much in our mind when we give you that outlook". He continued: "If circumstances change, and our ability to secure more supply changes, of course, we will uplift". In July 2026, Broadcom signed a $200B+ MOU with Samsung through 2030 covering HBM4/HBM4E, sub-2nm foundry, and advanced packaging.

The valuation anchor. At the after-hours low around $367, with FY2028 EPS guidance above $30, the forward P/E is ~12.2x. The FactSet consensus EPS for FY2028 is $26.38 — still only ~13.9x. Jefferies analyst Blayne Curtis reiterated a Buy with a $550 price target, noting FY2028 EPS could reach $30–$40. For a business compounding AI revenue at 100% annually, with operating margins above 65% and FCF conversion at 46% of revenue, that is not expensive.

The invalidation conditions are clear. This thesis breaks if: (1) FY2027 Q1 AI revenue growth decelerates below 15% sequential, undermining the credibility of the doubling trajectory; (2) Google materially shifts TPU volume to Marvell or in-sources completely (watch the TPU v8 allocation in 2027); or (3) HBM4E supply tightens globally and Broadcom fails to secure priority allocation despite the Samsung MOU.

The bottom line. The market priced a $230M quarterly miss and ignored a $53B long-term raise. More importantly, it priced AI demand as a function of existing hyperscaler capex cycles, missing the structural expansion Tan articulated — AI labs becoming hyperscalers themselves. At 12x FY2028 earnings, the market is pricing stagnation. The guidance implies compounding, driven by a permanent expansion of the buyer base. Those two things cannot both be right.

text:
NETWORKING AND OPTICAL INTERCONNECT

ETHERNET IS MOVING FROM SCALE-OUT INTO SCALE-UP, EXPANDING THE MERCHANT NETWORKING MARKET AND PRESSURING NVIDIA’S PROPRIETARY FABRIC (READ-THROUGH 7)

Affected companies: Arista Networks, Inc. (ANET: United States) — Positive, high magnitude. Celestica Inc. (CLS: Canada) — Positive, high magnitude. Accton Technology Corporation (2345: Taiwan) — Positive, high magnitude. Cisco Systems, Inc. (CSCO: United States) — Positive, medium magnitude. NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA: United States) — Negative, medium-to-high magnitude for networking and system attach.

Supporting call evidence: Broadcom stated that Tomahawk 6 has been deployed across “pretty much all of the AI hyperscalers,” including customers that do not use Broadcom XPUs. AI networking revenue increased by more than 2.5 times YoY and is expected to triple YoY in Q4. Tomahawk Ultra is beginning deployment in both XPU and GPU scale-up clusters, with management stating that adoption has “surprised us.” Broadcom also taped out Tomahawk 7, described as the industry’s 1st 200-terabit-per-second Ethernet switch.

Near-term trading catalyst: Tomahawk Ultra deployments began in Q3 and are expected to increase during FY2027. Broadcom’s Q4 expectation that AI networking revenue will triple provides an immediate demand signal for switching systems, white-box equipment, cabling, and optics.

Long-duration fundamental shift: Ethernet is expanding from conventional scale-out networking into scale-up domains that connect accelerators within tightly coupled clusters. Scale-up has historically favored proprietary or specialized fabrics because of stringent latency, loss, synchronization, and collective-communication requirements. Broadcom claims that Tomahawk Ultra can now deliver comparable performance using an open Ethernet architecture.

The positive transmission mechanism for Arista is a significant expansion of Ethernet’s addressable market. If Ethernet becomes viable inside the accelerator domain, the number and strategic importance of Ethernet switching layers per cluster increases. Arista also benefits from customer preference for open, multi-vendor networking and from hyperscalers seeking to avoid dependence on the accelerator supplier for the entire system architecture.

The benefit is not guaranteed to accrue exclusively to branded switch vendors. Hyperscalers may build direct white-box systems using Broadcom switch silicon. This makes Celestica and Accton particularly important read-throughs because both can participate in hyperscaler-designed networking equipment and custom platforms. Arista is best positioned where customers value a complete networking system and software stack; Celestica and Accton are better positioned where customers retain design control and outsource manufacturing.

Cisco receives a positive but lower-magnitude read-through. A broader open-Ethernet ecosystem expands the available market, although Cisco’s ultimate share will depend on its ability to compete in the highest-performance AI fabrics and secure hyperscaler adoption.

The negative transmission mechanism for NVIDIA extends beyond the potential loss of GPU units. Even when NVIDIA retains the accelerator sale, customers may select Broadcom-based Ethernet rather than NVIDIA’s proprietary networking and switch architecture. This reduces networking attach, limits full-system capture, and weakens the strategic value of bundling GPUs with networking.

Broadcom’s disclosure that Tomahawk Ultra is being adopted in some GPU clusters is particularly important. It demonstrates that accelerator choice and networking choice can be separated. The most adverse scenario for NVIDIA is therefore not only XPU displacement, but also retention of the GPU sale without the corresponding networking, switch, and system revenue.

OPTICAL INTERCONNECT DEMAND REMAINS SUPPLY-CONSTRAINED, BUT BROADCOM’S CAPTIVE LASER EXPANSION CHANGES THE COMPETITIVE EQUILIBRIUM (READ-THROUGH 8)

Affected companies: Coherent Corp. (COHR: United States) — Positive near term, mixed over the longer term; high near-term magnitude. Lumentum Holdings Inc. (LITE: United States) — Positive near term, mixed over the longer term; high near-term magnitude. Zhongji Innolight Co., Ltd. (300308: China) — Positive, high magnitude. Eoptolink Technology Inc., Ltd. (300502: China) — Positive, high magnitude.

Supporting call evidence: Broadcom stated that demand for EML and CW lasers is “fast surpassing supply out there in the industry.” The company is expanding its indium-phosphide, EML, and CW-laser factories in the United States and Singapore by more than 3 times YoY and plans further significant expansion over the following 2 years. Broadcom expects AI networking revenue to grow as rapidly as XPU revenue over the next several years.

Near-term trading catalyst: The explicit statement that laser demand is exceeding supply supports strong utilization, pricing, and order visibility across the optical component and transceiver chain. The Q4 tripling of AI networking revenue and the FY2027 ramp of Tomahawk 6 and Tomahawk Ultra create immediate requirements for higher-speed optical links.

Long-duration fundamental shift: Accelerator clusters are becoming larger, more distributed, and more bandwidth-intensive. Higher switch capacity does not eliminate optical demand; it increases the number of high-speed lanes that must be transported between racks, clusters, and data-center zones. The transition toward 200-gigabit-per-second lanes and future 200-terabit-per-second switches raises the requirement for 1.6-terabit and eventually higher-speed optical modules.

The positive transmission mechanism for Coherent and Lumentum is strong merchant demand for lasers, photonic components, and high-speed optical technologies. Industry scarcity should support factory loading and improve customer willingness to enter long-term capacity commitments.

The longer-term read-through is more mixed because Broadcom is aggressively internalizing the same optical components. Captive capacity can reduce Broadcom’s purchases from merchant suppliers and allow Broadcom to sell more complete optical solutions into the market. Broadcom’s scale in switch silicon and optical DSPs gives it a strong position from which to coordinate laser, DSP, and networking roadmaps.

The negative competitive effect should not be overstated. Broadcom’s decision to triple capacity also confirms that total market demand is expanding rapidly. Merchant suppliers can continue growing even if Broadcom captures a larger share, provided aggregate optical demand increases faster than industry capacity. The principal risk is therefore relative market share and pricing after additional capacity enters production, rather than a near-term demand contraction.

Innolight and Eoptolink receive a cleaner positive volume read-through because the cluster roadmap implies rapidly rising demand for complete optical modules. Company-specific awards were not disclosed, but the sector-level requirement is clear. The largest upside will accrue to suppliers able to qualify high-speed products, secure lasers and DSPs, maintain yield, and deliver at hyperscale volumes.

DATA CENTER POWER, COOLING AND PHYSICAL INFRASTRUCTURE

LAND, POWER AND SHELL—not accelerator demand—ARE EMERGING AS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT (READ-THROUGH 9)

Affected companies: Vertiv Holdings Co. (VRT: United States) — Positive, very high magnitude. Eaton Corporation plc (ETN: Ireland) — Positive, high magnitude. Schneider Electric SE (SU: France) — Positive, high magnitude. GE Vernova Inc. (GEV: United States) — Positive, high magnitude. Quanta Services, Inc. (PWR: United States) — Positive, high magnitude. Delta Electronics, Inc. (2308: Taiwan) — Positive, high magnitude.

Supporting call evidence: Broadcom’s financing platform is intended to support more than 20 gigawatts of compute infrastructure for OpenAI and Anthropic by the end of 2028. Management described approximately 30 gigawatts of potential deployment across its 6 XPU customers during FY2027 and FY2028. Hock Tan stated that “land, power and shell” dictate the specific timing of deployments and must be assessed before Broadcom includes demand in its financial outlook. Management also stated that power consumption per accelerator increases with every XPU generation.

Near-term trading catalyst: The first approximately $35 billion Anthropic infrastructure tranche has already closed and the associated 1-gigawatt deployment is underway. Additional 2027 sites must be in advanced development because land acquisition, utility interconnection, equipment procurement, and data-center construction have long lead times.

Long-duration fundamental shift: The principal AI bottleneck is moving beyond semiconductor availability toward physical infrastructure. The compute roadmaps disclosed by Broadcom cannot be realized without electrical distribution, substations, generation capacity, backup systems, power conversion, liquid and air cooling, transformers, switchgear, busway, and large-scale construction services.

The positive transmission mechanism for Vertiv is exceptionally direct. Higher accelerator power density increases cooling intensity, power-distribution requirements, and the value of integrated thermal and electrical solutions per rack. Even if a semiconductor program shifts from NVIDIA GPUs to Broadcom-enabled XPUs, the underlying facility still requires high-density cooling and power infrastructure. Vertiv therefore benefits from aggregate gigawatt growth with less sensitivity to accelerator market share.

Eaton, Schneider Electric, and Delta Electronics benefit from switchgear, UPS systems, busway, power conversion, rack-level electrical systems, and data-center energy management. The rise in power per accelerator increases content per rack even before accounting for the increase in total rack count.

GE Vernova benefits from the need for incremental generation, grid equipment, turbines, and electrification infrastructure. Quanta Services benefits from transmission, distribution, substation, utility interconnection, and specialized construction work required to bring large sites online.

The most important portfolio implication is that power and cooling suppliers may offer a cleaner exposure to the aggregate AI build than individual accelerator companies. The infrastructure requirement persists whether a site uses NVIDIA GPUs, Google TPUs, OpenAI XPUs, Meta MTIA, or another custom architecture.

Broadcom’s caution that not all 30 gigawatts will necessarily enter production during FY2027-FY2028 creates timing risk. However, the same constraint strengthens supplier pricing and backlog visibility because the limiting resources are precisely the products and services sold by the affected infrastructure companies. Delays may shift revenue between periods, but they do not eliminate the underlying need unless AI infrastructure demand itself is cancelled.

CUSTOM XPU DEPLOYMENTS SHIFT SYSTEM VALUE TOWARD HYPERSCALER ODM AND JDM RACK INTEGRATION (READ-THROUGH 10)

Affected companies: Quanta Computer Inc. (2382: Taiwan) — Positive, high magnitude. Wiwynn Corporation (6669: Taiwan) — Positive, high magnitude. Hon Hai Precision Industry Co., Ltd. (2317: Taiwan) — Positive, high magnitude. Celestica Inc. (CLS: Canada) — Positive, high magnitude.

Supporting call evidence: Broadcom described customer requirements in terms of both chips and, in some cases, completed racks. The company is coordinating successive generations of custom accelerators with networking, HBM, substrates, optical components, and complete data-center deployments. Management expects the largest AI laboratories eventually to operate their own 1st-party data centers as hyperscalers.

Near-term trading catalyst: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta all require production systems during FY2027, with multiple accelerator generations entering deployment. The systems must be engineered and qualified before the semiconductor revenue can be recognized at full scale.

Long-duration fundamental shift: The transition from merchant GPUs toward customer-specific accelerators changes where system value is captured. Standard merchant-server platforms become less relevant when the customer controls accelerator architecture, network topology, memory configuration, rack power, and cooling design. Hyperscaler ODM and joint-design-manufacturing capabilities become more important.

The transmission mechanism is demand for custom baseboards, compute trays, rack integration, high-current power delivery, liquid cooling, cable assemblies, optical connectivity, and factory-scale system testing. Each new XPU generation requires substantial mechanical, electrical, firmware, and thermal co-design rather than only substitution of a different processor into an existing server.

Quanta Computer, Wiwynn, and Hon Hai are positioned to benefit from hyperscaler-direct procurement models in which the end customer retains architectural control and outsources design implementation and manufacturing. Celestica benefits from similar capabilities across custom hardware, networking, and complex systems.

The disclosed supplier awards were not identified, so company-specific revenue allocation remains uncertain. The high-conviction conclusion is at the business-model level: custom AI infrastructure favors large ODM and JDM suppliers with hyperscaler relationships, high-volume manufacturing, advanced cooling expertise, and the ability to integrate non-standard accelerator systems.

The shift may be relatively less favorable for branded server vendors that depend on standardized merchant platforms and distributor-led sales. Those vendors can still participate if selected for rack integration or enterprise deployments, but the largest custom-XPU campuses are more likely to use direct, highly customized procurement models.

CAPITAL FORMATION AND AI INFRASTRUCTURE FINANCING

AI INFRASTRUCTURE IS BECOMING A LARGE PRIVATE-CREDIT AND INFRASTRUCTURE-LEASE ASSET CLASS (READ-THROUGH 11)

Affected companies: Apollo Global Management, Inc. (APO: United States) — Positive, medium-to-high magnitude, with contingent credit risk. Blackstone Inc. (BX: United States) — Positive, medium-to-high magnitude, with contingent credit and residual-value risk.

Supporting call evidence: Broadcom established the AI XPV platform with Apollo and Blackstone to enable more than 20 gigawatts of compute infrastructure for OpenAI and Anthropic through 2028. The first approximately $35 billion tranche supports Anthropic’s initial 1-gigawatt deployment and is already underway. Broadcom stated that third-party financial partners independently underwrite and capitalize the assets, while future tranches will contain structures tailored to specific laboratories and investors.

Near-term trading catalyst: Additional Anthropic and OpenAI deployment tranches will require financing decisions well before the relevant 2027 and 2028 systems enter production. Each closing can create substantial incremental fee-bearing assets, origination economics, and deployment opportunities for the participating alternative managers.

Long-duration fundamental shift: Frontier-model laboratories require infrastructure investment materially ahead of internally generated cash flow. This creates a structural role for private credit, infrastructure funds, asset-backed leasing, and special-purpose financing vehicles. AI compute is developing into a financing market comparable in scale to major infrastructure categories rather than remaining solely a technology capital-expenditure category.

The positive transmission mechanism for Apollo and Blackstone is the origination and management of large, long-duration pools of institutional capital. The initial $35 billion transaction demonstrates that individual tranches can be material even for the largest alternative-asset managers. Repeated financing across more than 20 gigawatts could generate meaningful fee-related earnings and strengthen relationships with technology companies, institutional investors, sovereign capital, and infrastructure operators.

The risk mechanism is customer credit and asset specificity. OpenAI and Anthropic are expected to monetize infrastructure through future AI-service revenue, but the systems are being financed before their long-term cash-flow capacity is fully established. The underlying assets may also be more customer-specific than standard GPU systems because custom XPUs are optimized around proprietary models, software, and network architectures.

Apollo and Blackstone can mitigate these risks through seniority, customer equity contributions, lease terms, Broadcom support, diversification, collateral rights, and residual-value protections. Nevertheless, the transactions should not be evaluated as risk-free infrastructure debt. Returns depend on utilization, model competitiveness, customer liquidity, and the secondary-market value of specialized AI systems.

The broader market implication is that access to capital is becoming part of semiconductor competitive advantage. Broadcom is helping solve not only chip design and supply, but also customer funding. Competitors unable to coordinate financing may be disadvantaged even if their underlying silicon is technically competitive.

OPENAI AND ANTHROPIC’S MOVE TOWARD FIRST-PARTY COMPUTE IS A LONG-DURATION CLOUD LOCK-IN RISK (READ-THROUGH 12)

Affected companies: Microsoft Corporation (MSFT: United States) — Negative, medium magnitude over the longer term; near-term neutral to positive. https://t.co/SpqvHNUxpK, Inc. (AMZN: United States) — Negative, medium magnitude over the longer term; near-term neutral to positive.

Supporting call evidence: Hock Tan stated that OpenAI and Anthropic “are going to be hyperscalers in their own right.” Management said the laboratories currently use 3rd-party cloud services but ultimately want 1st-party compute capacity, custom silicon, and their own data centers “as fast as they can.” Broadcom’s XPV financing platform is explicitly intended to bridge the gap between current customer cash flow and the upfront investment required to build those environments.

Near-term trading catalyst: The immediate effect is not negative for cloud providers. OpenAI and Anthropic continue to require large amounts of 3rd-party cloud capacity while first-party campuses are financed and constructed. Cloud partners can therefore continue benefiting from near-term accelerator consumption, infrastructure services, networking, and overflow workloads.

Long-duration fundamental shift: The laboratories intend to reduce structural dependence on external cloud platforms by owning or controlling more of the compute stack. If successful, this changes the laboratories from major cloud tenants into direct infrastructure operators and potential competitors in AI model and API delivery.

The negative transmission mechanism for Microsoft is a gradual reduction in the percentage of OpenAI compute that must be consumed through Azure. OpenAI-owned custom silicon and financed 1st-party data centers would increase OpenAI’s bargaining power, reduce the strategic exclusivity of the cloud relationship, and limit the long-term cloud-margin opportunity attached to OpenAI’s growth.

The comparable mechanism for Amazon is Anthropic’s move toward Google-architecture TPUs and independently financed infrastructure. AWS can remain a major partner while still capturing a smaller percentage of Anthropic’s incremental compute than would be possible under a single-platform arrangement.

The effect should be framed as dilution of lock-in rather than immediate workload loss. Frontier laboratories will likely maintain multi-cloud and overflow relationships because demand volatility, geographic distribution, resiliency, and product integration make complete independence uneconomic. The negative read-through concerns the terminal share of compute economics and strategic control, not the elimination of cloud consumption.

Alphabet is relatively better hedged against this development because its TPU architecture can potentially participate even when the end customer controls the infrastructure. A cloud platform with monetizable silicon intellectual property can retain economic exposure after workloads migrate from conventional rented cloud capacity toward customer-controlled environments.

SEMICONDUCTOR DESIGN SOFTWARE

OVERLAPPING MULTI-GENERATION XPU ROADMAPS SUPPORT A DURABLE EDA AND ADVANCED-DESIGN SPENDING CYCLE (READ-THROUGH 13)

Affected companies: Synopsys, Inc. (SNPS: United States) — Positive, medium-to-high magnitude. Cadence Design Systems, Inc. (CDNS: United States) — Positive, medium-to-high magnitude.

Supporting call evidence: Broadcom is simultaneously developing successive Google TPU generations, 3 OpenAI XPU generations, 3 Meta MTIA generations, Tomahawk 7, advanced optical DSPs, and multiple packaging and connectivity technologies. OpenAI’s 2nd-generation XPU was described as approaching tape-out while the 3rd generation is already in development. Broadcom highlighted its ability to move from product definition to production rapidly and without the need for redesign or respin.

Near-term trading catalyst: The number of active tape-outs and overlapping customer programs supports high EDA utilization immediately. Each customer requires parallel architecture, verification, physical design, package, power, thermal, and system-development work well ahead of production revenue.

Long-duration fundamental shift: The AI semiconductor cycle is increasing both the number and complexity of leading-edge designs. Custom silicon does not replace merchant GPU design spending; it adds additional accelerator architectures on top of continuing GPU, CPU, networking, memory, and optical development. The result is a structurally larger design workload across the semiconductor industry.

The transmission mechanism for Synopsys and Cadence is increased consumption of digital-design tools, verification, emulation, formal analysis, interface IP, package-design software, signal-integrity analysis, power analysis, and system simulation. Advanced accelerators integrating HBM, chiplets, high-speed SerDes, optical networking, and sophisticated packaging require EDA workflows extending beyond the silicon die.

The economic value of avoiding a design failure rises with each generation. A respin can delay a multi-gigawatt data-center program, disrupt customer infrastructure schedules, and postpone billions of dollars of revenue. This increases customers’ willingness to spend on verification, emulation, signoff, and system analysis.

Broadcom’s emphasis on time to market is particularly constructive for EDA suppliers. Faster overlapping roadmaps require greater automation and compute intensity rather than less tooling. The principal benefit is durable recurring demand rather than a single-quarter order catalyst.

PORTFOLIO SYNTHESIS

The Broadcom call is most positive for HBM suppliers, leading-edge foundry and packaging capacity, Ethernet networking, optical interconnects, power and cooling infrastructure, hyperscaler ODMs, and alternative infrastructure-financing platforms. These beneficiaries participate in aggregate AI deployment regardless of whether the accelerator is an NVIDIA GPU or a customer-specific XPU. The cleanest positive read-throughs are SK hynix, Micron, TSMC, Vertiv, Eaton, Schneider Electric, GE Vernova, Quanta Services, Arista, Celestica, Quanta Computer, Wiwynn, Apollo, and Blackstone.

The most important negative read-through is the emergence of a quantified custom-XPU displacement path for NVIDIA and AMD within the largest frontier-model customers. The impact is likely to appear first in accelerator share, networking attach, and pricing power rather than in absolute revenue contraction. NVIDIA’s exposure is compounded by Broadcom’s attempt to move open Ethernet into scale-up networking, allowing customers to separate GPU procurement from networking procurement.

The most differentiated strategic read-through is the weakening of cloud lock-in. Anthropic and OpenAI are being financed and equipped to become hyperscalers in their own right. This supports Google’s TPU architecture and Broadcom’s custom-silicon model while creating a longer-duration risk to the percentage of AI economics captured by AWS and Azure.

The principal caveat across all positive read-throughs is timing. Broadcom stated that demand exceeds its FY2027 and FY2028 forecasts, but land, power, shell, HBM, substrates, and system readiness determine when that demand becomes recognized revenue. The most attractive cross-portfolio exposures are consequently suppliers that benefit from the infrastructure bottlenecks themselves rather than only from the final accelerator shipment.

text:
Methodist University Denies Operating ‘Hidden’ DEI Program After Undercover Video Posted of School Official | Fox News

An official at Southern Methodist University was captured on undercover video describing what she called "a lot of maneuvering" surrounding the school’s diversity, equity and inclusion efforts, according to footage released by Accuracy in Media that purports to show how DEI initiatives continued under different names.

The video, shared Monday by school choice activist Corey DeAngelis, alleges SMU renamed its Office of Diversity and Inclusion the Office of Cultural Intelligence as part of an effort to keep DEI programming less visible.

The SMU staff member, who is identified in the video by Accuracy in Media as Danielle Palomo, coordinator for community engagement, social change and intercultural engagement division of student affairs, said, "As you can probably imagine, we've had to do a lot of maneuvering in order to remain kinda hidden under a lot of things. But as long as we can keep doing what we're doing even to a smaller capacity, that is what we're going to do. We're going to do our best."

In the video, an undercover journalist asks Palomo, "I was hoping to see if y'all had any existing, like, equity trainings that maybe y'all provide for staff faculty and that would give us an idea of what to go off of."

Palomo responded, "So, all of that is held through our Office of Cultural Intelligence. As you can probably imagine, we've had to do a lot of maneuvering in order to remain kind of hidden under a lot of things. But my office in particular, we do — we have had trainings like that in the past with students.

"It's not going to be as severe, hopefully, as some of the other public universities have had to deal with, but I know that the university is definitely finding its like 'P's and Q's' and it's slowly like working to like rename things and maybe do away with things," Palomo said in the video.

While SMU is a private university, it holds 164 active federal grants totaling nearly $30 million from agencies, including the departments of Defense, Health and Human Services, and Education, according to a May 2025 report by its independent student newspaper, The Daily Campus.

The outlet also reported that SMU’s research and development spending has more than tripled since 2010, rising from $18.7 million that year to nearly $59.8 million in fiscal year 2023.

The Trump administration has moved to restrict DEI initiatives at federally funded schools through executive actions and Department of Education directives, though federal judges have blocked portions of those efforts amid constitutional and procedural challenges.

The Department of Education has also warned state education departments they must remove diversity, equity and inclusion policies or potentially lose federal funding.

In a statement to Fox News Digital, a spokesperson for SMU said, "SMU does not operate a hidden Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) program. The university does offer activities under the Cultural Intelligence framework that was originally adopted in 2017. Cultural Intelligence focuses on the ability to learn from and understand different perspectives, strengthen relationships and foster mutual respect and community."

"Through this approach, we equip members of our university community with the skills to communicate, lead, teach, coach and innovate effectively across different perspectives and experiences," the spokesperson added. "As with all university programs, SMU regularly reviews its practices to ensure they align with applicable legal requirements and our institutional mission."

In a statement to Fox News Digital, school choice activist Corey DeAngelis said, "The Trump administration should pull every dollar of federal funding from universities that keep pushing DEI after pretending they shut it down. The radical left running these campuses is not rooting out Marxist DEI ideology. They are moving the goalposts, renaming offices and hiding the same agenda under new labels like ‘cultural intelligence.’

"SMU tuition is $63,736. Parents might be surprised to learn they are paying that much for a Christian university that is still pushing divisive far-left ideology. SMU also takes more than $25 million in federal funding each year.

"A school charging that kind of tuition does not need taxpayer money to keep DEI alive under another name. If they want to keep the ideology, they can do it without federal funds."

Fox News Digital reached out to Palomo for comment.

text:
What is the "Explanatory Memorandum" I have attached to this post for your viewing? 

It is a 1991 Arabic memo (with an English court translation) that federal prosecutors entered as evidence in the Holy Land Foundation trial.

***Full Title*** : *An Explanatory Memorandum on the General Strategic Goal for the Group in North America*  

***Date*** on the memo: May 22, 1991 (sometimes cited as May 19)  

***Author*** : Mohamed Akram (also rendered Mohamed Akram Adlouni)  

***How it became public : FBI agents found it in 2004 in the Annandale, Virginia home of Ismail Elbarasse. 

*Who was Ismail Elbarasse?***

**Ismail Selim Elbarasse** (also spelled Ismael Selim Elbarasse) is a Palestinian-American from Annandale, Virginia, identified by U.S. authorities as a Hamas activist and unindicted co-conspirator in Hamas fundraising cases.

In August 2004, he was arrested as a material witness after Maryland State Police saw his wife videotaping close-ups of cables and structural features of the Chesapeake Bay Bridge from their SUV. He was not charged in connection with the videotaping. Authorities held him for a Chicago grand jury investigating Hamas financing; he was released after about 10 days on $1 million bond (homes posted as collateral). He was about 57 at the time.

Elbarasse was a former board member of the Islamic Association for Palestine (IAP). He served on the Palestine Committee, a U.S. body created by the Muslim Brotherhood to support Hamas politically and financially. He worked as an assistant to Mousa Abu Marzook (then Hamas political director) and shared a Virginia bank account with him that authorities said was used to transfer hundreds of thousands of dollars linked to Hamas activities. Documents seized from his home in 2004—internal Palestine Committee records, organization charts, and related materials—were introduced as evidence (“Elbarasse Search” exhibits) in the 2008 Holy Land Foundation trial, in which five officials were convicted of funneling money to Hamas.

He was named an unindicted co-conspirator in related federal cases but was not himself convicted in those prosecutions. The documents and financial records from his home and accounts formed a significant part of the government’s evidence about the U.S. Hamas support network in the late 1980s and early 1990s.

Prosecutors used it as Government Exhibit 003-0085 in *United States v. Holy Land Foundation* (N.D. Tex. 3:04-CR-240). 

*** The original document "Explanatory Memorandum" is in Arabic; the English version circulating is the government’s trial translation. Both are included in the attached file. 

***What it says it is trying to do***
  
Akram presents it as an explanatory supplement to a longer-term plan he says the Brotherhood’s North American Shura Council approved in 1987. The stated general goal is “Enablement of Islam in North America,” meaning a stable Islamic movement led by the Muslim Brotherhood that:

-> Adopts Muslim causes at home and abroad  
-> Expands the observant Muslim base  
-> Unifies and directs Muslim efforts  
-> Presents Islam as a “civilization alternative”  
-> Supports “the global Islamic State wherever it is”

***The most-quoted passage*** :

-> “The process of settlement is a ‘Civilization-Jihadist Process’ with all the word means. The Ikhwan must understand that their work in America is a kind of grand Jihad in eliminating and destroying the Western civilization from within and ‘sabotaging’ its miserable house by their hands and the hands of the believers so that it is eliminated and God’s religion is made victorious over all other religions.”

It also talks about building “firmly-established organizations,” mastering “the art of coalitions,” “absorption,” and “cooperation,” and shifting from a “collision mentality” to an “absorption mentality.” An appendix lists groups it calls “our organizations and the organizations of our friends,” with the line “Imagine if they all march according to one plan.”

***How people treat the document***

Two readings sit side by side:

-> Critics and prosecutors treat it as an authentic internal Brotherhood planning paper describing a long-term political/settlement strategy (“civilization jihad”) inside the United States.

text:
They jailed her for refusing a seat, then gave her a mattress and she refused that too. It lay on the floor of the Roanoke Rapids cell filthy enough that Sarah Keys stayed upright in her uniform for thirteen hours, pacing in shoes with an inch-and-a-half heel. Her father had taught her to buy a through ticket so no Southern driver could touch her, and she had done it exactly right, and it did not matter. Go find out what your own people were taught about traveling south, because somebody in your family was taught something.

The mattress was on the floor and she would not put her body on it.

So for thirteen hours she stayed upright inside a locked room in a town she had never meant to stop in, in the uniform of the United States Army and a pair of shoes with a heel an inch and a half high.

Her name was Sarah Keys. She was a Private First Class in the Women's Army Corps, twenty-three years old, and she had been arrested a few minutes past midnight for staying where she was sitting.

She was sitting there on her father's instructions.

David Keys had taught all of his children how to travel from the North to the South, and the rule was one line long. Buy a ticket on a bus that runs straight through, no changes, no transfers, nothing that hands a Southern driver an excuse.

"I had purchased my ticket making sure that it was a straight through bus, a bus with no changes," she said years later, on a recording made to help raise money for a memorial to her. "But to my surprise, when I got to Roanoke Rapids, North Carolina, there was a big problem."

She had bought that ticket at Fort Dix and left on the evening of 31 July 1952, on her first leave since enlisting, headed home to Washington, North Carolina. The Supreme Court had ruled six years earlier in Morgan v. Virginia that Southern segregation law could not be laid on a passenger crossing state lines, and the through ticket was her proof that she was one of those passengers.

She took the fifth seat from the front. The back of a bus in August was the hot part, the part that took the bumps, the part where the engine came in through the rear windows.

Then she slept.

The first thing that went wrong was that the bus stopped at all. Shortly after midnight it pulled into the Trailways terminal on Roanoke Avenue and a different man climbed behind the wheel.

New drivers re-checked tickets at a driver change, so he started down the aisle with his hand out. A white Marine had boarded at that stop.

He reached the fifth seat, woke her up, and told her to move to the back so the Marine could have it.

She was still coming out of sleep when she answered him.

"I'm perfectly comfortable right here where I am."

He did not argue with her. He said nothing at all and kept moving down the aisle, taking tickets from everybody else.

Then he got off the bus. He was gone a few minutes.

When he came back he ordered every other passenger off and walked them onto a different bus in the lot. A sailor helped her get her luggage down.

She stood in the lot and watched the second bus fill up with the people she had been riding beside since Washington, D.C. Then she went inside the station to find out what was happening to her.

Inside there was a ticket window with a woman behind it. Sarah Keys walked up, and the woman pulled the curtain down in her face and dimmed the lights.

"It's sort of like in a movie, you know?" she said on the recording, all those years later.

She turned around. A tall Black man was standing in the terminal, and he looked at her.

"Miss, don't you know where you are?"

"I said to myself," she remembered, "Oh God, Sarah, you are in trouble."

The police came into the terminal and the driver pointed her out. They said she had been unruly and that she had been cursing.

Two officers took her by an arm each and put her in the back of a car. Roanoke Avenue had no street lights in 1952.

A Black woman, in the hands of white men, in the dark, in a town she did not know, with no way of telling where the car was going.

She asked to call her family. They told her they would make the call for her, and she believed them.

Where the car went was the cell with the mattress in it.

So she walked. Back and forth across a few feet of concrete in a pressed uniform and an inch-and-a-half heel, for thirteen hours.

"I paced the floor all night, and I cried and I prayed," she said. "What is happening to me?"

Nobody was coming. The officers had promised to make that call and never made it, and her parents spent that night and the day after it in Washington not knowing where their daughter was.

In the morning a jailer came and walked her out of the cell and took her to the chief of police.

The chief looked her over.

"Is that a uniform you're wearing?"

She had been on her feet since midnight.

"You mean to tell me you don't know the color of the United States Army uniform?"

He told her that was exactly why she had spent the night in jail. Because she was too damn smart.

He fined her twenty-five dollars and threatened to slap her. Then they walked her back to the bus station, put her on a bus, gave her an assigned seat and told her not to move from it until she reached her destination.

A twenty-three-year-old soldier had been jailed for keeping a seat and was released with a seat chosen for her and an order not to leave it.

She got home and did not want to talk about it. She wanted the whole thing behind her.

The officers had written her up as unruly and cursing. "Sarah was the quietest of us all," her sister Cornelia Hargrave said.

Her father would not let it go.

David Keys was a Navy veteran of the First World War and a convert to Catholicism in a stretch of North Carolina where he was, for a time, the only Black Catholic in his town. He was the man who had taught her the through-ticket rule, and the rule had not saved her, and he told her to go back and find out what had been disorderly about her conduct.

She went back and lost in the local court. The family carried it to the NAACP office in Washington, D.C., which was run by the Howard law professor Frank D. Reeves.

Reeves handed the file to a former student of his, on the theory that this client needed a particular kind of lawyer. He had one in mind who had been on a Southern bus in uniform herself.

In the winter of 1943, Dovey Johnson Roundtree had been riding through Miami recruiting Black women into the same Corps Sarah Keys would later join. She was ordered to give up her seat to a white Marine, threatened with arrest, and put off the bus.

There was no one to call. Katie McCabe, who spent ten years writing Roundtree's life with her, points out that Congress had declined the year before to pass a bill protecting Black service personnel traveling through Jim Crow states, and that the military had not backed it either.

If you were Black and in uniform on a Southern road in those years, you were on your own. Two women who had learned that the hard way now had the same case in front of them.

"It was as though I sat looking in a mirror," Roundtree wrote about taking the case, "so strong was my sense of having walked where Sarah Keys had walked."

She and her partner Julius Winfield Robertson had been at the bar about a year. They knew better than to try it in a Southern courtroom, so they filed in federal district court in Washington, and on 23 February 1953 that court threw it out for want of jurisdiction.

On 1 September 1953 they filed instead with the Interstate Commerce Commission, the federal body that regulated travel across state lines. Sarah Keys became the first Black petitioner ever to bring a Jim Crow bus complaint before it, on docket MC-C-1564, and then everyone waited on the Supreme Court.

Brown v. Board of Education came down on 17 May 1954. On 30 September 1954 the Commission's hearing examiner, Isadore Freidson, ruled that Brown had no bearing whatsoever on how a private bus company chose to run its business.

Roundtree found a Spelman classmate living in the right congressional district and got word to Adam Clayton Powell. Powell pushed, the full eleven-member Commission agreed to rehear it, and the lawyers were given thirty days to file exceptions.

Her own lawyers were worried about Sarah Keys. She was shy, she was quiet, and they did not know how she would hold up under hostile questioning from a federal commission.

She came in wearing the uniform and testified calmly all the way through. McCabe describes what Roundtree watched happen in that room as a coming of age.

On 7 November 1955 the Commission ruled for her. It found that assigning a traveler accommodation designed to imply his inherent inferiority solely because of his race had to be regarded as unreasonable, and that making Black interstate passengers sit in specified portions of a bus violated Section 216(d) of the Interstate Commerce Act.

It is still the only explicit repudiation of separate but equal ever issued by any court or federal agency in the field of bus travel across state lines. The decision was made public on 25 November, and the New York Times printed it with a compliance deadline attached: January 10.

By then she was out of the Army and working as a hair stylist in Harlem. "It is a big relief to have it behind me," she told the Times on 27 November 1955.

Asked to account for three years of it, she named one person. Her father had encouraged her, she said, when she needed encouragement.

Six days after the announcement, in Montgomery, Alabama, Rosa Parks did not move.

The Commission's vote that month had not been unanimous. One commissioner dissented, a South Carolina Democrat named J. Monroe Johnson, and he happened to be the chairman of the agency.

The historian Catherine Barnes records that Johnson consistently failed to enforce the ruling from that chair. January 10 came and went and the buses across the South ran exactly as they always had.

Five and a half more years went by. In May 1961 a Greyhound burned outside Anniston, Alabama, and men were waiting with pipes for the Freedom Riders in Birmingham and Montgomery.

On 29 May 1961 Attorney General Robert Kennedy petitioned the Interstate Commerce Commission to enforce its own rulings, citing the Keys case by name. The Commission issued the regulations on 22 September and they took effect on 1 November 1961.

That is nine years and three months after a driver in Roanoke Rapids worked his way down an aisle and woke a sleeping soldier.

She had not waited around for any of it. Sarah Keys married George Evans in 1958 and settled in Brooklyn, where she kept doing hair and belonged to Our Lady of Victory.

She never set foot in Roanoke Rapids again, not in five years, not in fifty, not in seventy.

In 2001 a writer named Amy Nathan found her name on a plaque at the Women's Memorial in Arlington and spent about two years interviewing her. No publisher would take the book.

"Several editors said to me, 'We already have a book about Rosa Parks, so that sort of covers the topic,'" Nathan said. She put it out herself in 2006.

Roanoke Rapids came around sixty-eight years later. On 1 August 2020 the city and Halifax County declared it Sarah Keys Evans Day and unveiled a mural of her arrest, eight panels by the Halifax County artist Napoleon Hill, with a plaza to follow the next year in Martin Luther King Jr. Community Park.

She was ninety-one and could not travel. So the woman being honored attended the ceremony in the town that jailed her by telephone, from an apartment in Brooklyn, six hundred miles away.

"This is a glorious day for me," she said down the line to a crowd standing in a park she had never seen. "I wish I could have been there in person."

A state highway marker went up in front of the old bus station in January 2022, after an eighth-grade social studies teacher named Rodney Pierce spent years pushing for one. Pierce is the one who points out that the avenue had no street lights that night, and he is also the person who noted publicly that the department which jailed her was run by a police chief named T. J. Davis.

The city of Roanoke Rapids still operates a recreation center named for T. J. Davis. The local paper's own caption says the chief helped build it.

The one thing that town never got around to was the money. The twenty-five dollars was never returned, and Ophelia Goulz-Faison, who researched the case for the plaza committee, confirmed that in 2022, when the fine would have been worth around two hundred and fifty dollars.

Sarah Keys Evans died on 16 November 2023 at ninety-four and was buried at The Evergreens Cemetery in Brooklyn. On the recording she had already said what she wanted out of all of it, and it was not money.

"I like to be remembered as someone who helped somebody along the way," she said. She said she liked the words pioneer and trailblazer, and that those were the ones she wanted.

So that is the debt, and it costs nothing but breath. The next time somebody starts the bus story in Montgomery, put the week before it back in, and put her name on it, because there was already a federal ruling on the books and a soldier's name was on it.

The docket is MC-C-1564 and it is free to read.

She spent thirteen hours on her feet rather than touch the only thing that town ever offered her to rest on. In the morning a man with a badge looked at the uniform she had stood up in all night and asked her whether it was a uniform at all.

I put a lot of effort into researching and sharing stories that matter. If you'd like to support the work, here's the link:
https://t.co/AeER0VXcAK

text:
Be Tommy Mello, SMB legend…

KKR just paid $2 billion for his garage-door company.

> Grew up in Sterling Heights, Michigan. 
> Parents split when he was seven. 
> Mom worked three jobs. 
> He listened through the wall while they fought about bills.
> At 8 he was mowing lawns and shoveling snow. 
> At 12 he washed dishes under the table for $4.05 an hour because Michigan said you had to be 13.
> Moved to Phoenix at 16.
> Landscaping. Bartending. Flipping cars. Reselling Bowflex machines. Cleaning pools. 
> By 20 he was already a hustler who could make money, not a founder yet.
> A roommate offered him $100 a door to paint garage doors. 
> He didn’t know how. He learned. 
> Weekends he was painting 10–12 doors a day.
> Then he noticed the real money wasn’t paint. It was springs, rollers, broken doors, and showing up when other guys didn’t.
> 2007: A1 Garage Door Service. 
> The name was a ranking hack. A1 came first in the Yellow Pages, so the phone rang. 
> First logo came out of a fighting video game. 
> First “HQ” was a house across from a 7-Eleven.
> Early years were chaos. $50k in debt. Used trucks. Stolen phones. People stealing toilet paper. No real CRM. If it could go wrong, it did.
> Around 2010 he takes the business from a partner who couldn’t scale with him. 
> Mom and stepdad move from Michigan to help. He is still the business. Vacation means revenue dies.
> First decade is practice. 
> Revenue crawls, then jumps: about $17M, then $30M, then $50M. 
> He kills the hustler version of himself and builds systems, SOPs, KPIs, and a company that can run without him in every truck.
> The four numbers he obsessed over: booking rate, conversion rate, average ticket, cost per acquisition.
> He rebrands when most owners wouldn’t (around $30–40 million in revenue) so the trucks, site, uniforms, and signs all look like one company.

A Coimbra linguist placed the later woman’s accent in Viseu. Post-1967 letters were judged forgeries, while the 2000 vision text was called authentic handwriting lacking Our Lady’s explanation.
