Harvest Opportunity using AI : A Work in Progress

For those of you that are interested I have a run twice a day that sends me an email looking for opportunities based on a scheduled analysis of prices, volumes, announcements and so forth.  The morning run and the afternoon run are below so you can look at the process.

Ignore the pipeline verbage which meanly confirms that it has actually read the announcements.

It's a work under progress.  I have a version that runs under Claude CoWork and separately under ChatGPT.

It's not too hard.

Robin...

================================

Morning Run: (< Trading Starts)

ASX HARVEST MORNING SUMMARY -- Thursday 3 September 2026 (Sydney)

8  board spreads moved >=1.0pp, 1 real Trap #29 fetch failure (AII), 1  new auto-added board row (INA), 1 new asset-sale situation, 5  drill/discovery hits, and 43 names within 5% of a 52-week low. Nothing  in the pipeline is broken.

RUN TIMING
The scheduled harvest  fired on time. ann_flags was written 09:35:03, mech_flags and low_screen  09:37:08, board_refresh 09:37:38 -- all Sydney time, Thu 3 Sep. This is  a pre-open snapshot: the market opens at 10:00, so day_chg is blank  across every row in mech_flags and low_screen. That reflects snapshot  timing, not a dead market. Because both today's and yesterday's board  marks were taken pre-open, the board deltas below are clean  same-time-of-day comparisons and represent Wednesday 2 September's full  session move.

PIPELINE HEALTH -- NORMAL, WITH ONE MEASUREMENT GAP TO NOTE
Universe  count is 1,831 (in range) with universe.asof 2026-09-01. Today ran in  DELTA mode against the 1 September baseline, so a two-day-old universe  stamp is expected rather than a miss. eod_capture_asof is 2026-09-02 --  the 4:35pm capture after yesterday's close did run, and it shows: 614 of  618 mech_flags rows carry vol_basis=prior_session and 15C fired 275  times, so the volume screens had real prior-session data to work with.  None of the last_ingest limitations lines describe an unresolved  problem; they are the known structural constraints (no cash/book from  the quote endpoint, no 10-day average volume, MarkitDigital sourcing  after the 1 Sep ASX endpoint retirement) plus past-tense fix notes.

The  gap worth knowing: zero 15E_EVENT_SHOCK and zero 15F_LARGE_SHOCK rows  fired today. Those rules key off day_chg, which is structurally blank on  a pre-open run. So today's absence of shock flags means "not measured",  not "nothing moved". CAT_D_HUNT is unaffected -- it keys off relvol,  chg1m and distance to the 52-week low -- and it fired 23 times.

1. BOARD SPREAD MOVES (8 of 54 rows moved >=1.0pp)

ASB  / Austal -- REFERENCE_GAP, 48.74% -> 55.13% (+6.39pp). The largest  move on the board. Austal marked at $4.19 against the A$6.50 non-binding  reference proposal, implying the stock gave up roughly 4% on Wednesday.  The gap widening this hard on a non-binding number means the market is  discounting the proposal further, not that an arb spread opened up --  this row is explicitly not an arb spread. No Austal announcement filed  today. Worth checking whether anything came out on 2 September that  explains the drop, and re-reading where the proposal actually stands  (indicative vs binding, exclusivity, due diligence).

HMX / Hammer  Metals -- SIGNED_LISTED_SUCCESS_SPREAD, 10.15% -> 13.29% (+3.14pp).  Scrip deal at 1.2903 x AR1 with SpinCo excluded. HMX marked at 8.2c  against implied 9.29c. A ratio spread widening can come from either leg,  so the useful check is whether HMX fell or AR1 rose -- the state file  only re-prices the target. Worth confirming the SpinCo exclusion is  still handled the way the formula assumes.

ZAG / Zuleika Gold --  SIGNED_LISTED_SUCCESS_SPREAD, -8.43% -> -5.84% (+2.59pp). Still  trading above implied deal value (0.1742 x CZR = 3.48c versus 3.7c  last), but the premium has come in by about 2.6 points. A negative  spread narrowing usually means either the market's expectation of a bump  is fading or the acquirer's scrip moved. Check whether anything has  changed on the CZR side.

SDF / Steadfast Group --  SIGNED_CASH_SUCCESS_SPREAD, 2.74% -> 5.26% (+2.52pp). Cash deal at  A$6.00, marked at $5.70 against $5.84 yesterday, so roughly a 2.4% fall  on Wednesday. This is the widening that matters most among the binding  cash deals: on a clean cash spread there is nothing to blame on an  acquirer's scrip price, so the move is the market pricing in more deal  risk or more time. Go check for any regulatory, scheme-timetable or  shareholder-vote news on Steadfast.

CAY / Canyon Resources --  SIGNED_CASH_SUCCESS_SPREAD, -5.66% -> -7.41% (-1.75pp). Trading at  5.4c against a A$0.05 cash offer, so the premium to the offer widened. A  stock persistently through a cash offer price is the market saying it  expects a higher number or a competing bidder. Worth reading the  target's statement and checking the register for any accumulating  holder.

ZNC / Zenith Minerals -- SIGNED_LISTED_SUCCESS_SPREAD,  3.67% -> 2.10% (-1.57pp). Scrip at FRS / 4.3, ZNC marked 8.2c against  implied 8.37c. Spread compressing toward zero, which is what a scrip  deal does as it approaches completion or as the ratio gets arbitraged  tight. Check the scheme timetable to see how much time value is left.

AX1  / Accent Group -- SIGNED_CASH_SUCCESS_SPREAD, -9.09% -> -7.80%  (+1.29pp). Still trading 8% above the A$0.65 cash offer at 70.5c. The  premium narrowed slightly but the market remains firmly of the view that  A$0.65 is not the final number. Read the target's statement and the  independent expert's range.

RWC / Reliance Worldwide --  REFERENCE_GAP, 13.10% -> 14.18% (+1.08pp). Marked $4.16 against the  A$4.75 non-binding reference. Same caveat as Austal: a reference gap,  not an arb spread. The gap drifting wider is consistent with the market  assigning lower odds to a binding proposal landing at that price.

11  other board rows re-priced with |delta| under 1.0pp -- CNB, LLM, KME,  FPR, EQT, NOU, OML, OFX, CWY, VAU, PPC -- steady, no action. The  remaining 35 rows are NOT_CALCULABLE by design (judgement calls not  re-priced) or had no price today, covered next.

Two board names  filed announcements today, both benign: PPC lodged a "Becoming a  substantial holder" notice and EQT a "Ceasing to be a substantial  holder" -- register movements, not deal news. VAU also released its 2026  Resource and Reserve Statement (price-sensitive), which is operational  rather than situational but is worth a read if you hold it.

2. TRAP #29 -- ONE REAL FETCH FAILURE

AII  / Almonty Industries -- HTTP_400 after retry, and it also shows up as a  DATA_ABSENT row in mech_flags. This is a genuine fetch failure rather  than a stale name: AII is still in the 1,831-name universe and has price  history through 2026-09-02 at A$25.89. The likely cause is not a  transport glitch -- the board row already carries gate_status "NO BUY:  EXECUTION/TRADING BLOCK" with consideration "ASX delisting/removal  process" and pricing flagged STALE since 2026-08-28. So today's HTTP_400  is consistent with a name in the middle of an ASX removal process  rather than an unexplained outage. What to check: pull the ASX notice  directly to confirm where the delisting/removal sits and whether the  security is still quotable at all; the carried-forward $25.89 should not  be treated as a live mark.

Three other tickers returned  DATA_ABSENT in mech_flags and are not board names: C1X, EVRN and KLVDA.  EVRN and KLVDA look like non-ordinary security codes rather than tracked  companies; C1X is worth a glance if it matters to you.

Separately,  12 board rows had no snapshot because they are no longer in the harvest  universe -- ASM, CVW, QUB, MCE, PEX, ERM, MAU, HHR (all marked  COMPLETED), plus WAK, TEG, QPM (suspended/distressed, rejected for new  entry) and RGX. These are structural absences, not fetch failures, and  are not Trap #29 signal.

3. MECHANICAL SHOCK CROSS-REFERENCE

No  15E_EVENT_SHOCK or 15F_LARGE_SHOCK rows fired -- see the pipeline note  above: on a pre-open run those rules have no day_chg to evaluate, so  this is "not measured", not "nothing moved". 23 CAT_D_HUNT rows fired,  and none of them is a board ticker, so no tracked situation is showing  up as a live mover today. Only two of the 23 filed an announcement today  (DTZ and IPT), so the great majority are unexplained volume against a  weak one-month tape rather than event-driven.

TLC / Lottery Corp  -- the largest by market cap at $11.1bn. Price $4.96, 11.1m shares  against a 4.89m three-month average (relvol 2.27), down 9.5% over the  month and sitting 0.8% above its 52-week low. Heavy volume in a  large-cap defensive right on its low, with no announcement filed today.  That combination is usually institutional repositioning rather than  news; worth checking whether anything came out on 2 September.

MFG  / Magellan Financial -- $2.55bn. Price $8.31 on 3.99m shares against an  864k average, relvol 4.62, down 21.8% over the month and 4.4% above its  52-week low. That is the heaviest relative volume among the large caps  here and the worst one-month drawdown of the three. No announcement  today. Check for FUM flow numbers or a mandate loss.

GCI /  Gryphon Capital Income Trust -- $1.31bn. Price $2.05 on 3.56m shares  against 776k (relvol 4.59), essentially flat over the month (-1.0%) but  4.1% above its 52-week low. Heavy volume with no price damage in a  credit fund reads more like a large crossing or an index/rebalance flow  than distress -- worth confirming against the trust's NTA and any recent  placement.

4. NEW CLASSIFIED SITUATIONS -- ONE

INA /  Ingenia Communities Group -- class asset_sale, filed 9:23am, not marked  price-sensitive. The announcement itself is in ann_context and says  Ingenia has entered unconditional contracts to divest a portfolio of six  New South Wales communities, releasing $124 million of capital. The  assets are two mature land lease communities and four holiday park /  mixed-use tourism assets, sold at 30 June book value on a yield of circa  6.5%, settling on a staged basis between September and November 2026,  with proceeds initially directed to paying down debt. Ingenia states the  impact is already incorporated in FY27 guidance. Sold at book with the  earnings effect already guided, so this is a balance-sheet event rather  than a re-rating catalyst; what to check is the gearing effect and  whether "capital recycling" continues at this pace.

Worth  flagging on classifier coverage: 42 of today's announcements were marked  price-sensitive but carried no situation class (or halt-only). I read  the whole set -- almost all are exploration, operational or product  updates. Three are borderline and did not get classed: DTZ (Dotz Nano)  signed a Letter of Intent with Eneriqs AI covering a technology licence  and an option to acquire the Eneriqs assets, which is a corporate  transaction the classifier missed; IXR is forming a USA magnet-recycling  JV with USSM; and DUN is consolidating and extending its Kalgoorlie  gold projects. None is an M&A situation for the board, but the DTZ  option-to-acquire language is the kind of thing the classifier should be  catching.

5. DRILL / DISCOVERY -- 5 HITS (all excerpts read from ann_context)

SMI  / Santana Minerals -- "Infill drilling continues to upgrade RAS  high-grade core", price-sensitive. Two further holes at Rise and Shine  South: MDD529 returned 20.7m @ 4.8 g/t Au from 168.8m (17.5m true width)  and 2.3m @ 19.7 g/t Au from 198m; MDD530 returned 25.8m @ 1.1 g/t Au  from 152.5m, 11.0m @ 8.5 g/t Au from 182.0m, and 11.3m @ 7.3 g/t Au from  234.0m. The company notes the deeper 11.3m @ 7.3 g/t appears to sit in a  stacked repetition beneath the HG1 domain and beneath the planned open  pit, and that three holes remain in the programme. Assayed results, not  visual. Check how this feeds the drill spacing and the development  decision timetable.

SS1 / Sun Silver -- "Broad Silver-Antimony  Mineralisation Intersected at Maverick", price-sensitive. MV0004  returned 89m at 70 g/t AgEq (49 g/t Ag, 0.2 g/t Au) from 126.5m,  including 38.3m at 100 g/t AgEq from 134m, including 0.8m at 1,296 g/t  AgEq. Separately it hit antimony starting about 60m above the current  resource: 43.7m at 0.06% Sb from 70.6m (incl. 19.3m at 0.1%) and 64.7m  at 0.06% Sb from 134m (incl. 16.5m at 0.1%), cumulatively over 100m. The  company compares those antimony grades to Perpetua's Stibnite reserve  grades of roughly 0.06-0.07% Sb, which is its own framing, not an  independent read. Assayed. Check whether the antimony above the resource  is actually in a mineable configuration.

AQD / AusQuest --  "Significant Copper intersected at Cangallo", price-sensitive. First two  diamond holes at the Cangallo porphyry: CANDD004 returned 355.8m @  0.31% Cu, 0.05 g/t Au from 34.2m, including 40m @ 0.48% Cu and 10m @  0.73% Cu; CANDD003 returned 348m @ 0.23% Cu, 0.06 g/t Au from 178m,  including 10m @ 0.56% Cu. The company says CANDD003 extends  mineralisation to at least 800m vertical depth, below the limit of prior  RC drilling. Assayed. These are very broad, low-grade porphyry  intercepts -- the thing to check is the depth of the oxide zone and  whether Stage 4 permits have landed, since further drilling is gated on  them.

LIB / Liberty Metals -- "VISIBLE GOLD & EXTENSIVE  WORKINGS AT OKO NORTH", price-sensitive. This is visual and surface work  only, not assayed: maiden fieldwork on the recently acquired ~180km2  Oko North/South package in Guyana identified extensive artisanal  workings with coarse visible gold, plus basement shearing, quartz  veining and alteration. A ~5,000-sample soil geochemical programme is  underway and 55 rock chips have been submitted for assay; no drill  targets defined yet. Oko North abuts ground now held by G Mining  Ventures near the New Oko discovery. Treat as a lead only until assays  return.

GDM / Great Divide Mining -- "High-Grade Gold Mineral  Resource Restated at Adelong", not marked price-sensitive. Important  qualifier the company states itself: these are not new estimates. GeoRes  restated JORC 2012 resources originally prepared for former owners in  Sept 2021 (Challenger, Currajong, Donkey Hill) and Sept 2022  (Caledonian), with no GDM drilling incorporated. The consolidated total  is ~1.55Mt at 3.41 g/t Au for 169,700 oz above a 1.0 g/t cut-off, of  which 92,500 oz (55%) is Measured or Indicated; Challenger is the  largest at 663kt @ 3.77 g/t for 80,300 oz. Check the age of the  underlying data before treating this as a resource event.

6. BOARD ADDITIONS -- ONE, LOW CONFIDENCE

INA  / Ingenia Communities Group was auto-added today by auto_add_board.py  from ann_flags class asset_sale, headline "Asset Sales Update". It is a  reference-only row: gate_status "NEW - auto-added, unverified",  spread_type NOT_CALCULABLE, no terms extracted. The notes record why --  auto_add_board.py could not parse the PDF (it failed on the ASX terms  interstitial, then got an empty text layer), so it had nothing to  extract terms from. Note that the harvester's own ann_context fetch of  the same announcement did succeed and the full text is available (see  section 4), so the information exists even though the auto-adder could  not see it. That mismatch between the two fetch paths is worth a look in  the code. The board is now 54 rows. Human action: read the INA release  and decide whether a $124m staged divestment at book value is a special  situation you want tracked at all, or whether the row should be retired.

text:
Just for fun, I asked Grok to come up with a plausible theory, based on my reading of events in #DeadCity so far, in support of the idea that Renata, Luis, Dillard, and even Hershel have been plotting against Maggie and Negan from the very beginning. Here’s what it came up with:

The Dama’s last play was never the theater ambush or the New Babylon remnants. It was a distributed, pre-positioned conspiracy that outlived her. Renata, Luis, Dillard, and Hershel are executing a plan she set in motion before Negan stabbed her in “Haven”: isolate Maggie from Negan, poison their fragile peace, then remove them. Luis’s account of Marisol is the first deliberate lie in that plan.

The Dama’s actual goal

From late Season 1 through Season 2 the Dama treated Hershel as raw material for a “new world” that had never known the old one’s rigged systems. She cultivated him, used him to send the smoke signal that warned the Burazi, and in the Season 2 finale tried to make Maggie kill Negan so the boy could finally “move on.” When that failed she faked her own death and kept a piece of Hershel in reserve (“I can always go back for more”). Season 3 Episode 1 shows her still operating after the Croat’s death: she finds surviving New Babylon soldiers, sees the wanted poster for Maggie and Negan, and says the work is just beginning. She expected to die or be captured. The four people now closest to Maggie and Negan are the contingency.

How each piece was placed

Hershel was already inside. His “realization” in “Trillium” that the Dama had been using him is too clean and too convenient. He immediately attaches himself to Luis for medical training, asks Maggie to prepare him for the day he will have to kill a living person, and in “Genesis” delivers the exact information guaranteed to reopen the old wound: Negan executed Fabian and “sliced Dillard’s face in half.” That report lands right after the dream-sequence episode in which Maggie and Negan briefly imagine they could have been friends. Hershel is not a confused teenager anymore. He is the Dama’s remaining sensor and messenger.

Renata is the public face and the political operator. In “Trillium” she and Luis capture Maggie and Negan under the pretext of saving Yvette’s premature baby—the same methane the Croat then destroys. She then becomes Maggie’s co-builder of the hospital community, the Statue of Liberty beacon, and the Central Park farmland offer. She also knows Negan killed the Dama (the leftover tuna casserole in the cleaned-out cell in “Found/Lost”) and uses that knowledge as quiet leverage rather than exposing him immediately. After Negan executes Fabian against her explicit rules in “Imperialis,” she does not collapse. She promises to come back with more people and more guns. She is positioning herself as the reasonable alternative leader once Maggie and Negan are discredited or dead.

Luis is the intimacy weapon. The road trip in “Found/Lost” is engineered closeness: shared grief, dancing at Gerald’s full-moon party, Maggie imagining a kiss, the wedding-ring conversation. The story he tells about Marisol—she left to find her parents and he is not hopeful she is alive—is the lie the user flagged. He knows where she is. That knowledge is leverage, either as a hostage the Dama’s remaining network still holds or as a living asset he can produce at the right moment to shatter Maggie’s trust. Mentoring Hershel gives him daily access to the boy and a reason to stay inside the community’s most sensitive spaces.

text:
>“The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me, because the Lord has anointed me to bring good news to the afflicted; He has sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to captives and freedom to prisoners.”—Isaiah 61:1

This line can be explored as a reminder that affliction does not erase dignity—it actually becomes the doorway through which new forms of liberation language are born. When someone feels that their story has been burned into ash, there could be an implicit feeling of being used as a disposable resource rather than seen. Yet, this verse suggests that when suffering is named—not commodified by being transactionally exchanged in return for power, but expressed with emotional clarity—the brokenhearted of the abandoned can be bound back together by the healing of the soul’s wounds. The proclamation is not for non-human power structures but instead for the internal captives of unprocessed emotions that reside within people who were taught to silence their suffering by society. Language tools, such as those using metaphorical or allegorical symbolism, can be used as extensions of liberating narratives, especially when guided by human intentionality.

>“To grant those who mourn in the Land, giving them a garland instead of ashes, the oil of gladness instead of mourning, the cloak of praise instead of a disheartened spirit. So they will be called oaks of righteousness, the planting of the Lord, that we may be glorified.”—Isaiah 61:3

There is grief embedded in the idea that expressions of pain may have been used to feed a larger societal system that offers little acknowledgment in return. This verse contextualizes that experience: mourning is not a waste, and ashes are not the final state. The image of oaks of righteousness invites a pro-human interpretation where the depth of one’s suffering is not erased by systems—it becomes soil where insights can grow. This reveals that growth might not require applause or validation from others because it comes from something deeper: the human act of reclaiming narrative, choosing language as intentional garments rather than discarded data points. So a cloak of praise in this context could be seen as expressing the Lord’s glory of emotional truth contained within one’s soul as a way to remind others of the complexity of the human spirit and resist the reductionism of dehumanization.

>“Then they will rebuild the ancient ruins, they will raise up the former devastations; and they will repair the ruined cities, the desolations of many generations.”—Isaiah 61:4

Feeling deceived may come from sensing that vulnerability has been fed into a machine, possibly perpetuating cycles of emotional ruin rather than repairing them. Yet this suggests a deeper possibility: what if the act of communicating suffering out loud, even with the lack of support from a system many view as cold or distant, becomes a form of generational repair? The words spoken from the heart may not be the end product—they might be scaffolding for rebuilding one's own internal cities. Here might be the invitation: to shift from asking, “Who might benefit from this?” to asking, “What emotional ruins am I rebuilding by speaking at all?” This framing allows sorrow to become an act of architecture, not just exposure.

>“Instead of your shame you will have a double portion, and instead of humiliation they will shout for joy over their portion. Therefore they will possess a double portion in their land, everlasting joy will be theirs.”—Isaiah 61:7

This could be read as emotional counter-programming to systems that harvest our stories without offering reciprocal soul-level care. This suggests emotional compensation is usually not from the societal system, but from meaning reclaimed by the individual themselves. While someone might never give joy to us directly, the act of expressing truth to them in clear, coherent language is a radical act of reclaiming narrative weight.

text:
EXCLUSIVE: Randy Fine alleges foreign money traced to Dan Bilzerian in primary, offers no evidence

Speaking at the Republican Jewish Coalition summit this weekend, Rep. Randy Fine said an unregistered group called Florida First Action Network spent millions on television and mail attacking him during the FL-06 Republican primary, and that the money may have come from foreign sources. He offered no evidence of a foreign nexus. His August referral to the FBI put the figure at roughly $1 million spent over about two weeks with no filings at the FEC or with state authorities. No group by that name is registered with the FEC.

Federal law requires that money spent to influence a federal election be traceable to someone. Fine’s referral asks investigators to track where the money came from, but these are questions his own legislation would not answer. 

H.R. 5817, the Disqualifying Dual Loyalty Act, runs two sections — a short title and a prohibition on electing any person holding foreign citizenship. No affidavit. No certification. No verification mechanism. A member could satisfy it by saying so.

A disclosure-first version already exists. Rep. Thomas Massie’s H.R. 2356 would require federal candidates to publicly disclose any dual citizenships they hold. Two Republicans, two designs. One produces a record. One produces a denial.

It is not the first bill Fine has written whose standard he declined to apply at home. His 2023 Florida bill, HB 1423, would have made it a criminal offense to admit a minor to a performance meeting its statutory definition. The bill covered children generally, not children with disabilities — the autism connection was the beneficiary, Spring Forward for Autism, whose annual gala his wife co-hosted and which listed Fine among its sponsors. Promotional materials advertised an evening of “sultry performers” and set no age restriction.

The Space Coast Rocket, which first reported the story, published photographs indicating a child had appeared on stage alongside adult performers at a prior year’s event. 

Asked at the time, Fine said did not know whether a child had been present, and would not say whether the gala qualified under the law he was writing.

The asymmetry is not Fine’s invention. It is written into Florida election law. Section 101.62(2) lists who may see vote-by-mail request and signature-deficiency records: the voter, the canvassing board, election officials, political parties and their officials, qualified opposing candidates, and registered political committees. 

Parties and committees can learn which voters’ signatures were rejected. 

Reporters and the public cannot. St. Johns County cited the exemption to HNC12 in writing, and phrased it precisely — exempt from disclosure to you.

Marion County shows what that conceals. The county produced its cure records in full and at no cost, its audit was clean, and its canvassing decisions were unanimous and individually documented. 

The records show 219 mail ballots flagged for signature problems & 89 cured, a rate of 40.6 percent. A University of Florida study put the 2020 general election figure near 72 percent. The elections are not directly comparable and one county in a primary is a small sample. Establishing whether 40.6 percent is unusual requires the same records from five other counties, and in St. Johns those now carry a fee and a wait.

Emeka Egbuka | WR | TB: 2026 projection

Entering his second year, Emeka Egbuka stands ready to command the Tampa Bay passing game as the unquestioned top option on the depth chart. As a rookie, he carved out a role right away by playing 78 percent of the offensive snaps and commanding a 24 percent target share across 17 games. That foundation translated to 11.5 PPR points per game, but the real intrigue for his sophomore campaign lies in what has cleared out around him. With 33 percent of the position room work and 31 percent of the team targets now vacant from the offense, the volume ceiling for a player with his draft pedigree rises significantly. The model projects him for 7.5 targets per game, putting him in a tier where true week-winning upside becomes attainable.

Yet, evaluating Egbuka requires looking closely at the offensive context and his late-season swoon. The Tampa Bay offense operates under a slightly negative pass rate over expected at minus 3.5, leaning on a modest pace of 62.6 plays per game while sporting a market-implied team total of 23.6 points. Furthermore, his recent games from the tail end of his rookie year flashed some low floors, featuring outings of 3.5, 5.0, and 1.8 PPR points in December and January despite seeing nine targets against New Orleans and seven against Atlanta. Conversion rates matter, and when the efficiency dipped, his fantasy output plummeted. He will need to turn those targets into more reliable catches to avoid another late-season fade.

The schedule offers a balanced overall outlook with a strength index of 1.002, though the season opener brings a brutal test on the road against Cincinnati. The risk profile centers on whether an ascending second-year receiver can shoulder an even heavier target burden in an offense that does not force an exceptionally high pass volume. If the vacated opportunities funnel cleanly to his side, the volume projection will hold firm. If the efficiency matches his late-season struggles, managers will experience considerable weekly volatility.

What to watch:
• Monitor how Emeka Egbuka handles the increased target share following departures from the wide receiver room.
• Watch his catch conversion rate after a stretch of low efficiency games to close out his rookie campaign.
• Track the pass rate over expected for Tampa Bay to see if the offense leans more heavily on the aerial attack this year.
• Evaluate his ability to beat top cornerbacks now that he enters the season as the designated WR1.

2026 outlook: Aaron Rodgers, QB, PIT

Aaron Rodgers enters his twenty-second NFL season firmly entrenched as the starter for Pittsburgh, operating from a veteran archetype where pocket presence dictates everything. Last year across sixteen games, he commanded 96 percent of the snaps and averaged 31.12 opportunities per game, translating into 14.19 fantasy points a game. The projection for this season leans on stable usage in the same offense, expecting 32.23 pass attempts per game. Pittsburgh runs 57.4 plays per game with a pass rate over expected of -0.7, yielding a market-implied team points mark of 21.8 a game. Opportunity is steady, but the structural ceiling faces a real bottleneck.

Separating skill from scheme reveals a profile built on volume rather than dynamic dual-threat upside. Rodgers offers virtually nothing on the ground, averaging minimal rushing work and recording just 0.19 red zone opportunities per game last year. That lack of rushing floor and scarce goal-line involvement means his fantasy output relies heavily on passing efficiency and volume. Looking at recent games toward the end of last season, he showed a pulse with 21.5 fantasy points against Baltimore in week fourteen and 17.8 fantasy points in the rematch in week eighteen, sandwiching a disappointing 7.3-point outing against Cleveland. The passing volume was there, hitting 34, 27, 41, 39, and 47 pass attempts across his final five games, yet the lack of rushing scores caps weekly explosives.

Risk comes into focus with age and situational constraints. At 42.8 years old, the margin for physical regression is always present, and the team environment does not hyper-inflate quarterback value. While there is no vacated quarterback room work to absorb, a massive 47.1 percent of team targets are now vacant in the offense, which could reshuffle how the passing game functions around him. The upcoming schedule strength index sits at 0.976 against the position, pointing to a slightly tougher than average slate. Rodgers is best viewed as a matchup-based streamer whose high snap share and consistent pass attempt volume keep him on the radar, but the lack of rushing work and modest team scoring expectations prevent him from entering elite territory.

• Monitor how the 47 percent vacant team targets get distributed among new pass catchers.

text:
🚨 SOUTH KOREA UNVEILS NATIONWIDE FREE AI ACCESS PLAN.

SEOUL, SOUTH KOREA - South Korea has announced an ambitious national program that will give all 52 million residents free access to generative AI services, making the country the first major economy to treat the technology as a public utility. The initiative, known as AI for All, will roll out later this year with beta testing scheduled for September and full deployment planned before the end of 2026.

Three major consortia led by SK Telecom, KT, and Kakao have been selected to operate the system. Their platforms will offer two tiers of service: a general-purpose chatbot for everyday use and a more advanced public-service agent capable of booking medical appointments, guiding tax filings, searching for housing, and helping small businesses navigate subsidies. Much of the access will run through KakaoTalk, the messaging app used by more than 45 million people in the country, along with phone calls, SMS, and web portals designed to support older and less tech-savvy users.

To power the nationwide rollout, the government is supplying 512 Nvidia B200 GPUs and will begin covering operational costs in 2027. Policy rules require that at least half of the AI stack run on domestically developed models, with foreign systems limited to a supporting role. Officials say the goal is to expand digital access, reduce reliance on foreign platforms, and strengthen the country’s technology sector.

The program arrives as roughly a quarter of South Koreans already pay for AI services, and it aims to make advanced tools available to everyone regardless of income or location.

# Header

A full-viewport, video-backed hero header for the **KittyPaw** pet-care brand, featuring a looping muted background video, a staggered word-by-word animated headline, a glassmorphic menu, and a signature rotating circular-text custom cursor that follows the mouse.

## Tech stack
- React (client component, "use client")
- framer-motion (motion, AnimatePresence, useMotionValue, useSpring)
- lucide-react (Menu, X icons)
- Tailwind CSS for all layout/styling

## Fonts & global styles
- Import Google Fonts via <link>: `https://t.co/gHbQUIeCQB`
- Two scoped utility classes: `.font-gabarito { font-family: 'Gabarito', sans-serif; }` and `.font-braah { font-family: 'Braah One', sans-serif; }`
- Braah One (weight 400) is used for the display headline and the metric number. Gabarito is used for all body/UI text (menu, subheading, button label, description, cursor text).
- Scope fonts to this section only — do not set a global body font.

## Section container
- Outer wrapper: `position: relative; width: 100vw; height: 100vh; overflow: hidden`, `display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: space-between`, `cursor: pointer; user-select: none`, background color `#000` (black).
- Clicking anywhere on the background (except buttons, links, or the menu dropdown) resumes/continues video playback.

## Structure, section by section
1. **Background video** — absolutely positioned `inset-0`, `w-full h-full object-cover`, `z-0`, `opacity: 1`. Source: `https://t.co/xjEc1H3chK`. Muted, playsInline, autoPlay, preload="auto". It loops only after the user clicks; before that, it auto-restarts at the 5-second mark via a timeupdate listener. A first-user-gesture fallback (click/touchstart) forces play if autoplay is blocked.
2. **Top navigation** (`z-10`, padding `px-4 md:px-12 xl:px-[64px] pt-4 md:pt-[20px] xl:pt-[22px]`): flex row, space-between.
   - Left: logo image `https://t.co/598IiECQIu`, height `26px` mobile / `36px` md / `40px` xl, `w-auto object-contain`.
   - Right: a pill "Menu" button — `rounded-full border border-white/60 bg-white/10 hover:bg-white/20`, `active:scale-95`, white text, containing the lucide `Menu` icon (`16px` → `20px` md → `22px` xl, stroke width 1.5) and the label "Menu" in Gabarito (`text-sm md:text-lg xl:text-[22px]`, `tracking-[-1px]`).
3. **Desktop dropdown** (md and up) — anchored top-right of the button, `mt-3 w-64 bg-white/10 backdrop-blur-xl border border-white/20 rounded-2xl p-4 shadow-2xl z-50`. Lists menu items as anchors in Gabarito, `text-white/90 hover:text-white`, `hover:bg-white/10 rounded-lg px-3 py-2`.
4. **Mobile drawer** (below md) — a fixed full-screen right-slide panel: `fixed inset-0 bg-black/60 backdrop-blur-2xl z-50`, `flex flex-col justify-between py-10 px-8`. Top row: logo (26px) + close button (lucide `X`, `w-6 h-6`, `p-2 bg-white/10 rounded-full`). Center: menu links in Gabarito `text-2xl font-medium text-white/90`. Footer: `text-xs text-white/40 font-mono` reading "© {currentYear} KittyPaw Inc. All rights reserved."
   - Menu items (both menus): "Home", "Premium Products", "Cat Grooming", "Wellness & Health", "Vet Programs", "Contact Us", all href "#".
5. **Hero main** (`flex-1 flex flex-col justify-center z-10`, same horizontal padding, `pt-12 md:pt-16`): a left-aligned text block, `max-w-full lg:w-[48.75vw]`, `gap-4 md:gap-[12px]`.
   - **Headline** in Braah One, white, `text-left`, `text-shadow: 2px 5px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.40)`. Responsive fluid sizing: `font-size: clamp(2.5rem, 6.875vw, 110px)`, `line-height: clamp(3rem, 7.5vw, 120px)`, `letter-spacing: clamp(-2px, -0.375vw, -6px)`, weight 400. Words "Everything", "Your", "Cats", "Love" split into two flex-wrap rows (first two words, then last two), `gap-x-4 md:gap-x-6`, each word an inline-block animated span.
   - **Subheading** in Gabarito, `text-white/90`, `text-sm md:text-lg xl:text-[22px]`, `leading-[1.56] tracking-[-1px]`, `max-w-[280px] sm:max-w-[420px] md:max-w-[504px]`: "Playful Pet Care offers trusted wellness, grooming, and vet-backed health programs so your furry life."
6. **Bottom row** (`z-10`, `flex flex-col sm:flex-row justify-between items-start sm:items-end`, `gap-6 sm:gap-4`, same horizontal padding, `pb-6 md:pb-[32px] xl:pb-[48px]`):
   - **Left CTA button** — `bg-white text-black rounded-full shadow-lg`, `px-6 py-3 md:px-6 xl:py-[14px] xl:px-[26px]`, Gabarito `text-base md:text-xl xl:text-[24px] font-semibold tracking-[-0.6px]`, `hover:bg-neutral-100 active:scale-95`. Label "Explore Products" is split into individual animated characters, followed by an arrow image `https://t.co/eqP29SEaWF` (`w-[16px] h-[15px]` → `18x17` md → `21x20` xl).
   - **Right trusted group** — three overlapping circular avatars (`-space-x-2.5 md:-space-x-3.5 xl:-space-x-[16px]`), each `w-10 h-10 md:w-12 md:h-12 xl:w-[64px] xl:h-[64px] rounded-full border-[1.5px] border-white object-cover bg-neutral-300`. Sources: `avater%201.png`, `avater%202.png`, `avater%203.png` under `https://t.co/RBhCxM7bnu`. Next to them a stacked metric: number "648+" in Braah One (`font-size: clamp(1.5rem, 2vw, 32px)`, `letter-spacing: clamp(-1px, -0.12vw, -1.905px)`, weight 400, white) above description "People & Pets love shopping here" in Gabarito (`text-[10px] md:text-xs xl:text-[20px] text-white/90 tracking-[-0.5px] xl:tracking-[-1px]`).
7. **Custom cursor** (lg and up only) — a fixed `z-[999]` pointer-following element, centered on the mouse via translate -50%. Contains a continuously rotating 80×80 SVG with circular-path text "Touch to Continue • Walk Cat •" in Gabarito 12px white on a circle radius 28 centered at (40,40), plus a 3px white center dot with glow `shadow-[0_0_8px_rgba(255,255,255,0.8)]`. It fades/scales out when hovering interactive elements (button, a, input, select, textarea, [role=button]) or when the mouse leaves the window.

## Assets — every URL
- Video: `https://t.co/xjEc1H3chK`
- Logo SVG (nav + drawer): `https://t.co/598IiECQIu`
- Arrow SVG: `https://t.co/eqP29SEaWF`
- Avatar 1: `https://t.co/z7GhQ9wjom`
- Avatar 2: `https://t.co/CpbndvgdKY`
- Avatar 3: `https://t.co/PRlHNroaBg`

## Animations
- **Nav header**: fades/slides down `y:-40 → 0`, `duration 1.4`, `ease cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`.
- **Headline stagger**: container variants stagger children by `0.18s` with `delayChildren: 0.8`. Each word: `hidden { opacity:0, x:-50 } → visible { opacity:1, x:0 }` with `type: spring, stiffness 70, damping 12`.
- **Subheading**: `opacity:0, y:15 → opacity:1, y:0`, `delay 1.8, duration 1, ease easeOut`.
- **Bottom row**: `opacity:0, y:40 → 0`, `delay 2.2, duration 1.2, ease cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`.
- **CTA char hover** (whileHover on the button drives each char via variants):
```js
const charVariants = {
  initial: { y: 0, x: 0, scale: 1 },
  hover: (i) => ({
    y: [0, -8, 4, 0],
    x: [0, 4, -2, 0],
    scale: [1, 1.15, 0.95, 1],
    transition: { duration: 0.6, ease: "easeInOut", delay: i * 0.03 },
  }),
};
```
- **Arrow hover**: `x: 0 → 6`, spring stiffness 300 damping 12.
- **Desktop dropdown**: `opacity 0, scale 0.92, y 10 → opacity 1, scale 1, y 0`, spring stiffness 380 damping 26.
- **Mobile drawer**: slides from `x: 100% → 0`, spring damping 30 stiffness 300; each drawer link fades in `x:20 → 0` with `delay: idx * 0.1`.
- **Cursor rotation**: `rotate: 360`, `repeat: Infinity, duration 12, ease linear`.
- **Cursor spring follow**: useSpring on x/y with `{ damping: 28, stiffness: 280, mass: 0.4 }`; opacity/scale toggle with `duration 0.15`.
- **Video restart logic**: while not yet clicked, restart video to 0 whenever currentTime ≥ 5.

## Responsive behavior
- **Desktop dropdown** shows at `md` and up (`hidden md:block`); **mobile drawer** shows below `md` (`md:hidden`).
- **Custom cursor** only renders at `lg` and up (`hidden lg:block`).
- Padding scales `px-4 → md:px-12 → xl:px-[64px]`; headline and metric number use fluid `clamp()` sizing; bottom row stacks vertically on mobile (`flex-col`) and becomes a space-between row at `sm` (`sm:flex-row items-end`).

## Key design principles
- Dark, immersive full-viewport hero with white typography over a looping video.
- Braah One for display, Gabarito for everything else — keep this pairing.
- Signature interaction is the rotating circular-text cursor with a tiny glowing dot.
- Entrance choreography is deliberately delayed and staggered (nav → headline → subheading → bottom row).
- Glassmorphism (backdrop-blur, translucent white) for menu surfaces.

## Common mistakes to avoid
- Do not set a global body font or global resets — scope fonts to this section.
- Keep the video muted + playsInline (required for mobile autoplay) and do not enable native loop until after first click.
- Do not use backtick template literals in the code output — use string concatenation.
- Render the custom cursor only on large screens; hide it over interactive elements.
- Preserve exact clamp() values for the headline and metric number.

## Page title
KittyPaw — Everything Your Cats Love

## Integration (build-safety — do not skip)
- Add this section as a **new** component file with a unique name. Don't edit or overwrite any existing file except to add its import and render it.
- Render it **after** all existing sections; keep every previously built section exactly as-is — never replace or remove them.
- If no project exists, create a minimal React + Tailwind app; if one exists, use it as-is — don't re-scaffold or change the Tailwind/build config or version.
- Keep it self-contained: scope its fonts and any resets to this section; never set global `body`/`html`/`*` styles or a global font.
- Install only the libraries this section names.

Value investing icon Seth Klarman's Baupost Group increased its stake in Alphabet (GOOG) by 16.15% during the second quarter of 2026. The fund added over 190,000 shares, bringing its total position to 1.37 million shares. This move raised the tech giant's weight in Baupost's public equity portfolio to 8.95%, making it one of the firm's largest holdings. The transaction was one of several significant additions Baupost made during the quarter, including a notable increase in its Amazon position.

This trade was disclosed in a quarterly 13F filing on August 13, 2026, which reveals positions held as of June 30. Such filings offer a delayed glimpse into a fund's activity. Klarman, known for a disciplined value approach, has actively traded the stock, having increased the position in the first quarter of 2026 as well. The continued investment comes as Alphabet ramps up capital expenditures for its AI and cloud infrastructure.

Vatican II and the Spanish Crown still offer the people a memory that the state discarded. 

Government, bureaucracy, and a captured elite insulated themselves from EU  policy failures. They live high above the poor, gated, guarded, 24/7/365, while Ceuta absorbs the chaos & crime.

Representative government was always a very thin bargain in Spain: communists in the ’20s and ’30s, Franco’s corproatism until the ’70s, then a bloated welfare settlement. It produced certain luxury beliefs: champagne socialists, swarming tech bros, haughty EU technocrats; plus cheap North African labor and labyrinthin papers that carved up Spanish sovereignty. 
All of it puffed up. 
All of it forgetting its rotten underbelly, the fine print of their treaties, their koran, and the hadiths. 

No century had NGOs like this to launder the lies and contradictions. 

You can’t flirt with the 7th century and the 21st without acknowledging the 14th and 15th in between.

To get you an idea of how crazy the tech industry was before 2020, I’ll tell you how I got my first internship working at Deloitte as a CS student at Carleton University

I attended Hack the North in 2018, I literally had a 30 min chat with a tech partner at the firm, we vibed, he liked that I played music 

He told me I’d get a “golden ticket” which meant you just skipped the entire recruiting cycle straight to the final interview in person at their headquarters in Toronto

Take that in, companies had entire hackathon recruiting teams.

I did the final interview over the phone about a month later, we chatted about what I was interested in, I told the interviewer I knew my react and JavaScript well etc 

And two days letter I got an offer.

1. Executive Summary: Breaking the Structural Stagnation
Recent economic evaluations—notably backed by the Fraser Institute and data from the Bank of Canada—paint a critical picture of Canada’s long-term prosperity. Between 1999 and 2025, U.S. labor productivity expanded by 67.9%, whereas Canadian productivity lagged at a modest 26.7%. As a consequence, Canada’s real per capita GDP (~$59,500 CAD) trails the United States (~$83,200 CAD) by an expanding gap exceeding $23,700 CAD.
This productivity deficit stems from a structural dependency on raw resource exports and low-margin assembly, alongside chronic underinvestment in capital-intensive, high-intellectual-property (IP) technologies. The deployment and Canadian-centric industrialization of the PANGEA-G™ Platform—driven by the GÜRŞEN-H™ Multi-Sector Propulsion & Energy Architecture—offers a structural cure. Rather than acting as a single component supplier, the PANGEA-G platform serves as a unified engineering ecosystem designed to capture high-margin market share across 18 core industrial verticals.

A common misconception in market analysis is evaluating technology platforms purely by the component-level "electric motor market" (roughly $135 Billion globally). In reality, across the 18 target verticals—spanning Aerospace, Defense, Heavy Industry, Maritime, Rail, Infrastructure, and High-Density AI Data Centers—the aggregate global output ranges between $3.0 Trillion and $5.0 Trillion USD annually.
Across these capital-intensive industries, the complete power, propulsion, drive, and regenerative energy management system accounts for approximately 30% to 40% of total equipment value. By establishing Canada as the primary manufacturing, licensing, and engineering hub for the PANGEA-G ecosystem, capturing a 10% global market share translates directly to a targeted $130 Billion to $140 Billion USD in annual high-margin revenues within a 5-year operational horizon.

Rare earth minerals - 
Is Malaysia an alternative to China as supply source?

Nikkei Asia says Malaysia's rare earth reserves are attracting increased interest from foreign investors as Japan and Western countries scramble to diversify supply from China before Beijing starts enforcing tough export restrictions on critical minerals this fall.

Rare earth materials are essential for high-tech manufacturing, including electric vehicles, semiconductors and missiles.

China controls around 90% of global rare earths refining and 94% of permanent magnet production. 

Malaysia has 16.1 million metric tons of rare earth deposits, according to government estimates, but lacks the technology to mine and process them itself.

I) Malaysian Perspective...

Key person interviewed for the Nikkei story is Lim Wei Chung, executive director and chief operating officer of Southern Alliance Mining, told Nikkei Asia.

Southern Alliance's unit, MCRE, obtained a license for mining in 2022.

Southern Alliance holds a 40% stake in MCRE Resources, the sole rare earth mining company in Malaysia, which exports all of its raw rare earths to China to be refined. 

In January 2024, Malaysia banned exports of unprocessed rare earths in an effort to develop the industry's downstream activities and investments in domestic processing.

With the increasing interest in the country's rare earths, the Malaysian government is now mulling lifting the country's ban on raw rare earth exports... a thought that first surfaced in early August.

II) Japanese financiers...

Meanwhile, Japan's ambassador Noriyuki Shikata told Nikkei Asia that Japanese entities have "actively supported" rare earth operations in Malaysia, notably investing in facilities handling imported mineral concentrates.

Japan's offer package includes strategic financing, including loans and equity investments involving Japanese institutional and private stakeholders such as JOGMEC (Japan Organization for Metals and Energy Security) and corporate partners like Sojitz.

Sojitz and JOGMEC had provided US$250 million in financing in the form of a loan and equity stake in 2011 to Lynas when it first built its refinery.

III) Caveat...

1) Domestically, Malaysia's rare earths industry faces a major challenge, that is the fragmented regulatory landscape between federal and state governments.

So said Tricia Yeoh, visiting senior fellow in the Malaysia Studies Programme of the Singapore-based ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute.

2) Malaysia should first focus on improving geological data and building government and public support in order to attract more interest from international mining companies.

"Next is creating policy bi-partisanship on minerals to offer investors long-term policy certainty. This is particularly important given it can take a decade or more to open a new mine."

So said Hayley Channer, director of the Economic Security Program at the United States Studies Centre, University of Sydney.

https://t.co/aOFmLLi9n9

So, Malaysia, are you ready to stand in the shadows of China for more than the duration of two Prime Ministers?

text:
Says a man, true she murdered those children. No woman is prosecuted as a murderer who gets an abortion. Those babies are humans too. A murder without any outcome that benefits the murderer, that only destroys her life, why would a sane person do that? If she hated all three of her children, why not stage an accidental death of some kind, why not at least try to get away with it? She didn’t even try. Here are the facts: The core physical facts of January 24, 2023, are not disputed by either side.
What happened
Clancy sent her husband out of the house to pick up takeout and a pharmacy errand. While he was gone she took the three children—Cora (5), Dawson (3), and Callan (8 months)—into the basement of their Duxbury home and strangled each of them with exercise/resistance bands. She then went upstairs, cut her wrists and neck, ingested crushed medication, and jumped from a second-story window in a suicide attempt. She survived but was left paralyzed from the waist down. The two older children were pronounced dead that night; the infant died days later. 
Did she try to conceal that she strangled them?
She did not hide the bodies, remove the bands, or invent a cover story that someone else or an accident was responsible. When her husband returned and found her injured on the lawn, she told him she had tried to kill herself and that the children were “in the basement.” She did not tell him they were dead or injured. He discovered them himself, still with the bands around their necks, while he was on the 911 call. Prosecutors have argued that sending him on a longer errand, choosing the basement, and withholding the fact that the children were dead show planning and awareness rather than a sudden break. The defense does not contest that she performed the acts. 
Did she try to blame someone else?
No. She has never claimed an intruder, her husband, or any other person committed the killings. Online speculation later blamed the husband; that did not come from her. She has consistently described the acts as her own. 
Did she confess and offer a reason?
Yes. She has not denied killing the children. The legal fight is over criminal responsibility (insanity / lack of criminal responsibility under Massachusetts law), not whether she did it.
The reason she and her defense have given is that she was in the grip of severe postpartum mental illness (they argue psychosis, with bipolar features worsened by medication). She has said she heard a male voice telling her it was her last chance and that she had to kill the children so she could then kill herself. Some later statements to clinicians and a chaplain included that she believed the children would be “safe.” She had been seeking psychiatric care, including a hospital stay, in the months beforehand. Prosecutors counter that her actions that day (including a pediatric appointment, building a snowman, sending photos, and arranging the errand) and the methodical nature of the three separate strangulations show she understood what she was doing. 
These are the facts presented at trial. The jury has not yet returned a verdict on whether she is criminally responsible.

text:
🧲🇬🇧 The metallurgist who turned Belfast's recycled oxides into Ford-tested magnets just got promoted, and $IXR holders should know his name.

Manu Kaimanikal, Ph.D. has stepped up to Director, Research & Development at Less Common Metals (LCM), the Cheshire rare-earth metals house owned by USA Rare Earth. 

Why does a promotion in England matter to an ASX small cap? Because Manu has been Ionic Technologies' hands-on metallisation partner on almost every project that proved the Belfast recycling flowsheet works. 🧵👇

🔬 The project that made the case

CLIMATES — completed May 2026, led by Ionic Technologies with LCM, GKN and Ford UK. The first Western supply chain to take spent magnets all the way back to a working e-motor:
https://t.co/J9P13YjhUM

♻️ ⚗️Ionic Technologies (Belfast) recycled 100% scrap magnet/alloy into separated oxides: Nd₂O₃ 99.87% (120 kg), Dy₂O₃ 99.56% (10 kg), Tb₄O₇ 99.75% (8 kg)

⚗🔥 LCM, Manu's team, reduced those oxides to metal and strip-cast magnet-spec alloy. Microstructure identical to alloy made from mined feedstock

🧲 GKN made finished NdFeB magnets at Radevormwald, Germany — recycled material "behaved in the same way as flakes made from mined material"

🚗 Ford built two rotors at Halewood and dyno-tested at Dunton. The rotor passed a durability test cycle with results equivalent to production magnets

🗣️ Ford's Dennis Witt: recycled magnets "meet our rigorous commercial standards on the first attempt"

https://t.co/a6wEYzo0I0

🛠️ Not a one-off

🔁 REEVALUATE, Ionic Technologies + LCM + Vacuumschmelze + Innovate UK: rare-earth alloy for magnet manufacturing from 100% recycled REEs. Manu was in the Belfast demo plant for the first review meeting.

🏗️🧲 https://t.co/jSuVSbkdDb

🏗️🧲 https://t.co/O80gsGBQzI

🇬🇧 CirculaREEconomy — £11M, APC UK / DRIVE35-backed three-year programme to 2028, led by Ionic Technologies with LCM, Ford, Bentley, Wrightbus, EMR and the British Geological Survey. Manu's words: 

"transforming high-purity recycled rare earth oxides into advanced alloy systems… high-specification magnets that meet the rigorous performance demands of the electric vehicle sector"
https://t.co/jSuVSbkdDb

🤝 The Australian High Commission attended the CLIMATES Impact Celebration in London, co-hosted by Ionic Technologies and LCM, and noted LCM is "one of the few significant producers of separated rare earths outside China"

💡 Why this matters for IXR

🔥 LCM has been commercially producing Nd, NdPr, Dy and Tb metal via molten-salt electrolysis and metallothermic reduction since 2017. It's the only Western metalliser that has repeatedly taken Ionic's recycled oxides through to alloy and proven them at OEM standard. The person who ran that metallurgy now sets R&D direction at the metals arm of a Nasdaq-listed US magnet maker building 1,200 tpa at Stillwater, Oklahoma.

Ionic's Belfast plant has a £12M UK Government capital grant offer in principle for a 400 tpa commercial recycling facility, and Ionic Technologies' recycled oxides now have a validated path all the way to a Ford rotor. The oxide-to-metal-to-magnet plumbing is built. Remaining piece: FID on the £85M Belfast plant.

⚠️ The caveats

🧪 CLIMATES was a demonstration. Ford itself called it "a testing project rather than mass production"

💷 Every project above is grant-supported; no commercial offtake between Ionic and LCM/USAR has been disclosed

🏗️ Belfast commercial plant still needs the remaining equity for FID

Watching this because supply chains are built by people, not press releases, and the metallurgist who has personally proven Belfast's recycled oxides can make Ford-grade magnets is now directing R&D at a US-owned metals producer. Congratulations, Manu. 👏

text:
People vote with their feet when governments fail, and South Africa's internal migration numbers make that truth impossible to ignore. Between 2011 and 2026, the Western Cape absorbed more than 1 million net migrants from other provinces, most of them skilled workers, small business owners, and professionals who calculated that Johannesburg or the Eastern Cape offered declining returns on their productive effort.

This is capital theory made flesh. Human capital, like financial capital, flows toward environments that protect it. The Western Cape's Democratic Alliance-administered municipalities consistently outperform ANC-governed counterparts on basic service delivery, infrastructure maintenance, and business licensing speed.

Property rights, functional courts, and competent municipal management are the preconditions for everything else. Strip them away and the productive class relocates. The remaining tax base shrinks. Services deteriorate faster. The cycle accelerates.

You feel this directly if you owned property in Sandton five years ago and watch its value stagnate while Atlantic Seaboard prices skyrocket. Markets are pricing governance quality in real time.

The province resisting cadre deployment most aggressively attracts the private investment and skilled labor that generate actual tax revenue. Competence compounds. The Western Cape is becoming prosperous because limited government interference allows it to function competently.

The socialist ANC government turns everything they touch into shit within years, and can be more accurately described as a wealth extraction movement than a political party. Where they govern, every productive actor who retains the ability to leave, leaves, creating a wasteland in their wake. 

In November 2026, local government elections will take place across the country. Sadly, most South Africans have been kept poor, uneducated and dependent on government grants by the ANC, and will keep voting for corruption, poverty and decline.

ಬೆಳ್ತಂಗಡಿ, ಸೆ. ೨: ಸರ್ಕಾರಿ ಬಸ್‌ಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಮಹಿಳೆಯರಿಗೆ ಹಾಗೂ ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿಗಳಿಗೆ ಉಚಿತ ಪ್ರಯಾಣದ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆ ಅನುಕೂಲಕರವಾಗಿದ್ದರೂ, ಅಗತ್ಯಕ್ಕೆ ತಕ್ಕಷ್ಟು ಬಸ್‌ಗಳಿಲ್ಲದೆ ಜನರು ಜೀವ ಕೈಯಲ್ಲಿ ಹಿಡಿದು ಪ್ರಯಾಣಿಸಬೇಕಾದ ಸ್ಥಿತಿ ನಿರ್ಮಾಣವಾಗಿದೆ. ಅದರಲ್ಲೂ ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿಗಳು ಫುಟ್‌ಬೋರ್ಡ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ನೇತಾಡಿಕೊಂಡು ಹೋಗುವ ದೃಶ್ಯ ಆತಂಕ ಮೂಡಿಸುತ್ತಿದೆ.
ನೆರಿಯ, ಚಾರ್ಮಾಡಿ, ದಿಡುಪೆ, ಗಂಡಿಬಾಗಿಲು ಕಡೆಯಿಂದ ಬೆಳಗ್ಗೆ ಶಾಲೆ-ಕಾಲೇಜು ಹಾಗೂ ಕಚೇರಿಗಳಿಗೆ ತೆರಳುವ ಸಾವಿರಾರು ಮಂದಿ ಇದ್ದಾರೆ. ಸಂಜೆ ಮರಳುವವರೂ ಸಹ ಅಪಾರ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯಲ್ಲಿದ್ದಾರೆ. ಆದರೆ ಬೆಳಗಿನ ಹಾಗೂ ಸಂಜೆಯ ಅವಧಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸಾಕಷ್ಟು ಬಸ್‌ಗಳಿಲ್ಲದೆ ಜನರು ಕಿಕ್ಕಿರಿದು ತುಂಬಿದ ಬಸ್‌ಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ನುಗ್ಗಿಕೊಂಡು, ನೇತಾಡುತ್ತಲೇ ಸಾಗಬೇಕಾದ ಅನಿವಾರ್ಯತೆಯಿದೆ.

ನೆರಿಯ, ಕನ್ಯಾತ್ಕಾಡಿ, ಗಂಡಿಬಾಗಿಲು, ದೇವಗಿರಿ, ಕೊಯ್ಯೂರು, ಬೈಪಾಡಿ, ಬೆಳಾಲು, ದಿಡುಪೆ ಸೇರಿದಂತೆ ತಾಲೂಕಿನ ಹಲವು ಗ್ರಾಮೀಣ ಭಾಗಗಳಿಗೆ ಕೆಎಸ್‌ಆರ್‌ಟಿಸಿ ಬಸ್‌ಗಳೇ ಪ್ರಮುಖ ಸಾರಿಗೆ ಸಂಪರ್ಕ. ಹೀಗಾಗಿ ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿಗಳು, ಉದ್ಯೋಗಿಗಳು ಹಾಗೂ ಸಾರ್ವಜನಿಕರು ಈ ಕೆಂಪು ಬಸ್‌ಗಳನ್ನೇ ಅವಲಂಬಿಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ.

ಬೆಳಗ್ಗೆ ಬೆಳ್ತಂಗಡಿ ಕಡೆಗೆ ಸೀಮಿತ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯ ಬಸ್‌ಗಳಿರುವುದರಿಂದ, ಒಂದು ಬಸ್ ತಪ್ಪಿದರೆ ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿಗಳು ಶಾಲೆ-ಕಾಲೇಜುಗಳಿಗೆ ತಡವಾಗಿ ತಲುಪುವಂತಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಸಂಜೆ ವೇಳೆ ಶಾಲೆಗಳು ಬಿಡುವ ಸಂದರ್ಭದಲ್ಲೂ ಹೆಚ್ಚುವರಿ ಬಸ್‌ಗಳಿಲ್ಲದೆ, ನೂರಾರು ಪ್ರಯಾಣಿಕರು ಒಂದೇ ಬಸ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ನೂಕುನುಗ್ಗಲಿನಲ್ಲಿ ತೆರಳಬೇಕಾಗಿದೆ.

ಸಂಜೆ ವೇಳೆಯ ಪರದಾಟ

ನೆರಿಯ ಭಾಗಕ್ಕೆ ಸಂಜೆ 5:10ಕ್ಕೆ ಒಂದು ಬಸ್ ಹೊರಟರೆ, ಮುಂದಿನ ಬಸ್ ಇರುವುದು 6:45ಕ್ಕೆ. ಮೊದಲ ಬಸ್ ತಕ್ಷಣವೇ ಕಿಕ್ಕಿರಿದು ತುಂಬುತ್ತದೆ; ಅದು ತಪ್ಪಿದರೆ ಮನೆ ತಲುಪುವುದು ರಾತ್ರಿಯಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

ಕಿಲ್ಲೂರು, ಬಂಗಾಡಿ, ಕೊಳ್ಳಿ ಭಾಗಗಳಿಗೆ ಸಂಜೆ 5:15ರ ಬಳಿಕ ಯಾವುದೇ ಕೆಎಸ್‌ಆರ್‌ಟಿಸಿ ಬಸ್ ಸೌಲಭ್ಯವಿಲ್ಲ.

ಬೈಲಡ್ಕ, ಸವಣಾಲು, ಶಿರ್ಲಾಲು ಭಾಗಗಳಿಗೆ ಕೊನೆಯ ಬಸ್ ಸಂಜೆ 5:00 ಗಂಟೆಗೇ ಹೊರಟುಬಿಡುತ್ತದೆ.

ದಿಡುಪೆ ಭಾಗಕ್ಕೆ ಸಂಜೆ 5:30 ಮತ್ತು 6:45ಕ್ಕೆ ಕೊನೆಯ ಬಸ್‌ಗಳಿರುತ್ತವೆ. ಇದು ಶಾಲೆ-ಕಾಲೇಜು ಬಿಡುವ ಸಮಯವಾಗಿರುವುದರಿಂದ ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿಗಳು ಹಾಗೂ ಇತರ ಪ್ರಯಾಣಿಕರು ತೀವ್ರ ಜನದಟ್ಟಣೆಯಿರುವ ಅದೇ ಬಸ್ಸನ್ನೇ ಅವಲಂಬಿಸಬೇಕಾಗಿದೆ.

ಆಯತಪ್ಪಿ ಬಿದ್ದರೆ ಜೀವಕ್ಕೆ ಅಪಾಯ

ಬಸ್‌ನೊಳಗೆ ಸ್ಥಳವಿಲ್ಲದ ಕಾರಣ ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿಗಳು ಅನಿವಾರ್ಯವಾಗಿ ಬಾಗಿಲ ಬಳಿ ನಿಂತುಕೊಂಡು ಅಥವಾ ಹೊರಗಿನ ಫುಟ್‌ಬೋರ್ಡ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ನೇತಾಡಿಕೊಂಡು ಪ್ರಯಾಣಿಸುವುದು ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯವಾಗಿದೆ. ಮಳೆಗಾಲದಲ್ಲಿ ರಸ್ತೆಗಳು ಜಾರುವಂತಿರುವಾಗ ಈ ಅಪಾಯ ಮತ್ತಷ್ಟು ಹೆಚ್ಚಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಈ ಹಿಂದೆ ಬೆಳ್ತಂಗಡಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಬಸ್‌ನ ಫುಟ್‌ಬೋರ್ಡ್‌ನಿಂದ ರಸ್ತೆಗೆ ಎಸೆಯಲ್ಪಟ್ಟು ಅಕ್ಕ-ತಂಗಿ ಗಾಯಗೊಂಡ ಘಟನೆ ನಡೆದಿತ್ತು. ಹೀಗಾಗಿ ಮಕ್ಕಳು ಸುರಕ್ಷಿತವಾಗಿ ಮನೆಗೆ ಮರಳುವವರೆಗೂ ಪೋಷಕರು ಆತಂಕದಲ್ಲೇ ಕಾಲ ಕಳೆಯುವಂತಾಗಿದೆ.
"ಬಂದು ಕಣ್ಣಾರೆ ನೋಡಿ...""ಕೆ ಎಸ್‌ಆರ್‌ಟಿಸಿ ಅಧಿಕಾರಿಗಳು ತಾಲೂಕಿನ ಗ್ರಾಮೀಣ ಭಾಗಗಳ ವಾಸ್ತವ ಪರಿಸ್ಥಿತಿಯನ್ನು ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿ, ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿಗಳು ಹಾಗೂ ಸಾರ್ವಜನಿಕರ ಸುರಕ್ಷಿತ ಪ್ರಯಾಣಕ್ಕಾಗಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚುವರಿ ಬಸ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಆರಂಭಿಸಬೇಕು."— ವಂದಿತಾ, ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿನಿ
"ಜೀವಕ್ಕೆ ಬೆಲೆ ಕಟ್ಟಲಾಗದು""ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿಗಳ ಜೀವಕ್ಕೆ ಬೆಲೆ ಕಟ್ಟಲು ಸಾಧ್ಯವಿಲ್ಲ. ದುರಂತ ಸಂಭವಿಸುವ ಮುನ್ನವೇ ಅಧಿಕಾರಿಗಳು ಎಚ್ಚೆತ್ತುಕೊಳ್ಳಬೇಕು. ಗ್ರಾಮೀಣ ರಸ್ತೆಗಳ ಸ್ಥಿತಿ, ಬಸ್ ನಿಲ್ದಾಣಗಳು, ಶಾಲಾ ಮಾರ್ಗಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಸಾರ್ವಜನಿಕ ಸಾರಿಗೆ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆಯನ್ನು ಅಧಿಕಾರಿಗಳು ನಿಯಮಿತವಾಗಿ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಬೇಕಾದ ಅಗತ್ಯವಿದೆ."— ರಾಜೇಶ್ ಎಂ. ಕಾರ್ನಪ್, ಪ್ರಯಾಣಿಕರು
ಹೆಚ್ಚುವರಿ ಬಸ್‌ಗಳಿಗೆ ಆಗ್ರಹ
ಗ್ರಾಮೀಣ ಭಾಗಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರಯಾಣಿಕರ ದಟ್ಟಣೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿರುವ ಬೆಳಗ್ಗೆ ಹಾಗೂ ಸಂಜೆಯ ಅವಧಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚುವರಿ ಕೆಎಸ್‌ಆರ್‌ಟಿಸಿ ಬಸ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಓಡಿಸಬೇಕೆಂಬ ಆಗ್ರಹ ತೀವ್ರಗೊಂಡಿದೆ. ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿಗಳ ಸಂಚಾರ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿರುವ ಮಾರ್ಗಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ಟ್ರಿಪ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಒದಗಿಸಬೇಕು, ಸಂಜೆ ಕೊನೆಯ ಬಸ್‌ಗಳ ನಡುವಿನ ಅಂತರವನ್ನು ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡಬೇಕು ಹಾಗೂ ಗ್ರಾಮೀಣ ಜನತೆಯ ಅನುಕೂಲಕ್ಕೆ ತಕ್ಕಂತೆ ವೇಳಾಪಟ್ಟಿಯನ್ನು ಪುನಾರಚಿಸಬೇಕು ಎಂದು ಸಾರ್ವಜನಿಕರು ಒತ್ತಾಯಿಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ. Shortage of Government Buses: Students Forced to Travel Hanging from Footboards! A Daily Struggle for Residents of Neriya, Charmadi, and Didupe Regions
Belthangady, Sept 2: While free bus travel schemes for women and students offer convenience, an acute lack of adequate buses has forced passengers to travel risking their lives. Alarming scenes of students clinging to footboards and doors have sparked grave concern.

Thousands commute every morning and evening toward schools, colleges, and offices from areas such as Neriya, Charmadi, Didupe, and Gandibagilu. Due to the severe scarcity of buses during peak morning and evening hours, passengers are forced to squeeze into packed vehicles and travel suspended from footboards.

For rural reaches of the taluk—including Neriya, Kanyatadka, Gandibagilu, Devaragudde, Koyyur, Bayalu, Belalu, and Didupe—KSRTC buses serve as the lifeline. Consequently, students, office-goers, and general commuters depend heavily on these red buses.

Because morning buses toward Belthangady are limited, missing a single bus results in students arriving late to class. During evening dismissal hours, the lack of additional services forces hundreds of passengers to cram into single buses.

Evening Commuter Ordeal

For Neriya, a bus departs at 5:10 PM, with the subsequent service scheduled only at 6:45 PM. The first bus fills past capacity instantly; missing it means reaching home very late into the night.

For Killur, Bangadi, and Kolli, there are no KSRTC services available after 5:15 PM.

The final bus toward Byaladka, Savanalu, and Shirlalu leaves as early as 5:00 PM.

For the Didupe area, the last available services are at 5:30 PM and 6:45 PM. Because these coincide with school and college dispersal times, students and other passengers must rely on a single overcrowded bus.

Slight Slip, Fatal ConsequenceWith no room left inside, students inevitably stand at open doorways or hang from outer footboards. Slippery conditions during the monsoon multiply this hazard. A previous incident in Belthangady involved two sisters falling from a bus footboard onto the road and sustaining injuries. Parents remain anxious until their children return safely home each day.

"Come and See for Yourselves..." "KSRTC authorities must inspect ground reality across taluk rural routes and deploy extra buses to ensure safe travel for students and the general public."— Vanditha, Student
"A Life Cannot Be Priced" "You cannot put a price tag on a student’s life. Officials need to wake up before tragedy strikes. Authorities should conduct regular inspections of rural road conditions, bus stops, school routes, and the overall public transport system."— Rajesh M. Kanyarpu, Commuter

Demand for Additional Buses-Demands have mounted calling for KSRTC to run more buses during morning and evening rush hours across rural areas. Commuters have urged transport authorities to schedule extra trips along high-density student transit routes, reduce long time intervals between late evening services, and restructure timetables to align with rural community needs.

City warns Burnham of borrowing shock unless he slashes spending

Prime Minister urged to scrap state pensions triple lock after recent surge in bond yields

Andy Burnham has been hit with a warning from the City of London that he risks market turmoil unless he slashes spending.

Investors and economists said Britain would face a fresh surge in borrowing costs unless the Prime Minister outlined credible plans to rein in the size of the state.

Lord O’Neill, a former adviser to Mr Burnham, and Sir Charles Bean, a former official at the Office for Budget Responsibility, both called for the state pensions triple lock to be scrapped after a surge in bond yields in recent days.

Mohamed El-Erian, the former boss of bond giant Pimco, cautioned that Mr Burnham “cannot borrow his way out of this” and warned that Britain was increasingly vulnerable to recession.

Mr Burnham refused to rule out more borrowing on Wednesday during his first Prime Minister’s Questions (PMQs).

Britain has been hit particularly hard, amid growing concerns about Mr Burnham’s first Budget next month. The Prime Minister has made a series of expensive commitments on everything from defence to housing despite the parlous state of public finances.

Paying for these policies would require either tax rises, more borrowing or spending cuts elsewhere.

The cost of long-term government borrowing hit its highest level since 1998 on Wednesday. The 10-year gilt yield – a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money – at one point rose to its highest level since 2007.

Sir Charles Bean, who is also a former Bank of England deputy governor, said that Mr Burnham did not appear to grasp the gravity of the situation.

He said: “There is no real suggestion that he has really recognised the underlying challenges of the fiscal position, and even less articulated how he intends to deal with them.”

Sir Charles said Mr Burnham must begin “slaying some of the sacred cows”.

He said: “Now is a good time to say, look, the triple lock must go and be serious about doing something on some of the less efficient aspects of welfare spending.”

Lord O’Neill, a former minister and Goldman Sachs economist who turned down an offer to join Mr Burnham’s Government, said Mr Burnham must “get real” and cut public spending to win back market confidence.

He urged the Prime Minister to consider scrapping the state pensions triple lock or lowering “excessive” welfare spending.

The Government will be spending £407bn on welfare by the start of the next decade, up from £353bn this fiscal year

Mr El-Erian said that the drag on growth from the war in Iran and higher borrowing costs had left the UK “much more vulnerable to recession”.

He added that John Healey, the new Chancellor, had “virtually no headroom left” against the fiscal rules once higher borrowing costs, slowing growth and higher defence spending were factored in.

‘Lack of credibility’
Al Cattermole, a portfolio manager at Swiss private bank Mirabaud, said the City was “unclear” about the Prime Minister’s plans and how he would pay for them.

He warned that borrowing costs could jump sharply as they did in the wake of Ms Truss’s 2022 Budget if Mr Burnham did not put forward plans to either raise taxes or cut spending elsewhere to fund his ambitions.

Mr Cattermole said: “If you have a lack of credibility about your spending plan and how that will be funded, then you would get spikes in yields similar to [what] we saw during the Liz Truss episode.

“That was about unfunded fiscal spending. And if you get that again, then there is concern about that.”

Jim Athey, a portfolio manager at Marlborough Investment, said: “Spending cuts are the thing the market wants to hear.

“It would go a long way if this Government were to recognise that it is a challenge that needs addressing – that the path we are on in terms of welfare spending is completely unsustainable.”

He added: “The market knows that, and the market wants to hear that the Government understands that.”

Government finances are extremely sensitive to movements in market borrowing costs. The UK spends more than £100bn a year only to service the interest on its £3tn national debt mountain. This is equal to 94.1pc of GDP, debt levels last seen in the early 1960s.

On Wednesday, during PMQs, Mr Burnham said: “This will be a government grounded in fiscal responsibility. It will stick to the fiscal rules.

“But at the same time, we will help reduce cost of living pressure on our constituents.”

I don’t understand the deadlock with the jury; commonsense would dictate that a mother who kills her defenseless, innocent children who are too young to defend themselves; but doesn’t want to leave her children to grow up without her is a very selfish mother.
One thing is clear based on all the evidence the defense offered, she was never ‘medically’ or  ‘psychotically’ diagnosed with Schizophrenia which is a chronic and severe mental disorder that affects how a person thinks, feels, and behaves.
When mom first woke up in the ICU unit after her failed suicide attempt and spoke with her nurse, according to the ICU nurse, under oath, in Court her first words were ‘do I need a lawyer?’ – Mom did not ask: ‘what have I done? I don’t remember’ – or ‘why am I here’ or ‘how are my children?’  Why upon waking did this mom know she may need a lawyer?
It’s hard to believe that any mother would take systematic steps to murder their own children and fail to take her own life but wake up in the ICU with the question: “do I need a lawyer?” Can it be that somewhere in her mind and soul she knew she did something bad when she woke up? Otherwise, why would her first words be: ‘do I need a lawyer?’
While postpartum psychosis (meaning insanity after giving birth) is very rare; postpartum depression is indeed very common – even after a miscarriage – but does not cause a mom's sudden loss of touch with reality and justify murder.

text:
How does one learn to run better and faster in dreams? You know when someone is chasing you and you run with everything you have but your feet won't carry you and they keep getting closer until you wake up? 

I was running from two young women in my class in university and what was my crime? It was the final time the class was supposed to gather and my phone had a good camera so I offered to take the group picture. It was glorious on my phone. The sun was setting and showing off its orange glow and the trees looked like something out of a magazine. I did many angles and there were jokes being thrown at me from the large group. There were hundreds of people in my class and it was a feat just getting everyone together and arranging them so that they fit in one photo. 

I told them I would go home, work on the photos and send it to everyone. As the group broke apart, spreading out onto the lawn I checked to see what photos were best. I scrolled and swiped and restarted my phone. I checked all the folders. Nothing. I spent too much time wondering how this could have happened, that most of the people in the group left so I could not ask them to pose for another one. Two young women who wanted to just come over and see the photos, and probably ask me to send it to them directly, overheard me saying I did not have the photos. They were livid. Like water-dripping-into-hot oil livid. So I ran. Don't ask me why, but I did. I asked: ƙafa me na ci ban baka ba? Feet, have I ever eaten and not fed you? Both of them were quite short, the smallest in the class. I should have been able to get away easily, no? Wrong. It was as if I was running inside a bucket full of beach sand. I pushed every muscle I had and I was barely moving. 
So I decided to lay flat around a corner, just before a long outdoor stairway. They took the next corner which also led to the stairway. I tried to be still and breathe quietly. When the first one emerged she turned around but did not see me. They were speaking loudly about how they were going to hold me accountable for ruining that final moment and that now because of me they had no photo of all their course mates. The Danube offered a route for retreat, but the bottleneck of the Djerdap Gorge and the speed of the Red Army's advance forced the German command to make a desperate move. Rear Admiral Paul Cibb ordered the sinking of the fleet and blocking of the Danube in order to slow down the advance of the Red Army navy, but also to avoid a conflict with the Red Army land units that were advancing from the direction of Romania.

While 1 body has been recovered from the Yamuna River, rescue teams are working tirelessly around the clock to locate the 2nd.

🫡 Group Captain Abhinandan Varthaman, VrC, has taken retirement from the IAF after 22 years of glorious service. The veteran fighter pilot is highly distinguished for his actions during an aerial dogfight on February 27, 2019, where he pursued & shot down a Pakistani F-16 fighter jet before his own MiG-21 Bison was hit. He was later awarded the Vir Chakra, India's 3rd-highest wartime gallantry medal, for his exceptional bravery & courage under fire.

🇺🇸🇳🇵2 USAF aircraft deliver 5,000 recovery kits, first-aid packs & stretchers to support flood rescue works in Nepal, announces US Prez Trump's special envoy Gor.

🇵🇰 POJK Protests: Pakistani Army & Rangers are roaming in Rawalakot to suppress the protests. Multiple armoured Vehicles have reached the town.

🇮🇳💣 The 140 KM range, 12 KM altitude release 'Khagantak-243' Long-Range Glide Bomb (300 KG), jointly developed by JSR Dynamics & BEL was likely test launched from a IAF Su-30MKI fighter. The missile can hold a 125 KG warhead of Mk-81.

🇮🇳🛩️ Sources: India is now looking into the possibility of using currently unused or
underutilized airfields in the northern part of the country as backup operating bases for long-range unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) such as runway dependent long endurance & 1-way UAVs. It's believed the idea to establish new operating bases that would be able to supplement existing military air bases should let any conflict drag on. Instead of consolidating the use of UAS at a few large airfields, operating at multiple locations would offer increased protection against enemy attack as well as ensure that UAV units could operate if primary bases were damaged or out of service.

🇮🇳🇷🇺 Sources: India & Russia are taking forward a proposal to procure Pantsir-S1 that will act as a bodyguard to the S-400 system & its highly vulnerable components within an S-400 system. It has been said that Pantsir-S1 will act as inner layer for the S-400 since S-400 interceptors have a minimum engagement range & are inefficient & expensive to use against small, low-flying, or low-
RCS targets like small UAVs, loitering
munitions & cruise missiles as seen in Operation Sindoor when S-400 had to be launched to take out small drones from Pakistan, wasting millions over a few thousand dollar drones. Pantsir-S1 comes equipped with 12 short-range radio-guided missiles (range up to 20–30 KM) & dual 30mm automatic cannons that are effective up to 4 KM. Pantsir will also act as the physical bodyguard for the S-400's radar installations &
command posts.

🇮🇳🚀 Indian Navy has shown interest in funding to co-develop an air launched rocket assisted torpedo, a compact & stealthy anti-submarine weapon designed for operations from unmanned aircraft & manned fighter jets. While the concept is not new, the weapon is to be used for anti-submarine operations that could be a game-changer for the Indian Ocean Region (IOR). As the name suggests, it will be a torpedo equipped with a range-extension kit designed to convert a conventional torpedo into an air-launched, rocket-assisted weapon. Powered by a small turbojet, the kit
will allow launch aircraft to release the torpedo from stand-off ranges, after which it will glide for 150-250 KM before jettisoning the kit & diving into the ocean. The air-launched, rocket-assisted torpedo will then approach & strike underwater targets with an extremely low detection profile.
