FAKE NEWS WEEK: A Guide to Mainstream Media ‘Fake News’ War Propaganda
FEBRUARY 14, 2017 BY 21WIRE 8 COMMENTS

 In response to the establishment media’s contrived ‘fake news’ crisis designed to marginalise independent and alternative media sources of news and analysis, 21WIRE is running its own #FakeNewsWeek campaign, where each day our editorial team at 21st Century Wire will feature media critiques and analysis of mainstream corporate media coverage of current events – exposing the government and the mainstream media as the real purveyors of ‘fake news’ throughout modern history…
Patrick Henningsen
21st Century Wire
As mainstream media pundits, government officials and Silicon Valley technocrats continue the alarmist crusade over the perceived scourge of ‘fake news’ circulating on social media, their misplaced obsession belies the fact that the government-media complex has long been waging its own private disinformation war, against the global public.
As the establishment continues its attempt to discredit alternative sources of information through its fake news faux crisis, it’s clear that some corporate media moguls would like to turn back the clock – back to the days when a handful of powerful institutions enjoyed a complete monopoly over the production of news and dissemination of information.
Through this information syndicate, they have been able to create a type of consensus reality. By channeling public opinion, the establishment has been able to facilitate a number of engineered outcomes, including war.
More than ever, it’s important to highlight how for many decades, these same media organizations, including the most respected brands in western mainstream media, have been the driving force behind some of most deceptive reporting and militaristic propaganda campaigns which have enabled the conditions for violent conflict worldwide. These acts of media malice have contributed to the unnecessary deaths of countless innocent people.
Undoubtedly, many who work in the media will not see it that way, but history speaks for itself.
Here are but a few of the greatest war propaganda deceptions of all-time – brought to you by the establishment’s own mainstream media. Here are the real consequences of fake news…
‘Remember the Maine!’
War propaganda is as old as the media itself.
In the winter of 1898, a terrible incident befell America after the USS Maine, one of its flagship Naval vessels had sunk following an unexplained explosion in Havana harbor in Cuba. Afterwards some leading US newspapers took advantage of the confusion and emotive nature of the story, including William Randolph Hearst’s New York Journal and its racy sister publication, the Evening Journal, and also Joseph Pulitzer’s New York World, blaming the incident on Spanish saboteurs. Shortly afterwards, the US entered the Spanish-American War in order to capture Cuba, Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines. This practice of over-reporting and embellishing a story to stir public outrage became known as “yellow journalism” – a badge proudly worn by Hearst in his day. Certainly, Hearst was well ahead of his time in believing media outlets should insert themselves into events in order to affect political outcomes on behalf on the government. One year earlier in 1897, Hearst’s New York World [1] opined the doctrine of “journalism of action” which meant that a newspaper should inject itself into public life, in order to “fitly render any public service within its power.”
Are things really much different today?
The Gulf of Tonkin Deception
On August 4, 1964, a joint US Navy patrol ran into bad weather off the coast of Vietnam, causing problems with US radar and sonar, at a time when heightened tensions in the region had placed the US national security team on red alert. Amid the confusion, some US agent or official, either in the CIA, the NSA or the Pentagon national security structure – circulated a false report that the US Navy vessels and planes were under attack from North Vietnamese patrol attack boats in international waters in the Gulf of Tonkin. The next day, President Lyndon B. Johnson appeared on national television to announce[2] his intent to retaliate against North Vietnamese targets, stating, “Repeated acts of violence against the armed forces of the United States must be met not only with alert defense, but with positive reply. The reply is being given as I speak to you tonight.” The infamous event came to known as ‘The Gulf of Tonkin Incident.’ Despite the fact that there were obvious discrepancies in some of the government account of events, the mainstream media accepted the government’s fake story without question. With the media providing public relations backing, Washington was then able to take the next step and declared War on Vietnam, albeit on false pretenses. This was the beginning a 10 year-long bloody conflict which saw 55,000 US servicemen killed and 250,000 injured and maimed, along with over 1 million Vietnamese killed.
The First Gulf War
It seems that Saddam Hussein’s incursion in neighboring Kuwait wasn’t enough to justify this historic US military operation because the first Gulf War, or ‘Persian Gulf War’ featured a number of fabricated and fake reports produced or circulated by the corporate mainstream media.
On October 10th, 1990, 15 year-old Nayirah al-Ṣabah, daughter of Saud bin Nasir Al-Sabah (the Kuwaiti ambassador to the US) provided a tearful testimony in front of the mainstream media TV cameras, in tears recounting alleged human rights abuses in front of a US Congressional Committee. The Kuwaiti teenager claimed that Iraqi soldiers took hundreds of babies out of incubators in a Kuwaiti hospital during the Iraqi invasion of Kuwait. Her dramatic testimony later turned out to be completely false.
During the 1990-1991 Gulf War when a leaked clip showed how CNN had constructed a fake blue screen studio set-up to give a false impression that reporters like Charles Jaco were at alternative locations, including a live sound stage used to simulate missile attacks in Saudi Arabia complete with fake date palm trees.
This was also the first war where US cable TV provided the bulk of 24 hour mainstream media propaganda promoting every aspect of America’s military operation, led by CNN. Since then, CNN has become the Pentagon’s premier military and war propaganda outlet in the US.
Kosovo ‘Genocide’
After the Rwanda massacres of 1994 the ‘genocide’ alarm has become a tried and true tool used by western media outlets. As the narrative commonly goes, because the US “did not act” in 1994, over 500,000 Tutsis were killed. Granted, the desire to intervene in such a tragedy is born out of compassion and concern for humanity, but when the term ‘genocide’ is casually tossed about in the media in order to invoke an emotional reaction of public outrage, then the media risks stripping the term of its real meaning, and its potency as a call to humanity.
From 1998-1999, Europe and NATO backed Kosovan Liberation Army (KLA) ‘rebel’ fighters from the Kosovo region of Yugoslavia in a poxy war against the military forces of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. With the help of NATO intelligence and military assets, the KLA began attacks on police and Yugoslavian government facilities in Kosovo, which led to an increased presence of Serb paramilitaries and ‘regular forces’ who then began targeting KLA personnel and political sympathisers and political opponents. It is estimated that Federal forces killed some 1,500 to 2,000 civilians and KLA combatants. From here, the conflict, or “civil war” as it was portrayed in the Western mainstream media, began to escalate dramatically, and with that, a flurry of alarmist and sensational western media reporting. Independent journalist Justin Raimondo editor of https://t.co/jRxThKSMRt reported back in 2000:
“The headline in the London Guardian [18 Aug. 2000] was really a bit of an understatement: “Serb killings ‘exaggerated’ by West.” The subhead, however, underscored the enormity of the lie: “Claims of up to 100,000 ethnic Albanians massacred in Kosovo revised to under 3,000 as exhumations near end.” Think of what this has to mean: Madeleine Albright, James Rubin, and Jamie Shea didn’t pull this off single-handedly. Not only the US government, but the worldwide media fabricated a “genocide” and, on that basis, launched a savage war against a sovereign nation that had never attacked us, in the name of “humanitarianism – a war, I might add, that was stopped but has not ended.”
Raimondo continues, “Where are the bodies, all 100,000 of them? This became the task of the “war crimes experts,” as the Guardian describes them: to produce what never existed in the first place – a task that naturally had to end in failure. The Guardian reports:
“As war crimes experts from Britain and other countries prepare to wind down the exhumation of hundreds of graves in Kosovo on behalf of the UN’s International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia in the Hague, officials concede they have not borne out the worst wartime reports. These were given by refugees and repeated by western government spokesmen during the campaign. They talked of indiscriminate killings and as many as 100,000 civilians missing or taken out of refugee columns by the Serbs.”
As the standard progression goes, on back of the humanitarian outrage which was playing out in the western media, the west soon demanded a “No Fly Zone’ over Kosovo and parts of Yugoslavia. In the end, it decided to proceed unilaterally, outside of the remit of international law, and in true Matador fashion – the western press offered no resistance at all. Journalist Lewis MacKenzie of the Globe and Mail explains:
“In 1999, with NATO celebrating its 50th anniversary and no enemy in sight to justify its existence, it sought a new role and solicited a UN resolution to establish a no-fly zone over Serbia/Kosovo – the scene of a civil conflict in the latter, with involvement of the former. When it proved impossible for the UN Security Council to approve such a resolution, NATO, in a highly questionable and arguably illegal move, commenced bombing a sovereign nation, the former Yugoslavia (Serbia/Kosovo). Justification, it was argued, was provided by a dated, no-longer-applicable UN resolution that provided for a no-fly zone to protect European Union monitors in Kosovo. The fact that the EU monitors were no longer deployed in Kosovo was conveniently ignored. What followed was an all-out bombing campaign against the infrastructure of the former Yugoslavia, all under the guise of enforcing a “no-fly zone.” The term was beginning to get a bad reputation.”
By the end of the war, you could see a clear process had been formalized – the production and dissemination between political leaders and the mainstream media outlets – in order to steadily advance the agenda of the war. Antiwar’s Raimondo concludes:
“It was lies, all lies, from beginning to end. They may have originated from government sources, in most cases, but in spreading these lies far and wide the Western media were more than willing accomplices. Keeping in mind that over 5,000 civilians were slaughtered in the NATO air strikes, the ladies and gentlemen of the Fourth Estate might fairly be characterized as Madeleine’s willing executioners. This is a takeoff, of course, on the favored phrase of the New Republic wing of the War Party, which condemns the entire Serb nation as “Milosevic’s willing executioners.” Based on the myth of an Albanian Kosovar “holocaust” perpetrated by the Serbs, not only Milosevic and his regime but the entire Serbian people are condemned as being no better than the “good Germans” who voted Hitler into power and tacitly supported the Holocaust. Here was classic war propaganda, on a par with stories of Belgian babies impaled on German bayonets during World War I and tall tales told during the Gulf war of babies dumped out of incubators and gasping for breath on the floor of a Kuwaiti hospital. The idea is to get public opinion behind the complete subjugation and “reeducation” of the Serbian people, utilizing the postwar German model.”
It has to mentioned also, that one of the leading agents of disinformation in NATO’s Kosovo operation was CNN’s ‘war correspondent’ Christiane Amanpour, whom Raimondo singles out as a key purveyor fake news that moulded public opinion enough to allow the war to escalate on schedule for NATO:
“In the case of the Kosovo war, the retreat has already begun. Far too late to help the victims of the vicious “Allied” air war: they are dead and buried, or else mutilated beyond repair. Yet we are still waiting for some acknowledgment – aside from a few stories in overseas newspapers – from the media that they were wrong. After endless horror stories illustrated with fantastically high death tolls were aired day after day on CNN, when will we hear a retraction? Christiane Amanpour repeated her husband’s lies with a perfectly straight face: tens of thousands slaughtered, we were told, and the murderous drug-dealing KLA were really “freedom fighters,” the Albanian equivalent of George Washington and his Continental Army! Journalists didn’t question the government line about alleged Serbian “genocide”: instead they wanted to know if the President would send in the ground troops – and if not, why not?”
Incredibly, we would see a near repeat of this planned model again in Syria.
Osama Bin Laden: A Mythology of Convenience
A really big lie which was already baked into the official 9/11 narrative: “The terrorist known as Osama bin Laden carried out the 9/11 attacks and he is being given shelter in the nation of Afghanistan. If the Taliban government does not hand over this fugitive, then the US will have no choice but to retaliate against Afghanistan.” Kabul then asked if the US would provide evidence that bin Laden was indeed responsible for the spectacular attacks. This request was ignored by US authorities, but Washington’s ignorance paled in comparison to the mainstream media’s collective inability to follow-up on this, the most crucial piece in the story. In reality, the US was not going to wait for answers, or for the illusive bin Laden to appear. Washington had already mapped out its ‘strategic’ targets and scrambled its long-range stealth bombers. Assets were being mobilized and a new war began as ‘Operation Enduring Freedom’ launched on October 7, 2001.  Some 15 years later, the Afghans are still having to endure the Pentagon’s version of freedom, as US-led forces are still occupying and controlling large regions of the country, but doing so conveniently under a NATO banner. To understand the scale and scope of the Afghanistan lie, consider the following:  In 2006, the Muckraker Report[3] contacted FBI Headquarters to inquire why Bin Laden’s “Most Wanted” poster did not indicate any connection to 9/11. When asked why, the FBI official stated that, “The reason why 9/11 is not mentioned on Usama Bin Laden’s Most Wanted page is because the FBI has no hard evidence connecting Bin Laden to 9/11.” You’d think that would have been the big scoop, for some investigative journalist working at the New York Times, or the Washington Post. Instead, the press simply fell into line with the official narrative coming out of the Bush Administration.
Beyond all this however, a bigger media failure which still continues to this day, is the total redaction of the fact that Obama Bin Laden was an intelligence asset of the CIA since the 1980’s during Operation Cyclone, facilitating a US policy of funding and arming a radical Islamist Mujahideen ‘rebels.’ Sound familiar?
The Media’s WMD Deception in Iraq
In March 2003, on the eve of the Iraq War, US and UK government officials had managed to convince their respective mainstream media cadres that Iraq’s Saddam Hussein was harboring massive stockpiles of chemical weapons which came to be commonly known as “Weapons of Mass Destruction.” Despite repeated assurances by UN weapons inspectors and long-time US weapons experts on the ground like Scott Ritter, both President George W. Bush and Prime Minister Tony Blair appeared to have already made up their minds that Saddam was hiding vast stores of deadly munitions and therefore a US-led invasion was a fait accompli. Despite the fact  they had no proof or actual evidence, the press didn’t seem to mind because they were “very confident” about the “intelligence.” The White House then dispatched Secretary of State Colin Powell to the United Nations in New York where he regurgitated a made-up story about Saddam Hussein’s deadly mobile anthrax labs, aka “The Winnebagos of Death” [4]. Yes, it sounded completely crazy to millions of intelligent, normal people at the time, and yet – it was good enough for the mainstream media circa 2002 – 2003.
Aside from CNN, ABC, and NBC’s complete allegiance to the government’s fraudulent war effort, America’s alleged ‘papers of record,’ The New York Times and The Washington Post, helped endlessly in republishing government-issued fictional accounts. One ‘journalist’ in particular, Judith Miller from the New York Times, managed to dupe the public by citing the same ‘sources’, like disgraced Iraqi dissident Ahmed Chalabi, that were feeding the US intelligence community false information about Iraq’s supposed stockpiles of WMDs.
The Times Later admitted that many of Miller’s stories were false. Still, the damage was already done. The result of this government-media complex campaign of actual fake news was 1 million dead Iraqis, thousands of dead US servicemen, tens of thousands wounded and maimed, along with trillions of US taxpayer funds spent – an open bill which continues to this day.
Miller has since been rewarded for her patriotic efforts with a job at FOX News.
The Planned Take-Down of Libya
Next was a revamp of the Iraq narrative, this time spear-headed by the new liberal ‘humanitarian interventionists,’ led by America’s Barack Obama and France’s Nicholas Sarkozy against Libya in 2010, and under cover of the NATO flag. To get the ball rolling, western politicians and the media tried to frame political dissent in Libya as part of the wider ‘Arab Spring’ movement, while simultaneously supporting armed opposition groups on the ground.
In 2011, after working behind the scenes helping to organize, arm and equip militant Jihadis fighters and rebel operatives in Libya, the Obama Administration, led by then Secretary of State Hillary Clinton, desperately needed an excuse to ground the Libyan Air Force in order that NATO-backed Jihadi fighters on the ground could successfully overthrow the government of Colonel Muammar Gaddafi. The most direct route to achieve air superiority would be to implement a ‘No Fly Zone’ over Libya, but with the public relations scars still fresh from the Iraq debacle, Presidents Obama and Sarkozy knew that a No Fly Zone needed broad international support and therefore had to be done through the United Nations. In order to get the global public behind the campaign, a series of fake news stories were concocted by the US State Department and the mainstream media. The first one was the popular talking point that Gaddafi was using military fighter jets to “gun down peaceful protesters in the streets.” Despite the lack of any proof or evidence that this actually happened, the entire mainstream media in the US and Europe ran with it anyway. This bogus claim became the keystone of the No Fly Zone campaign. Another outlandish tale was that Gaddafi was issuing Viagra to his troops so that they could go out and commit “mass rape” against the women of Libya. This invented story was originally disseminated by Qatari government media outlet Al Jazeera[5], and was specifically designed to help generate more liberal leftwing sympathy for a ‘humanitarian intervention’ by NATO, particularly from women in the US and Europe. The key emissary who delivered this fake news item to the public –and gave it credibility, was none other that Obama’s former US ambassador to the UN, Susan Rice[6].
The other media lie which was promulgated in partnership with the US political establishment was the myth that ‘Genocide’ was imminent in Libya at the hands of Colonel Gaddafi’s black ‘African Mercenary’ brigades, prompting the routine trope in the the Responsibility to Protect script of, ‘We must act now, before it’s too late.” Writer Maximilian Forte describes how this narrative was constructed:
“Just a few days after the street protests began, on February 21 the very quick to defect Libyan deputy Permanent Representative to the UN, Ibrahim Dabbashi, stated: “We are expecting a real genocide in Tripoli. The airplanes are still bringing mercenaries to the airports”. This is excellent: a myth that is composed of myths. With that statement he linked three key myths together—the role of airports (hence the need for that gateway drug of military intervention: the no-fly zone), the role of “mercenaries” (meaning, simply, black people), and the threat of “genocide” (geared toward the language of the UN’s doctrine of the Responsibility to Protect). As ham-fisted and wholly unsubstantiated as the assertion was, he was clever in cobbling together three ugly myths, one of them grounded in racist discourse and practice that endures to the present, with newer atrocities reported against black Libyan and African migrants on a daily basis. He was not alone in making these assertions. Among others like him, Soliman Bouchuiguir, president of the Libyan League for Human Rights, told Reuters on March 14 that if Gaddafi’s forces reached Benghazi, “there will be a real bloodbath, a massacre like we saw in Rwanda”.[7]
As a result of these and other unfounded ‘human rights’ abuses trumpeted by the mainstream media, on 17 March 2011, UN Resolution 1973 was passed by the UN Security Council and the No Fly Zone was then immediately transformed into a US-led mass-bombing campaign of Libya by NATO. It is estimated that 30,000 Libyans were killed through ‘rebel’ ground fighting, artillery and relentless NATO bombing which toppled the Libyan government, turning the country into a permanent failed state and terrorist haven. Looking back, it’s hard to believe that so few questioned these made-up stories, but like with Iraq and so many other wars, the media played their role in propelling the fake news.
SEE ALSO: AN INTRODUCTION: Smart Power & The Human Rights Industrial Complex – By Patrick Henningsen
Russia’s Phantom Invasion of the Ukraine
As far as the corporate mainstream is concerned, this story is the media’s gold standard of fake news. Not a day goes by in the US media that you don’t hear the need for the US and NATO to “Counter Russian aggression,” alongside the tandem claim that, “Russia’s invasion of the Ukraine,” or “Russian annexed Crimea,” and are somehow ‘occupying’ the peninsula militarily.
So who is driving this narrative? Once again, leading the way in the collective media construction of the ‘Russian Invasion’ narrative was a familiar rag. In April 20, 2014, a photo was published by the New York Times allegedly from inside Russia showing ‘Russian soldiers’ said to have later appeared in eastern Ukraine. This fake news story was then sent along the usual disinformation daisy chain, with CNN and others elevating the story into “proof” nefarious Russian aggression. This in turn, was then cited by US State Department, and then by hawkish US politicians as proof required to back a more aggressive policy against Russia. However, the photographer later went on record to state his photo was actually taken inside the Ukraine.
Award-winning investigative journalist Robert Parry[8] explains:
“Two days after the New York Times led its editions with a one-sided article about photos supposedly proving that Russian special forces were behind the popular uprisings in eastern Ukraine, the Times published what you might call a modified, limited retraction.
“Buried deep inside the Wednesday editions (page 9 in my paper), the article by Michael R. Gordon and Andrew E. Kramer two of the three authors from the earlier story has this curious beginning: “A collection of photographs that Ukraine says shows the presence of Russian forces in the eastern part of the country, and which the United States cited as evidence of Russian involvement, has come under scrutiny.”
By that time, the damage had already been done, and the media and political classes were already off and running with the narrative.

Down Memory Lane…

Once a year, on Family Day, naval families get an opportunity to sail aboard our warships to experience, even if only for a few hours, the world in which their loved ones serve.

It is a day that offers families a glimpse into what the Indian Navy truly stands for: the unforgiving seas, the risks undertaken, the long separations, the sacrifices quietly made through it all, the sailor who carries on with courage, pride and a smile.

Looking back, I feel immensely blessed and proud to have once been a part of this magnificent institution, the Indian Navy.

Some bonds never fade. Some memories never grow old.

या फिर, 
जैसे तुम दिखते हो, वैसे बन जाओ।”

Dial a Sailor is a 1990 X-rated (hardcore adult) feature (by director John T. Bone) shot on location in Australia.  It was part of a short-lived series of Australian-shot ("Down Under") adult films made that year by US performers and crew who traveled there specifically for the productions.  

The title directly references a genuine, long-running US Navy/Australian community hospitality program active in the 1970s–1990s (and earlier in some ports).  When US 7th Fleet ships (destroyers, frigates, etc.) made port calls in places like Brisbane, Sydney, Melbourne, Perth, or Fremantle, local residents volunteered via a "Dial-a-Sailor" hotline or desk set up on the quarterdeck or at the pier.  Families, couples, and especially single women would call to offer to host sailors for meals, sightseeing, barbecues, boomerang throwing, pub crawls, or... pure Anglo-Celtic Aussie hospitality!

Battle buddies have each other’s six (backs) 

We strive to serve.

One team; one family; one labor; one fight! 

It's been a blessing this week to head across the country to the East coast to Virginia for  duty during which I reconnected with my original US Army team leader and Battle Buddy, John Harwood. Over 20 years ago, as a young Privates Stoddard and Estrada, we learned life and leadership from then-Sergeant Harwood. The photo from that deployment still captures us as a couple of Soldiers training under his guidance and mentoring. 

We trained and served together both CONUS (Continental US) and OCONUS (Outside the US), and later each of us independently in multiple countries and combat zones. Seeing him again after more than two decades felt seamless, because true Battle Buddies never stop having each other’s backs. One team; One fight. 

We met up in Yorktown Virginia the same place he asked his better half to marry him. Yorktown Virginia is layered with American history: the surrender of British General Cornwallis to US General George Washington, our first President and the Commander who led the Continental US  Army. The towering monument in the picture was the gift monument authorized by Congress, just days after Cornwallis surrendered at Yorktown. The Continental Congress passed a resolution directing that a monument be erected at Yorktown to commemorate the victory.

From the Revolution through the War of 1812, the Civil War, the World Wars, Korea, Vietnam, and the long fight in Afghanistan and the Middle East, America has repeatedly faced what looked like overwhelming odds. Imperfect people, guided by something greater, have continued to secure liberty, the freedom to worship how, where, and what we choose. God and heavenly and earthly servants labor onward. 🙌

The United States remains a special country, a melting pot made stronger together. One team;  One fight.

text:
Tariffs Appear to Spook Markets.

On Sept 2, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said the Trump administration is developing a semiconductor tariff framework explicitly tied to U.S. manufacturing. In a CNBC interview, Lutnick said the policy would effectively mean: companies that build semiconductor production in the United States receive tariff relief, while companies that do not should expect to pay tariffs to access the U.S. market. He confirmed that linking tariff relief to U.S. semiconductor investment is the administration’s intended approach.

During the same interview, when the interviewer characterized Samsung Electronics and Hynix as effectively being “on notice,” Lutnick agreed and said, “They need to build here.” He cited Micron’s more than $250 billion planned U.S. investment through 2035 as an example of the kind of domestic semiconductor-manufacturing commitment the administration wants to encourage. Micron says those investments are intended eventually to support production of approximately 40% of its DRAM in the United States.

The tariff rates, country quotas, qualifying-investment thresholds and exact product scope have not been finalized. One proposal under consideration would extend semiconductor-related tariffs beyond chips themselves to certain products containing them, potentially including laptops, gaming consoles and data-center servers. South Korea’s presidential office said Sept 3 that, as far as it knows, details of the U.S. semiconductor tariffs remain unresolved.

Hnix’s new Indiana facility:
SK hynix says leading-edge wafers will continue to be fabricated in Korea and then shipped to Indiana for advanced HBM packaging and testing. The Indiana project therefore should not automatically be assumed to satisfy a future tariff exemption designed specifically around domestic front-end semiconductor manufacturing. Whether it qualifies will depend on rules that have not yet been published.

Samsung already has substantial U.S. semiconductor manufacturing operations in Austin and is building its advanced-process Taylor, Texas fab, with more than $40 billion of Central Texas investment previously contemplated. Samsung may therefore be better positioned than SK hynix under a manufacturing-linked exemption, although it remains unknown whether Samsung’s existing U.S. footprint would satisfy whatever investment or production thresholds the administration ultimately sets.

For now, this is a potential policy risk to be further monitored but 2027 p/e multiples of Hynix and Samsung  (see prior posts) are already so low at present stock prices, even if tariffs could be implemented quite high hypothetically, even in that unlikely case, the Korean listings of both would still remain exceedingly cheap (recall UBS 2027 p/e of about 2.7 based on UBS forecasts...   more like mid 3s for Samsung).

2.7; the stock prices could raise 500% and Hynix and Samsung could still appear relative cheap. 

Trump administration is also already fighting inflation perceptions as they relate to interest rates; applying tarifs on memory when memory prices are already inflationary (Jensen called the situation "extreme" is not itself without political risks ahead of mid terms. Nor does the Trump Administration like it when US markets sell off.  Higher memory prices due to tariffs will not be good for nvda and several others in US markets; i interpret this as most likely mere leverage being exerted to get Hynix to, longer term, do more in the US and/or ongoing politics with the Trump Administration having previously complained about wanting more offers to help from S Korea with Hormuz. 

 The day Hynix listed its ADR shares (on or about July 10th), it did appear Hynix was keen to expand further in the US in any event (see Bloomberg tv interview).

Perhaps this is also a back up policy of the Trump Administration to disfavor CXMT as much as or more than anyone else.

text:
The spread between U.S. and Chinese 10-year government bonds has widened to 312 basis points  just a few basis points below the roughly 315 bp record reached early last year. The U.S. 10-year Treasury briefly reached 4.81%, its highest level in nearly three years, while China’s 10-year yield remained around 1.69%.
This is not simply a bond-market statistic.
It is a divergence in economic regimes.

The United States is confronting persistent inflation, elevated energy costs, substantial fiscal borrowing and renewed expectations that the Federal Reserve may need to keep monetary policy restrictive  or even raise rates further. China, by contrast, is operating with dramatically lower yields as policymakers prioritize economic recovery and continue to support domestic demand.
That creates an extraordinary asymmetry in global capital allocation.
Think about the incentive structure.
An investor can obtain approximately 4.8% from a 10-year U.S. Treasury, while a comparable Chinese government bond offers roughly 1.7%.
The difference is more than 3 percentage points per year before accounting for currency risk, hedging costs and other considerations.
That changes portfolio mathematics.
It can increase the relative attractiveness of U.S. dollar assets, put pressure on the international demand equation for Chinese bonds and potentially encourage capital to seek higher risk-adjusted returns outside China.
But there is an important caveat:
A 312 bp spread does not automatically mean capital will flee China.

China's capital controls, enormous domestic savings pool and relatively low foreign ownership of government bonds act as significant buffers. Reuters notes that foreign investors held only about 4.6% of China's government bond market at the end of July, limiting the potential for a sudden foreign-driven liquidation.

The deeper issue is therefore not simply capital flight.
It is capital allocation efficiency.
The U.S. is effectively offering global investors a much higher nominal sovereign yield while China is maintaining exceptionally low domestic borrowing costs to support growth.
That divergence can influence:

USD/CNY → global bond flows → reserve allocation → Asian currencies → equity valuations → commodity demand → liquidity conditions.

And there is an even bigger macroeconomic implication.
If U.S. yields remain elevated because of inflation, fiscal deficits and enormous Treasury issuance, the global financial system is forced to operate with a significantly higher risk-free discount rate.

That matters for everything.
Equities become more expensive to justify.
Corporate financing costs rise.
Emerging-market debt becomes more difficult.
Private capital demands higher returns.
And speculative assets face a higher opportunity cost.

Meanwhile, China is moving in the opposite direction attempting to lower the cost of capital and stimulate economic activity.
One economy is fighting inflation.
The other is fighting insufficient demand.
That is why the U.S.-China yield spread deserves much more attention than the headline itself suggests.
If the gap approaches or breaks the historical 315 bp area, markets will be watching not simply for a record in the bond market, but for evidence of a deeper restructuring of global capital flows.
Because interest-rate differentials ultimately influence where the world's capital wants to live.
The bond market is telling us that Washington and Beijing are currently operating under two very different economic realities.
And when the world's two largest economies move in opposite monetary directions, the consequences rarely remain inside their borders.
The next battle may not be for trade dominance.
It may be for global capital.

text:
Dad of girl left permanently disabled in crash with illegal rejects fake sympathy from Democrats!📷
Marcus Coleman sat in a House hearing room on Tuesday and told the Democrats across from him that he did not want their sympathy.
His daughter Dalilah is seven years old.
In June 2024, an 18-wheeler doing 60 miles an hour plowed into the vehicle she was riding in on a Southern California highway.
She came out of it with a fractured skull, a broken femur, and a traumatic brain injury.
She will live with that injury for the rest of her life.
The man behind the wheel was Partap Singh, an illegal immigrant from India. California had given him a commercial driver’s license. Authorities say he was speeding and did not stop for traffic in a construction zone.
Coleman came to testify before the House Judiciary subcommittee that handles immigration enforcement. The subject was sanctuary policies in California, Colorado, and Maryland. Those policies limit how much local police and state agencies cooperate with federal immigration authorities. The Democrats on the panel offered him their condolences. He handed them back.
“I reject your guys’ sympathy,” he said. He told them not one of them had ever reached out to his family. Not one had stopped him in a hallway to say they were sorry.
The only time they cared, he said, was inside that room with the cameras on.
Then he pointed at his daughter and told them she was the end result of sanctuary cities.
Anyone who has spent time around Washington knows the ritual. A witness with a painful story sits down. Members express their deep sorrow.
Then they pivot to talking points and move on to the next witness. Coleman refused to play his part.
He named the people he holds responsible and said he always will.
His argument rests on a simple point. Singh should not have been in this country. He should not have held a California license to drive a truck that weighs 40 tons.
Every step that put him on that road involved a policy choice made by people in government.
Coleman’s daughter is paying for those choices.
The cost to his family did not stop with her injuries. Coleman used to drive a truck for a living. He cannot do that anymore. He has nine children. He told the committee he is pinching pennies and stretching every dollar.
A man who was providing for his family is now scraping by, because someone who broke the law to get here was handed the keys to a rig.
He made one more point that Democrats might want to sit with. His wife is an immigrant. She came here the legal way. She filled out the forms, waited her turn, and did what the law asked of her. Coleman does not see why people who jumped a fence should get the same treatment she earned.
Millions of legal immigrants feel the same way. They know the difference between a line and a shortcut better than anyone.
Coleman was not the only parent at the table. Patricia Fox told the committee about her daughter, Carissa Aspnes. In March 2025, a hit-and-run driver in Colorado, an illegal immigrant from Venezuela, sent Carissa headfirst into a concrete barrier at close to 50 miles an hour.
The driver and passenger left without checking whether she was alive.
Carissa survived. Her mother now uses a lift to get her out of bed.
She blends her daughter’s food and feeds her through a tube.
She gives her the medications and bathes her.
She sleeps lightly so she can hear the alarm if her daughter’s oxygen drops in the night. Fox told the committee that one collision turned an entire family into victims.
Fox asked the question that sanctuary supporters never answer.
If an American citizen had hit her daughter, she would still be grieving. She would not also be sitting in Congress asking why someone with no legal right to be here was on that road in the first place.
She had a message for the other side of the aisle, too. She said she understands they hate the President.
She has seen the campaign ads.
She told them they need to love Americans more than they hate Donald Trump, and that doing so is their job.
Defenders of sanctuary policies say they protect trust between immigrant communities and the police. Where was the protection for Dalilah Coleman?
A policy that makes it easier for people here illegally to stay, work, and drive is a policy that accepts the risk of what happened to these two girls.
Someone in government decided that risk was worth it. Nobody asked the Colemans or the Foxes.
Coleman said the building should be checked for mold, since the people inside seem to have lost their minds thinking sanctuary cities are a good idea.
That is a father talking, and he earned the right to say it.
The lawmakers who support these policies should have to look at Dalilah Coleman’s face when they cast their votes. She did not ask for any of this.
Her father is right about that. The people who crossed the border illegally made a choice.
The officials who chose to shield them made a choice.
The only person in that room who never got a choice is a seven-year-old girl who will carry a brain injury for the rest of her life.
Marcus Coleman asked Congress for one thing. Change the policies so the next father never has to sit in that chair. That request should not depend on which party you belong to. It is the least his daughter is owed.

text:
If you let the map sit next to an older map for a moment, Cairo has heard this speech before, in a different accent.

In 1956 Gamal Abdel Nasser took the Suez Canal from Britain and France. London and Paris, with Israel, tried to snatch it back. Washington and Moscow both told them to stop. 

Egypt learned a hard lesson: the great powers will fight over your waterway and call it your independence. 

Nasser then took Soviet weapons, later drifted, and spent the rest of his life trying to be “non-aligned” while still needing someone’s spare parts. 

Seventy years later Xi sits in the same city, on the seventieth anniversary of China–Egypt ties, and says the people of the Middle East should be “masters of their own affairs.” 

The offer is real enough to sign twenty documents. 

The catch is the same as in 1956: mastery that arrives in someone else’s airplane is still a lease.

Now do a thought experiment and widen the frame from physical palaces to the spiritual law. Listen to what is being promised:

The Law of Free Will says no being — not a president, not an archangel — may coerce another soul’s choice. 

“Masters of their own destiny” sounds like that law spoken in diplomatic Chinese. 

The Law of Affinity adds the part the communiqué leaves out: you end up in the company that matches the frequency you actually live, not the frequency you announce. 

The Qur’an puts the same hinge in one sentence: “Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves.” (13:11) 

A Course in Miracles is blunter about special relationships between nations: “You do not realize how much you have misused your brothers by seeing them as sources of specialness.” 

Egypt can take Chinese data centers and still cash the American military cheque. That is not hypocrisy so much as a soul that has not yet chosen which field it belongs to.

Does that look like Egypt expressing their free will after all?

The Puntland–Somaliland comparison misses the strategic point.

Somaliland offers Washington geography. Puntland offers Washington leverage.

Yes, Berbera is well located. But strategic analysis does not end where the map begins.

The real question is a simple cost-benefit one:

What does Washington get and what does it have to pay for it?

With Somaliland, deeper strategic access eventually runs into the recognition premium: political capital spent to unlock geographic value.

Puntland offers a cleaner return: strategic access, local forces, intelligence, maritime reach, counterterrorism capacity against ISIS, and political leverage inside Somalia without the same diplomatic cost.

That is the comparison that actually matters.

text:
China told Pacific Island nations to keep Taiwan out of the Pacific Islands Forum leaders' meeting, or face "consequences." That's not a paraphrase. That's what Beijing communicated, according to ABC News Australia reporting from September 1, 2026. Unspecified consequences. Delivered to small island governments that depend heavily on Chinese aid, investment, and diplomatic relationships. The coercive structure here is not subtle.

The Pacific Islands Forum has been a slow-motion battleground for years, but this is a more naked version of what usually happens behind closed doors. Beijing typically prefers to move these levers quietly, through back-channel diplomacy and the steady application of economic dependency. Going public with a warning like this means Beijing decided the demonstration value outweighed the reputational cost. They want Pacific governments to understand clearly that association with Taiwan carries a price. That's a message meant not just for this meeting, but for every future decision these governments make about Taiwan's international participation.

The backdrop matters. Taiwan has watched its formal diplomatic relationships in the Pacific erode steadily as Beijing runs what amounts to a structured campaign to flip recognition. Solomon Islands is the most prominent example. It switched from Taipei to Beijing in 2019, and part of what followed was a security agreement with China that sent actual alarm bells through Canberra and Washington. Kiribati made the same switch the same year. Taiwan's formal Pacific allies have shrunk to a short list, and Beijing's goal, pretty clearly, is to get that number to zero while simultaneously closing off the informal and multilateral spaces where Taiwan might otherwise show up.

The PIF is one of those spaces. Taiwan's presence at the leaders' meeting is not equivalent to full membership, but it matters symbolically and practically as a venue where Taipei can engage with regional governments, make its case, and maintain some form of multilateral visibility. That's precisely why Beijing is working to block it. The logic of Beijing's Taiwan policy is to reduce Taiwan's international presence to the point where the question of its status stops being a live issue on the world stage. Every forum exclusion, every flipped diplomatic relationship, every "consequence" warning is a brick in that wall.

Pacific Island nations are not passive objects in this contest, even if they're often treated that way in coverage that centers Washington and Beijing. They have real agency, real interests, and real leverage that comes from controlling strategic waters, ports, and seabed resources that the major powers want access to or want to deny to rivals. Palau is a good example of how this plays out. Fortune's concurrent reporting describes Palau as "ground zero for a U.S.-China standoff," which is a reasonable description. Palau maintains formal diplomatic relations with Taiwan, sits in strategically significant waters, and has become a focal point of competition precisely because of that geography. When Beijing warns of consequences, governments like Palau are doing math that includes not just Chinese aid packages but also what their relationship with the United States and Taiwan is actually worth in security and economic terms.

The problem is that math doesn't always favor Taiwan's allies. Chinese investment through Belt and Road programs creates real economic dependency in countries with small populations, limited revenue bases, and genuine development needs. Climate change is an existential issue for low-lying Pacific Island states, and they need resources and international attention to address it. Beijing offers infrastructure money. The diplomatic cost, increasingly, is compliance on Taiwan-related questions. That's a transaction a lot of governments will take, especially when the alternative is an abstract principle of multilateral openness backed by less concrete support.

What's striking about this particular moment is that Beijing made the warning in a way that ABC News could report it, which means it filtered out through Pacific government channels into the press. That suggests the warning was delivered in a form that wasn't purely deniable back-channel pressure. Beijing chose to make the cost of including Taiwan legible. That's a calibrated move. It signals to every Pacific government watching that Beijing is watching them, that deference on Taiwan is an expected deliverable, and that there will be a reckoning for governments that don't deliver it.

The PIF meeting's stated agenda includes climate change, fisheries governance, and economic development. Those are serious issues that directly affect the lives of people in Pacific Island communities. The concern flagged in the ABC News reporting, that China-Taiwan tensions could "explode into the open" and crowd out that agenda, is legitimate. It also illustrates a structural problem with Chinese coercive diplomacy in multilateral forums: even when Beijing wins the specific fight, it creates instability and resentment in institutions that Pacific nations built to serve their own interests. That resentment doesn't always translate into pushback, but it accumulates.

The broader U.S. role here is worth being clear-eyed about. Washington has beefed up its Pacific diplomacy in recent years, reopened the embassy in Solomon Islands, pushed new aid and compact arrangements, and tried to counter Chinese influence. Some of that has worked at the margins. But the United States has a credibility problem in the Pacific that predates the current competition with China, rooted in decades of inconsistent engagement and, for some island communities, a legacy of nuclear testing. China's pitch to Pacific nations doesn't have to be particularly good. It just has to exist and come with money attached.

For Taiwan, the PIF situation is part of a pattern that has no easy solution. Its formal diplomatic allies in the region are few and under sustained pressure. Its informal multilateral access is contested at every turn. The tools available to Taipei to push back are limited, and they depend heavily on the United States and other democratic partners treating Taiwan's international space as a priority worth expending diplomatic capital to protect. That priority competes with a lot of other priorities.

China's warning to Pacific Island Forum members is coercion. It's documented, it's explicit, and it follows a playbook Beijing has used consistently across the Indo-Pacific and beyond. The Pacific is just where the terrain is particularly favorable to Beijing's preferred methods: economic leverage applied to governments with limited alternatives, on questions where the major democratic powers have historically underinvested. The consequences Beijing is threatening are unspecified by design. Vague threats are often more effective than specific ones because they let the target's imagination do the work.

At the National Art Gallery in Dublin, a husband and wife were staring at a portrait that had them completely confused. 

The painting depicted three black men, totally naked, sitting on 
a bench. Two of the figures had black penises, but the one in the middle had a pink penis. 

The curator of the gallery realized that they were having trouble interpreting the painting and offered his personal assessment.

He went on for over half an hour explaining how it depicted the sexual emasculation of African Americans in a predominately white patriarchal society.

After the curator left, an Irishman approached the couple and said, "Would you like to know what the painting is really about?"

"Now why would you claim to be more of an expert than the curator of the gallery", asked the couple?

"Because I am the artist, who painted the picture", he replied.
“In fact, there are no African Americans depicted at all. They're just three Irish coal miners. 
The guy in the middle went home for lunch".

Subject: Request for technical fact-check of an unusual Facebook account-switching incident

The user is asking ChatGPT to fact-check its own explanation of an unusual incident that occurred on Facebook.

She was scrolling normally on her primary Facebook account when, apparently instantaneously, the app logged her out of that account and placed her into her secondary Facebook account. At essentially the same time, a notification/prompt appeared concerning Meta Verified and the option to subscribe for $14.99.

What is confusing her is that, from her perspective, accomplishing those things manually would have required several separate actions: switching accounts, opening or accessing notifications, locating the verification offer, and selecting the subscription. She says that her notifications were turned off, yet the verification prompt appeared immediately after the account switch. She ultimately subscribed and was charged $14.99.

ChatGPT previously told her that an ordinary software/session problem or automated account behavior was substantially more plausible than Mark Zuckerberg or another person at Meta remotely manipulating her account. ChatGPT also explained that a single software or server event can produce a chain of visible changes without a human performing each individual click.

However, she does not want to simply be told “it was a glitch.” She wants to understand technically how such a glitch could produce this particular sequence of events.

Specifically, could a Facebook/Meta application experience a session or account-state error that simultaneously or sequentially:

terminates or loses the active session for Account A;
restores or switches to Account B already stored on the device;
loads an account-specific notification or promotional prompt for Account B;
displays a Meta Verified subscription offer even though notifications were disabled; and
potentially initiate or complete a subscription flow resulting in a $14.99 charge?

If that sequence is technically possible, what mechanism could produce it? For example, could cached account state, authentication/session expiration, push-notification behavior, server-side account configuration, app state restoration, or a race condition cause several apparent “clicks” to happen automatically?

She is specifically asking for a technical explanation of what could have happened, not merely reassurance that she imagined it or a generic statement that “bugs happen.”

She also wants an important distinction made between three possibilities:

an ordinary software/session bug;
an automated Facebook/Meta system behaving unexpectedly; and
deliberate intervention by an individual at Meta.

ChatGPT has said that the first two are technically plausible but that the described incident by itself does not provide evidence for the third. She would like that conclusion independently fact-checked rather than simply repeated.

Finally, she would like to know whether the $14.99 charge can be technically connected to the account-switching event or whether the billing event should be treated as a separate issue requiring examination of the actual Apple/Meta billing record.

The goal is simply to solve the technical mystery: what could cause a computer application to produce a sequence of actions that, to the user, looks like several deliberate clicks even though the user did not perform those clicks?

Captives of the Golden Sun – Part III • The Gilded Cage & The Broken Promise 

👉 Manager Clotilde’s Notice —
This image is from the story Captives of the Golden Sun – Part III • The Gilded Cage & The Broken Promise — A Second Rendering, now available on our Patreon.
https://t.co/6CkNLmynUe

Scene 23

23. Once the blindfold is removed, Ingrid recognizes Malik as the man she briefly met during her last visit to Samira’s house with Lotte. She does not yet know what happened after their separation or the part he played in her beloved’s fate. Anticipating a violent reaction to the truth, Samira secures Ingrid’s wrists behind her back and binds her arms and body tightly with broad leather straps before allowing Malik to speak.

Captives of the Golden Sun – Part III • The Gilded Cage & The Broken Promise

The Story So Far (Part III. description)

In the summer of 1975, European travelers Ingrid and Lotte were lured into a carefully prepared trap by Samira, drugged, captured, and violently separated. Ingrid surrendered her freedom after Samira promised that her obedience would ensure Lotte’s safety. Unknown to her, Lotte was instead handed over to Samira’s brother Malik and taken across the desert as merchandise.

In Part II, Lotte endured an exhausting journey to the city, where she was prepared for auction and sold to a wealthy Sheikh. Meanwhile, Ingrid was transformed into Samira’s silent servant—dressed in gold, restrained, and forced to endure repeated humiliation in the belief that every act of obedience was protecting the woman she loved.

Part III follows their two distant paths as they continue to unfold beneath the same unforgiving sun.

Lotte is brought to the Sheikh’s home as an expensive gift for his wife, Nawal, whose fascination with women and control is immediately awakened by the silent European captive. Yet beneath Nawal’s dominant nature lies a capacity for compassion that Lotte has not encountered since her ordeal began. As she listens to Lotte’s story, improves the conditions of her confinement, and offers her protection, curiosity slowly develops into tenderness. Lotte remains restrained and far from free, but within this gilded cage she discovers the first fragile traces of safety—and perhaps the beginning of an unexpected bond.

Ingrid’s captivity follows a far darker course. Still believing in Samira’s promise, she submits to degrading service and bears every restraint with quiet dignity for Lotte’s sake. That sacrifice becomes meaningless when Samira returns with Malik and allows him to reveal the truth: Lotte was taken to the market and sold, while brother and sister shared the profit.

The revelation destroys Ingrid’s last reason to cooperate. Her grief soon hardens into open defiance, and she declares that Samira will never again receive her willing obedience. Deprived of the lie that once gave her power, Samira turns to force, leaving Ingrid bound in a cellar until thirst, exhaustion, and isolation can accomplish what deception no longer can.

Thus, the two women end this chapter farther apart than ever. Lotte’s captivity begins to soften under Nawal’s growing compassion, while Ingrid’s ordeal descends into an increasingly merciless struggle of wills. Neither knows where the other is, whether she is safe, or whether they will ever meet again—but even across the distance, their love remains the invisible force shaping every choice they make.

Their cages are different. Their futures remain uncertain. And their story is far from over.

The Visual Journey (Photo Descriptions)

1. After paying a considerable price for Lotte at the city slave market, the Sheikh brings her into his home as a living gift for his senior wife. He studies the silent, hollow-eyed young woman and wonders whether such a withdrawn captive was truly a wise investment. Lotte no longer weeps or resists; exhausted by all she has endured, she has retreated into lethargy, consumed above all by uncertainty over Ingrid’s fate.

2. Before leaving, the Sheikh orders one of his servants to give the parched Lotte water. His concern is partly pragmatic—she is an expensive possession intended for the woman he loves—but the servant’s response is genuinely compassionate. Lotte drinks eagerly and looks up at her with quiet gratitude, finding a first small trace of human kindness within the unfamiliar household.

3. The Sheikh proudly presents his costly gift to his senior wife, Nawal, knowing well of her attraction to submissive women and actively encouraging it. Lotte immediately captures Nawal’s curious attention, yet the young captive remains emotionally absent, overwhelmed by recent suffering and fear for the beloved Ingrid whose whereabouts she still does not know.

4. Having accepted Lotte as her new possession, Nawal leads her to a private wardrobe and invites her to choose from its elegant dresses. The offer creates a small illusion of choice, but Lotte gives no answer and shows no interest in the garments before her. Her silence reveals how far she has withdrawn from a world in which every meaningful decision has already been taken away.

5. Since Lotte will not choose, Nawal dresses her in a modest black ensemble selected according to her own taste. The heavy wooden pillory has finally been removed, but freedom lasts only briefly: Nawal now holds the iron restraints that will replace it. She is not driven by simple cruelty, yet her fascination with submissive women, possession and restraint is unmistakable—and she intends to exercise it upon her husband’s gift.

6. Moments later, Lotte stands before Nawal with iron cuffs locked around her wrists and ankles. The restraints are less brutal than the wooden pillory, but their weight and short chains still restrict every movement and clearly define her new position within the household. Nawal studies her with growing interest, while Lotte remains distant and resigned, physically present yet still searching inwardly for some sign of Ingrid.

7. The narrative now shifts to Ingrid, who remains captive within Samira’s residence. As Samira bids farewell to her guest Layla, Ingrid waits silently beside them, displayed in an exquisite robe, golden restraints and an ornate mask as proof of her captor’s triumph. For a woman once accustomed to commanding obedience, such decorative servitude is profoundly humiliating—and Samira understands this perfectly. Yet Ingrid endures it because she believes every act of compliance helps keep Lotte safe.

8. Once the guest has departed, the glittering performance ends and the raw reality of captivity returns. Samira takes Ingrid into a neglected storeroom and maliciously presents the plain, coarse dress that will replace her magnificent costume. The beautiful European trophy displayed before company is now reduced to an ordinary household captive.

9. Dressed in the simple garment, Ingrid sits against a wooden post while Samira finishes securing her with broad leather straps. Samira’s cruel satisfaction reveals how much she enjoys the helplessness of another dominant woman, especially one who might once have regarded herself as an equal. Ingrid meets the humiliation with outward calm, preserving her strength by thinking only of Lotte and the safety her obedience is supposed to guarantee.

10. Exhaustion eventually allows Ingrid to fall asleep despite the restrictive straps and hard cellar floor. A soft, almost blissful smile appears upon her face—the only happiness captivity has permitted her. It belongs not to the room around her, but to a fragile dream of Lotte and the life they once shared.

11. Morning brings heavier iron restraints and a new series of commands. Kneeling before Samira, Ingrid is made to raise her face and look directly into her captor’s eyes while the day’s duties are explained. She does not flinch or lower her gaze; her body obeys, but the proud Mistress within her remains carefully hidden and intact.

12. At breakfast, Samira cannot resist transforming an ordinary meal into another demonstration of hierarchy. She eats comfortably from a richly laid table while Ingrid, shackled at her feet, receives coarse food upon the floor. Ingrid accepts the indignity in silence, still believing that every humiliation endured may buy another measure of safety for Lotte.

13. Later, Samira relaxes with her water pipe while ordering Ingrid to polish her tall black boots. The reversal is deliberately chosen: the former Mistress now kneels in chains, tending the symbols of another woman’s authority. Samira watches with quiet satisfaction, while Ingrid performs the task without offering her the emotional surrender she seeks.

14. Samira’s next command turns Ingrid into an instrument of her comfort. As her captor reclines with a book, the shackled Ingrid kneels beside her and works a large hand fan. The duty appears almost peaceful, yet its stillness conceals the same calculated humiliation—Samira rests because the woman she has conquered must labor.

15. Before leaving for the city, Samira secures Ingrid against the wall with her wrists raised, ankles shackled and eyes covered by a broad leather blindfold. Dressed in her conservative black public robes, she offers an ironic farewell wave to a woman who cannot see it. Ingrid is left to wait in darkness, able to hear Samira depart but powerless to know when—or with whom—she will return.

16. For the last time in this part, the narrative returns to Lotte. Nawal orders her shackled captive to kneel, but instead of demanding service, she invites the previously silent woman to tell her story. As Nawal listens, her curiosity gives way to genuine sympathy: Lotte is slowly becoming more than a private plaything in her eyes—a wounded woman with a past, a lost love, and emotions of her own. Yet this awakening compassion has its limits, and Lotte’s restraints remain firmly in place.

17. The scene moves to the bath, where Nawal asks Lotte to wash her back. Lotte obeys, beginning to regard her new Mistress with cautious relief; although she remains confined, Nawal treats her with a decency she has not known during the brutal days since her capture.

18. After the bath, Nawal’s changing attitude becomes visible in a small but meaningful concession. She replaces Lotte’s heavy, uncomfortable irons with more elegant and comfortable restraints, personally fastening the ornate cuffs around her wrists and ankles. It is an act of consideration, though not freedom—Nawal softens the conditions of Lotte’s captivity without surrendering her control.

19. Lotte now faces her first test of life within the household: serving Nawal and the long-established women of the harem while still shackled. Concentrating intensely, she struggles with movements made awkward by her chains, while the other women laugh at the European newcomer’s clumsiness, forgetting how difficult their own beginnings once were. Amid their amusement, Nawal offers Lotte a quiet, encouraging gaze—as if promising that she will learn, adapt, and eventually find her place.

20. Later that evening, the Sheikh asks his wife whether she is satisfied with his costly gift and whether Lotte has shown proper obedience and respect. His presence deeply unsettles Lotte, reminding her of the auction, the brutal journey in the wooden pillory, and the men who have caused her so much suffering. Sensing her distress, Nawal draws her close with an arm around her shoulders—not as a gesture of possession, but of protection, silently assuring her that she is safe beside her.

21. At the end of the long day, Nawal gives Lotte a modest room of her own. The restraints remain, and a long chain secures her to the bed, but she is granted privacy and enough freedom of movement for her basic needs—a mercy far removed from the cold cellars and storerooms she has come to fear. As Nawal gently covers her with a blanket, kindness and the first trace of deeper attachment appear in her expression; Lotte responds with quiet gratitude, increasingly aware that her new Mistress may not be the monster she expected. Here we leave Lotte for now—but her story, and the strange bond beginning to form between these two women, is far from over.

22. For the last time in this part, the narrative returns to Ingrid. Samira arrives home from the city accompanied by her brother Malik—the man who secretly took Lotte to the slave auction despite Samira’s promise to keep her safe in exchange for Ingrid’s obedience. Still blindfolded and chained to the wall, Ingrid hears only approaching footsteps, laughter, and unfamiliar words, unaware that her fragile illusion of Lotte’s safety is about to be destroyed.

23. Once the blindfold is removed, Ingrid recognizes Malik as the man she briefly met during her last visit to Samira’s house with Lotte. She does not yet know what happened after their separation or the part he played in her beloved’s fate. Anticipating a violent reaction to the truth, Samira secures Ingrid’s wrists behind her back and binds her arms and body tightly with broad leather straps before allowing Malik to speak.

24. Malik now reveals everything: the journey to the city, the auction, and the wealthy Sheikh who purchased Lotte. With cruel pride, he empties the purse of gold he received onto the table, turning the price of Lotte’s suffering into a display of his own success. For the first time, Ingrid’s strength finally breaks; unable to bear the truth about the woman she loves, she sinks into helpless tears.

25. Bound tightly and emptied of resistance, Ingrid lies on the carpet while Samira and Malik divide the gold earned from Lotte’s sale. The image draws its cruelty from the stark contrast between Ingrid’s silent grief and the satisfied smiles of the siblings, who reduce another woman’s ruined life to neat stacks of shining coins.

26. Pleased with his profit, Malik takes his leave and shares an affectionate farewell with his sister. Samira keeps one hand firmly on Ingrid’s arm while watching him depart, but Ingrid barely reacts. The revelation has pushed her beyond tears into a state of numb resignation, her expression distant and extinguished.

27. Once Malik is gone, grief gives way to fury. Still bound and kneeling, Ingrid confronts Samira over her betrayal, denouncing the broken promise and declaring that she will never willingly serve, obey, or humble herself before her again. Samira remains outwardly calm, yet realizes that her most powerful weapon is gone: from now on, only physical restraints can hold Ingrid under her control.

28. Recovering quickly from this setback, Samira decides to force the obedience she can no longer obtain through deception. Ingrid is taken to a cellar storeroom and secured to a tall wooden cross, her outstretched wrists, body, and ankles held by strong leather straps while her feet remain on the floor. Samira makes her terms unmistakably clear—Ingrid will remain there until she capitulates and promises obedience—but Ingrid answers only with contemptuous silence.

29. Night settles over the storeroom, illuminated only by a pale shaft of moonlight entering through the small window. Exhaustion eventually pulls Ingrid into sleep, but there is no trace of the peaceful smile she wore the previous night. Her head hangs heavily and her rest is tormented by fear for Lotte, whose unknown fate now haunts even her dreams.

30. In the morning, Samira returns carrying a pitcher of water and offers Ingrid one final choice: submission in exchange for relief. Thirsty, exhausted, and soaked with perspiration, Ingrid nevertheless refuses with the same determined silence. Laughing at her defiance, Samira slowly pours the water onto the stone floor, allowing it to form a small pool before her helpless captive. Thus Part III closes with Ingrid’s fate as uncertain as Lotte’s—not with surrender, but with a silent and unresolved battle of wills.

text:
The War in Iran.
War, being the only remaining option against Iran, should be treated as a case of offer and acceptance.
The United States and Israel did not invent this war out of boredom. They accepted an offer the IRGC had already placed on the table: years of proxy war, missile build-up, and a nuclear programme pursued behind a fog of talks. Iran refused a viable peace and systematically reneged on the arrangements it had already entered. When a party does that long enough, the other party is entitled to treat the contract as broken.
It is fair to add that Washington has put real economic offers in front of Tehran — the kind that would have improved the country’s outlook if ordinary Iranians were allowed to feel the benefit. Those offers were rebuffed by the ruling elite precisely because a freer economy would weaken the system that keeps the Guards in power. Relief for the public is a threat to the clique that lives off isolation and fear.
The rest of the noise is a distraction. The core of the matter is the IRGC’s attempt to assemble a nuclear arsenal with which it can keep bullying its neighbours, set against Israel’s and America’s attempt to stop that from happening. Call it whatever diplomatic name you like. That is the bargain Iran offered, and that is the bargain now being answered.
Let us be clear on this. A state that uses negotiations as cover, rejects economic openings that would help its own people, and keeps reaching for the one weapon that would make its intimidation permanent has already chosen war. Accepting that offer is not the same thing as having started the argument.

text:
You can buy my face in any night market in South East Asia, printed on a cotton Tshirt, right next to Che Guevara and Bob Marley.

So what am I?

A revolutionary hero? A founding father? Or an icon flattened into a souvenir?

It's funny. People think of me as an ideologue. They think I sat in a cold room in Paris reading Marx, built a movement out of pure doctrine, and brought down an empire using political theory.

That's not what happened.

I didn't start with doctrine. I started with a simple, brutal observation: my country didn't belong to us. French rubber plantations ran on crushed bones. Taxes ate the harvest before it hit the dirt. If a Vietnamese man raised his head, he went to Poulo Condore prison in chains.

So I went looking for help.

I didn't go to Moscow first. I went to London. I washed dishes at the Carlton Hotel. I swept snow in Paris. I wrote letters to Woodrow Wilson in 1919 asking for basic civil rights for my people under French rule.

He didn't even reply.

The Western democracies talked about self determination, but they meant self determination for white Europeans. The imperial powers were never going to vote to dismantle their own empires.

So who offered to help end colonial rule?

Lenin. 

That's the part people miss. I didn't embrace communism because I was obsessed with Soviet economic theory. I embraced it because the Third International was the only international organization willing to support anti colonial movements. Communism was a vehicle. Nationalism was the engine.

So, does that mean I just used communism as a tool?

It's not that simple. You can't use a tool for 50 years without it shaping the way you build.

To win a war against a global power, you can't just have angry peasants. Angry peasants get slaughtered. You need organization. You need absolute discipline. You need a structure that operates underground, survives torture, replaces dead leaders overnight, and coordinates a million invisible moving parts. The Leninist party model offered exactly that. It turned a loose national desire for freedom into a military machine.

Without that machine, we couldn't have beaten the French at Dien Bien Phu. We couldn't have survived the American carpet bombing.

But what happens when you build a machine like that?

It doesn't just fight the enemy. It eats its own society.

To keep that machine running, we eliminated alternatives. We didn't just fight French soldiers and American troops; we crushed rival Vietnamese nationalists. Non communist patriots who wanted a free Vietnam were assassinated, jailed, or driven into exile. During the land reforms in the North in the 1950s, we unleashed class hatred that got thousands of innocent peasants executed by public tribunals.

We wanted to free our people, yet we created a system where speaking against the party became treason.

So was I a liberator or a dictator?

Both. You can't separate the two.

The liberation of Vietnam required total mobilization. Total mobilization required total control. The very discipline that saved the country from foreign rule created an authoritarian state that outlived the war by decades.

And look at what happened after I died.

I explicitly asked in my line of instructions to be cremated. I wanted my ashes scattered on three hills across Vietnam, one in the North, one in the Centre, one in the South. I wanted to save farmland and avoid useless monument building.

What did the party do?

They preserved my corpse in a glass box in Hanoi. They built a massive granite mausoleum using Soviet architects. They turned my body into a holy relic to legitimize their own absolute power.

I spent my life trying to end the worship of foreign masters, and my successors turned me into a idol that no one is allowed to criticize.

Today, Vietnam is unified and independent. That was the dream, and it succeeded. But to keep that independence, the current government hosts American warships, opens sweatshops for foreign corporations, and jails bloggers who demand the same civil rights I asked Woodrow Wilson for a century ago.

The irony is complete.

I helped my people gain their country back, but in the process, we built a state that ensured they couldn't fully own themselves.

text:
In Nigeria, The Battle For Votes Is Getting Uncomfortably Personal

Nigerian politics has produced another episode that would almost sound ridiculous if the allegations were not so disturbing. A young man identified as Madu says his decision to publicly support an opposition candidate allegedly ended with him being forced into a vehicle, taken to the private residence of a serving Ebonyi commissioner and subjected to a brutal assault.

Madu alleges that four men identified as Ikechukwu Egede, Emmanuel Nwambe, Okwy Nwambe and Ogeje Kingsley accosted him and forced him into a Toyota Sienna after he refused to go with them voluntarily. He says they took him to the residence of Commissioner Oguzorkanu Offia-Nwali, where the matter apparently became less about politics and more about making sure he understood the consequences of having political preferences of his own.

According to Madu, the commissioner confronted him over a video in which he had expressed support for Rollins, the commissioner’s brother, who is contesting a State House of Assembly seat under the NDC. Madu says he explained that his comments were directed at poorly performing politicians generally and that he supported Rollins because he believed he could offer better governance.

That explanation, he alleges, did not exactly calm the room.

Madu claims the commissioner then attacked him personally, kicking his face, slamming his head against the floor, repeatedly slapping him around the eyes and stomping on his head while he was pinned down. Another video circulating online appears to show Madu on the floor with the commissioner’s leg over him, while the men who allegedly brought him remain nearby.

Because apparently, in this particular political drama, the ballot box was not considered sufficient.
