text:
Gerald Ford, the 38th President of the United States, was a genuine football star who turned down the NFL, and later a professional fashion model, yet he's mostly remembered as a clumsy klutz. That last part is the great injustice of his life. In college at Michigan, Ford was so good that he played on two national championship teams and got contract offers from both the Green Bay Packers and the Detroit Lions. He turned them both down to go to law school instead. He was probably the single most athletic man ever to become President.

On top of that, he worked as a male model. In the 1940s he modeled for a top agency, appeared in a Look magazine ski feature with his fashion-model girlfriend, and even landed on the cover of Cosmopolitan in his Navy uniform. The future President was cover-model handsome.

So it's almost cruel that his public image became "the clumsy guy." He happened to stumble a couple of times on camera, most famously slipping down the wet steps of Air Force One, and comedian Chevy Chase turned it into a running joke on Saturday Night Live. The most gifted athlete to ever hold the office got branded as a bumbling oaf, and it stuck.

He also has a distinction no other President can claim: he was never actually elected to the job, or to the vice presidency either. Nixon's VP resigned in scandal, so Nixon appointed Ford as Vice President. Then Nixon himself resigned over Watergate, and Ford became President. He rose to the two highest offices in the country without ever winning a national election for either one.

And in a wild stretch of just 17 days in 1975, two different women separately tried to assassinate him, one a follower of cult leader Charles Manson. Both attempts were foiled by bystanders, and Ford was unharmed both times.

So the real Gerald Ford: a national-champion athlete who turned down the NFL, a Cosmopolitan cover model, the only President never elected President or VP, and a man who survived two assassination attempts in under three weeks, all while being mocked as a klutz.

That's a President.

text:
I've tried more than two dozen different psychedelics over the years, and every single one has taught me something unique and special that I don't think any of the others could have.

The way I always describe 5-MEO-DMT is that it's essentially the polar opposite of N,N-DMT. Not opposite in a bad way, just opposite as in two things that balance each other out perfectly.

If DMT is the positive polarity - whose experience is defined by the spatial depth and three-dimensionality of the highly articulated visual experience it induces, 5-MEO-DMT is comparatively nonvisual.

DMT is an experience of infinite connection, 5-MEO-DMT strips everything away, instead.

This feeling of experiencing "the void", which is the polar opposite of DMT's "hyperspace", is so common that it's even mentioned on the Erowid page where it describes the effects.

When my eyes were open, the visual effects I experienced were closer to psilocybin in some ways, more morphing and distorting, some color shifting, and a feeling of seeing in "high-def", that can also happen with psilocybin or DMT. Not really flooded with shifting colorful fractals as much as other psychedelics.

Many people describe seeing a white light, when my eyes were closed, I saw the white light mix with the black of the inside of my eyelids, and form dancing shadows in shades of gray.

There was still some shifting three-dimensionality, but the experience was like seeing dancing shadows in an expansive void rather than swimming in a cosmic sea full of things like you'd experience with DMT.

I suppose you could think of the void state induced by 5-MEO-DMT as essentially close to a state of Buddhist Nirvana, a state of complete and total detachment which allows for total inner peace. This total Nirvana-like detachment from all things has often been described as dissociating for that reason.

There are of course positive and negative aspects to taking the shortcut to Nirvana though, because the mind does tend to hold on to its attachments rather tightly and it can cause some distress if you're unwilling to let go. This is the reason why I describe it as sometimes having a cold, hard edge to it as well.

But diving head first into that space can also teach you many things about yourself and the nature of life if you're willing to take that plunge and dive in head first.

I would say it should still be on the list of essential bucket list psychedelics for a psychonaut who really wants to experience the full depth and range of what psychedelia has to offer, but definitely buckle up for that one, because 5-MEO-DMT can definitely be a doozie.

I think the reason why I don' t like 5-MEO-DMT is because a lot of my personal issues boil down to having difficulty connecting with people, which is something psychedelics have greatly helped with. 5-MEO-DMT kind of feels like going backwards for me because its core feature is total Nirvanic disconnection.

Different things affect different people differently. Your mileage may vary.

text:
80-yrs on, the broadcast that changed history: How Neville Chamberlain told Britain it was at war with Germany

The BBC radio announcer who introduces the broadcast with the historic line, 'This is London...'

Neville Chamberlain - Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, delivering the official declaration of war from the Cabinet Room at 10 Downing Street on 3 Sep 1939.

✲ Announcer: 'This is London, you'ill now hear a statement by the Prime Minister.'

✲ Neville Chamberlain: 'I am speaking to you from the Cabinet Room at 10 Downing Street. This morning, the British Ambassador in Berlin handed the German government a final note stating that unless we heard from them by 11 o'clock that they were prepared at once to withdraw their troops from Poland, a state of war would exist b/w us. I have to tell you now that no such u/taking has been received, and that consequently, this country is at war with Germany.

You can imagine what a bitter blow it is to me that all my long struggle to win peace has failed. Yet I cannot believe that there is anything more or anything different that I could have done and that it would have been more successful.

Up to the very last, it would have been quite possible to have arranged a peaceful and honourable settlement b/w Germany and Poland. But Hitler would not have it. He had evidently made up his mind to attack Poland whatever happened. And although he now says he put forward reasonable proposals which were rejected by the Poles, that is not a true statement. The proposals were never shown to the Poles, nor to us. And though they were announced in the German broadcast on Thursday night, Hitler did not wait to hear comments on them, but ordered his troops to cross the Polish frontier the next morning'

✲ Why this moment matters ?
• End of appeasement: Chamberlain had spent 3-yrs pursuing a policy of appeasement to avoid another world war, most famously signing the Munich Agreement in 1938 - the broadcast was his public admission that the strategy had collapsed.

• Trigger - Invasion of Poland: Germany invaded Poland on 1 Sep 1939. Britain and France had a mutual defence pact with Poland. Chamberlain's ultimatum gave Hitler until 11 AM on 3 Sep to withdraw and the deadline passed with no response.

• Medium is the message: For the first time in British history, war was declared not in Parliament first, but directly to the public via radio. At 11:15 AM, millions of British families heard it live on the BBC Home Service - it made the war instantly personal and national.

• Hitler's deception: Chamberlain directly refutes Nazi propaganda. Germany claimed Poland rejected a reasonable peace offer. Chamberlain clarifies the proposals were never actually presented to Poland or Britain and were broadcast only as cover while troops were already ordered to cross the border.

This 2-min address marked the beginning of World War II for Britain and the Commonwealth.

Rico, this isn’t analysis. It’s a relocation ad with a siren on it. You’re “The Cyprus Guy.” You sell tax setups and off-plan. Fine business. Just don’t dress the sales funnel as a morality lecture about “brainwashed” Nordics. 🤡😂

You lumped Norway, Finland and Denmark in with Sweden’s gang problem and then sold sunshine + 15%. That’s the whole trick.

Where the Nordics actually smash Cyprus

•  Happiness: Finland #1 for the 9th year. 

Denmark and Iceland right behind. Sweden and Norway still top 6. Cyprus sits around the low 60s with a score ~6.1 vs ~7.5. If that’s “brainwashed,” the brainwashing is remarkably consistent across decades of surveys.

•  Corruption: Denmark and Finland are #1–2 on Transparency International. Norway/Sweden ~80. Cyprus ~55 and mid-table. Funny how the “scam government” countries keep winning the clean-government contest.

•  Peace/safety (GPI): Denmark and Finland live in the global top 10-ish. Cyprus is closer to 70–80. Sweden has a real gang problem. That is not “the Nordics.” Stop photocopying Malmö onto Helsinki and Aarhus.

•  Sexual offence stats: Sweden’s reported numbers are high because the legal definition is broad, every incident is counted separately, and people actually report. Brå has said for years the raw EU ranking is not a like-for-like crime rate. Using that chart as a “don’t let your kids walk home” scare is textbook ragebait.

•  Education: PISA. Cyprus is tens of points behind the EU average and falling, despite spending a fat share of the budget on schools. Finland/Denmark/Estonia still punch in a different league. “Top tier schools” is a brochure line, not a scoreboard.

•  HDI / institutions / trust: Nordics sit at the very top of human development. Cyprus is “very high” and still a clear step down. High tax + high trust + public registers is not a glitch. It’s how a high-trust society works. Your 50M client leaving because his address is findable is a niche rich-person problem, not a diagnosis of 27 million people.

•  Money you can actually spend: Danish net pay and purchasing power still crush Cyprus for normal salaries. Low headline tax is nice if you have a company and a non-dom cert. Most people are not you.

Cyprus wins weather, winters, and a sweet non-dom package for mobile entrepreneurs. That’s a real offer. Own it. What you don’t get to do is pretend Denmark is a failed state because January is dark and the tax receipt is itemised.
Nordics are not “working half the year for free.” They’re buying a state that mostly works, schools that mostly work, hospitals that mostly work, and the boring luxury of not having to rent a villa in Paphos to feel the government isn’t picking their pocket and falling apart.

You felt unsafe zero times in seven years. Good. Denmark’s homicide rate is still in the same low band as Cyprus. The difference is you need Sweden’s grenades to make the pitch land.

text:
St. Stephen, King of Hungary from Lives of the Saints by Father Francis Xavier Weninger, DD, SJ., 1876.
.
St. Stephen, who is justly called the Apostle of the Hungarians, on account of his unwearied zeal in disseminating the true faith, was born in Hungary. His father, Geisa, was a renowned leader and general of the wild Huns and ruled over them with the title of Duke. Severely as he treated his heathen subjects, he was mild to the Christians who came into his dominions, and when God had bestowed upon him the grace of recognizing the truth of the Christian religion, he determined to establish it in his land. One day, when, occupied with this thought, he laid himself down, an angel appeared to him in his sleep, who announced to him that he would become father to a son, who was chosen by God to execute all that he was just now revolving in his mind. The angel further said, that on the following day, a messenger of God would come to him, whom he should receive, and to whose words he should listen with due reverence. A similar vision was shown, at the same time, to the wife of Geisa. St. Stephen, the protomartyr, appeared to her, and, among other things, told her to give his name to the child to whom she was soon to give birth. St. Adalbert, bishop of Prague, arrived on the following day. He instructed the duke and duchess in the truth and baptized them. The prince who was soon afterwards born, was joyfully received into the Church of the Lord by the holy bishop, who gave him, in Baptism, the name of Stephen. Geisa led an edifying life until he died.
.
When Stephen had arrived at manhood, and had taken the reins of government, he resolved most earnestly, to exterminate all idolatry among his people, and everywhere to plant the emblem of the Christians, the Cross. To be more secure in his pious undertaking, he formed an alliance with the neighboring princes in order to prevent them from assisting those of his subjects who might oppose his design. Notwithstanding this, some of the Hungarian nobility dared to take up arms in defense of idolatry, and to make war against their legitimate Lord. St. Stephen, full of trust in the Almighty, met the rebels with his small force and defeated them so completely, that in future none ever dared refuse him obedience. The great and rich booty of which St. Stephen became possessed on this occasion, he appropriated to the building of a Monastery in honor of St. Martin, a native of Hungary. The Saint then invited from different Catholic lands, priests and religious men to Hungary to instruct the people.
.
Those who were converted were favored with many privileges and immunities by the devout prince, while the refractory were dealt with in such a manner, that they were prevented from opposing others in embracing Christianity. In various cities and villages he erected Churches and Chapels, endowing them all richly. The number of the faithful grew in a short time so much, that he divided Hungary into ten dioceses, to all of which he endeavored to give holy bishops. He sent a certain bishop Anastasius to Rome, to request the Pope to confirm all he had done for the propagation of the Christian faith, and also to beg the holy Father to proclaim him King, so that he would be invested with greater power, happily to conclude the conversion of the entire country. During the night on which Anastasius arrived at Rome, an Angel informed the Pope of St. Stephen's request, and commanded him to give to the Saint's ambassador the crown which he had designed for another prince. Inexpressibly rejoiced at everything that Anastasius related to him, the Pope confirmed what St. Stephen had done to disseminate the faith of Christ, and granted him the privilege to act further as he and his bishops thought the welfare of the Church demanded. He also sent him the crown and a cross of gold which should be carried before him after the coronation.
.
No sooner had Anastasius returned, than St. Stephen was solemnly anointed and crowned as first King of Hungary. After this he married Gisela, the sister of the holy emperor Henry, a princess not less talented than pious, who assisted him most assiduously in all his virtuous undertakings. Besides St. Stephen's apostolic zeal in spreading the true faith, his charity and generosity deserved the admiration of the world. He was almost prodigal in distributing alms, and spared neither his own garments nor the royal treasures. He often washed the feet of the poor, visited the hospitals during the night and served the sick. Many hours of the night he passed so devoutly in prayer, that he frequently went into ecstasy and was raised high above the earth. The hours of the day he devoted most earnestly to the affairs of the government, and every one of his subjects had free access to him. He indulged neither in hunting, gaming, nor other similar amusements, giving all his time to the administration of the state and devout exercises; "for," said he, "they are more pleasing to me than hunting, gaming and whatever else may amuse a king."
.
Towards the Queen of heaven, whom he called "My Lady," he was most devout from his tender youth and he chose her as patroness of Hungary. To her honor he built a most magnificent temple at Alba, where he resided. He built churches in her honor in several cities not in his dominions, as at Jerusalem, at Rome and at Constantinople, and to these he attached large convents. Hence, it is not surprising that the divine Mother protected her faithful servant, as the following events will prove. When the emperor Conrad II. invaded Hungary with his army, St. Stephen humbly begged his holy patroness to take him under her mighty protection. Then, at the head of his army, he went to meet the much stronger forces of the enemy. The following day, when everyone expected that a battle would take place, an imperial message arrived, ordering all the generals of the emperor's army to retreat without showing any hostility to the Hungarians. In this manner, the king won a bloodless victory, which he gratefully ascribed to his heavenly patroness.
.
In truth, the Queen of heaven had rescued him; for, the emperor knew nothing of the message nor the order it contained, and when his generals showed him his own hand and seal, he was convinced that St. Stephen was under the protection of a higher power, and marched away with his forces. At another time, four of the most distinguished noblemen entered into a plot against the holy king, and one of them came into the royal apartment during the night, to murder him. On entering, the dagger, which he had concealed under his cloak, fell upon the floor, and the noise of it aroused the king, who was sick. He asked who was there, and the man, trembling with fear, cast himself at his feet, discovered the plot, and entreated his pardon. Stephen recognized again the motherly protection of the Blessed Virgin, and out of love for her, pardoned him, but committed his accomplices into the hands of justice.
Speaking of the sickness of the holy king, we must not omit to relate that God visited his servant, notwithstanding his fidelity and zeal, with great sorrows. He sent him a sickness which lasted three years, and what was still more painful, deprived him, by an early death, of all his children except one son. St. Stephen brought up this son, who was called Emeric, with the greatest care, and wrote, with his own hand, several instructions for him which he desired him to observe. Foremost among these were, that he should remain faithful to the Catholic faith, protect and disseminate it; that he should show due honor and obedience to the clergy; that he should cherish his subjects; attend to his prayers with fervor; be generous to the poor and suffering; deal out justice, and submit himself in adversity to the will of the Almighty. Emeric manifested in his conduct that he endeavored to live according to these holy precepts, and thus gave inexpressible peace and comfort to his father. The king daily begged the Almighty to preserve the life of this beloved son, that the Christian faith might have a protector in him. But this son also, whose holy life was an example of all Christian virtues, was destined to die before his father's eyes, whose grief was too great for words; but greater still was his heroic resignation to the will of the Most High. He even conquered himself so far as to thank God that He had called his beloved son before him into the Kingdom of heaven.
.
The holy son was soon followed by the holy father. When his last hour, which God revealed to him, approached, he devoutly received the holy Sacraments, and then exhorted the bishops and the first men of the state to Christian charity and union; to rule with justice; to remain true to their faith; and not only take the utmost care to protect this, the only faith instituted by Christ, but also to propagate it more and more. After this, the dying Saint turned his eyes to God and his blessed patroness, Mary, and addressing the latter, he said: "To thee, O Queen of heaven, and to thy guardianship, I commend the holy Church, all the bishops and the clergy, the whole kingdom, its rulers and inhabitants; but before all, I commend my soul to thy care." In such devout sentiments, he died, on the festival of the Assumption of Our Lady, his greatly venerated patroness. He was truly a great king, adorned with all the virtues of a Christian. His holy body gave out a heavenly fragrance, and the health of many infirm was restored by touching the sacred relics. The hand with which the holy king had distributed so many generous alms, and which had done so many acts of kindness to the sick and the unfortunate, remained incorrupt long after his death.
.
PRACTICAL CONSIDERATIONS
.
I. The whole life of St. Stephen shows that he labored much for the honor of God and the spiritual and temporal welfare of man; and that he bore the crosses God laid upon him with Christian patience. For all this he now receives his reward in heaven: because his intentions were always holy, and his heart was free from sin. If you desire to be rewarded for your good works, and for what you do and suffer, your intentions, while working and suffering, must be good. But at the same time, you must be in a state of grace; for, the holy church teaches: first, that we can earn a reward from God through our good works, because God has promised to recompense them.
.
Secondly; that we can gain heaven, or an eternal reward in heaven by our good works, if they are performed in the proper manner. The judgment which Christ pronounces on the last day when He will invite the just to take possession of the heavenly kingdom as a recompense for their good works, is sufficient proof of this. It is, however, also necessary to know that we must be in a state of grace, that is, not burdened with a mortal sin, if we desire to obtain heaven by our good works; for, the grace of God is the root of all supernatural merits. When we perform our labors, or suffer, in a state of disgrace, in a mortal sin, we cannot expect, for such work or suffering, a reward in heaven, however good the works, or however bitter the suffering may have been. "And if I should distribute all my goods to feed the poor and have no charity, it profiteth me nothing," to gain an eternal reward. Thus writes St Paul (i. Cor. xiii.). Hence, if you desire an eternal reward for your works and your sufferings, take heed that you may be constantly in a state of grace.
.
II. The holy king continued his good works and his patient suffering in a state of grace until his last hour. Hence he now enjoys an eternal reward. Had he, in the last year, nay, even in the last hour of his life, committed a mortal sin and died in it, he would not have received a recompense in heaven either for his good works, or his sufferings. For, the true faith teaches that, by committing a mortal sin, we lose all the merits of the good works we had previously performed. The words of God testify to the truth of this: "But if the just man turn himself from his justice and do iniquity all his justice which he hath done shall not be remembered and in his sin he shall die." (Ezekiel, xviii.)
.
Learn from this what harm may be done by one mortal sin, and how earnestly we should endeavor to avoid it. If you were sure that you would lose all you possess, for which you have labored many years with care and pains, if you committed a mortal sin, tell me, would you consent to do it? Most assuredly, you would not, unless you had lost all your good sense. Why then do you commit sin so wantonly when you are assured that you will thereby lose much greater possessions, even the entire treasure of your merits? Is not this loss and the loss of heaven much more to be considered than that of all your temporal possessions? Ah, consider this earnestly, and be not your own enemy; do not injure yourself. "They that commit sin and iniquity, are enemies to their own souls." (Tobias, xii.)
.
What has been said above is for every one; but the following words are especially for those parents whom death early deprives of their children. Many are sad at this, they murmur and complain against God. They ought to remember the conduct of the holy king Stephen, when he lost his beloved, kind and pious son; and they should endeavor to imitate him. That they should grieve or weep when death takes a child from them, is no sin, provided they remain within the limits of Christian patience and resignation. But to grieve immoderately, and to murmur and complain against God, is sinful. Tell me, you sad father, you weeping mother, who is it that has taken your child from you? Is it not God, the Lord over the life and death of all men? Does not your child belong more to the Almighty than to you? Does He wrong you by taking it from you? Not in the least. He is the Lord and Creator; He can take His own whenever He likes. Or shall He first ask your permission? Shall He account to you why He does it?
.
I trust that you do not entertain so unreasonable a thought. Why then do you murmur and complain against your God? You must know that what God did, was done either out of love for the child, or, from love to you. Perhaps God, reading the future knew that by your immoderate love or the bad education you would give to your child, you would draw upon yourself eternal misery. Perhaps He saw that your child would become a slave to sin and vice, and lose heaven. Is it not, therefore a sign of love towards you and your child, that God took it early to Himself? You ought to rejoice at the happiness it has attained, if it died in innocence. Could you have procured for him greater felicity? It ought surely to be enough for you to know that God demanded your child. The Lord called it away. What more can you require? If you will act sensibly, submit to the decrees of Providence, and confess before God, that you subject your will to His. Offer to Him the grief that death has caused you, and remember that all that God does is well done. Say with Holy Writ: "It is the Lord, let him do what is good in his sight." (1 Kings iii.)

الحمدللہ، #KRBT  کو یہ شرف حاصل ہے کہ ہم نے مارچ اپریل میں اس قومی پلان کو ایکسپوز کرنا شروع کیا۔ اُس  وقت بہت لوگ ہمارے اوپر بھونکے اور شور مچایا کہ ہم خان صاحب کی بہنوں پر الزام لگا رہے ہیں۔ تب بھی ہم نے بہنوں کو یہی بتایا کہ اس دو نمبر عسکری حکومت سے کنارہ کشی اختیار کر لیں، یہ خان کو بیچ رہے ہیں اور آپ کا کندھا استعمال کر رہے ہیں

مگر سوشل میڈیا پر بیٹھے فوجی ٹاؤٹوں نے اسے ایسے پھیلایا کہ ہم خان صاحب کی بہنوں کی بے حرمتی کر رہے ہیں۔ ایسا کچھ نہیں تھا۔ ہم بہنوں کو بتا رہے تھے کہ ان کے ساتھ بڑی سازش رچی جا رہی ہے اور ان کا کندھا استعمال ہو رہا ہے۔

اس لیے اس عسکری پی ٹی آئی کو، ان عسکری دگردلوں، بے غیرتوں، فسادیوں، دو نمبر، بکے ہوئے لوگوں اور عسکری کنجروں کو چھوڑ دیں۔ کیونکہ یہ آپ کا کندھا استعمال کر کے قومی حکومت، جو فوج کی دیرینہ خواہش ہے، اس پر کام کر رہے ہیں۔ یہ وہی کریں گے جو ان عسکری بے شرموں  فوج بتائے گی

آج آپ دیکھیں، آٹھ مہینے خان صاحب کو آئیسولیٹ رکھا گیا، کسی سے ملنے نہیں دیا گیا، اذیتیں پہنچائی گئیں۔ عسکری پی ٹی آئی کا مقصد خان صاحب کی رہائی نہیں، بلکہ نعوذ باللہ، زندہ بھٹو، یا پھر نعوذ باللہ، خان صاحب کو جانی نقصان پہچانے کا پلان ہے۔

عسکری پی ٹی آئی پوری طرح فوج کے ساتھ ملی ہوئی ہے۔ پچھلے چند دنوں کے واقعات دیکھ لیں، یہ B1 Scenario  چل رہا ہے جس کا ہم نے تین چار مہینے پہلے ذکر کیا تھا، جس پر ہمارے اورپر چند سوشل میڈیا پر فوج کے بیٹھے ٹاؤٹ  بھونکے اور شور مچایا

اس وقت بھی ہمارا مؤقف یہی تھا کہ اس حرام خور قیادت کو مائنس کر دیا جائے، مگر کسی نے ہماری نہ سنی۔ آج یہ کھل کے سامنے آ گئے ہیں۔

یہ سندھ گیا نہیں ہے، یہ لانگ مارچ جھوٹا ہے، یہ سب فراڈ، سب دو نمبر ہے۔ یہ سندھ لائے گئے ہیں تاکہ پیپلز پارٹی پر پریشر ڈالا جا سکے۔ دیے گئے کلپس سے آپ کو اندازہ ہوگا کہ یہ سارا کھیل خان کی رہائی نہیں قومی حکومت بنانے کا پلان ہے اور عسکری PTI اس کی پوری سہولت کاری کر  رہی ہے 

یاد رہے اگر یہ غدار قومی حکومت بنانے میں اگر کامیاب ہو گئے تو آسم  منیر صدارت کے عہدے پر بیٹھ کے اگلے دس سال تک اس ملک پر قبضہ رکھے گا

🆘 یہ قومی حکومت خان کی زندگی اور رہائی پر بہت بڑا حملہ ہے 

🆘 یہ پلان لندن سے کھیلا جا رہا ہے جہاں فوجی اور سیاسی غدار اکٹھے ہو رہے ہیں

کارکنان سے گزارش ہے، اب بھی سمجھ جائیں، اس سے پہلے کہ دیر ہو جائے۔ یہ پاکستان کو ٹکڑوں میں بانٹ کر خان صاحب کو اگلے دس سال تک غائب یا نظر بند کر دیں گے۔ نعوذ باللہ، خان صاحب کو جانی نقصان بھی پہنچا سکتے ہیں

خدا کا واسطہ ہے، اس عسکری پی ٹی آئی کے جھانسے میں مت آئیں۔ یہ جو کچھ بھی کر رہے ہیں، فوج کے حکم کے مطابق کر رہے ہیں۔ یہ اٹھتے، بیٹھتے، بولتے اور گھر سے نکلتے بھی فوج کے حکم سے ہیں۔ یہ لوگ فوج نے لائے ہیں اور فوج کے لیے بیٹھے ہیں

ان کا سر سے پاؤں تک انگ انگ کرپشن میں ڈوبا ہوا ہے۔ یہ خان کو کبھی رہا نہیں ہونے دیں گے۔ خان کی رہائی ان حرام خوروں کی سیاسی موت اور ان کی حرام کی دولت کے اوپر لات ہے

اس لیے پاکستانیوں، کارکنان اکٹھے ہو جائیں اور اس لانگ مارچ کا بائیکاٹ کریں۔ یہ اسلام آباد جا کے کچھ نہیں کرنے جا رہے۔ خان صاحب نے لانگ مارچ سے منع کیا۔

اپ دیکھیے گا جوں ہی قومی حکومت کا گرین سگنل ملے گا، آپ دیکھیے گا یہ لانگ مارچ ہوا میں تحلیل ہو جائے گا۔ آپ کو پتہ بھی نہیں چلے گا کہ کون سا لانگ مارچ، کیسا لانگ مارچ۔

یہ عسکری PTI والے جب منہ کھولتے ہیں، جھوٹ بولتے ہیں

ان سے کنارہ کشی اختیار کریں اور خود لیڈرلیس ہو کے نکلیں، جیسا کہ #KRBT  بار بار سمجھاتی رہی ہے

text:
Federal Government Can Lease Land to Data Centers 

The U.S. government has several active pathways for leasing federal land and buildings to data center developers:

Executive Order Push (Jan 2025): The Department of Defense and Department of Energy were directed to identify federal sites suitable for gigawatt-scale AI data centers. Both agencies now run competitive leasing processes, allowing private developers to build, own, and operate the infrastructure entirely at their own expense — not a grant program.

Enhanced Use Leases (EULs): Agencies like the Army use this long-standing authority to lease underutilized federal property to private parties for commercial development, including data centers. This tool predates the AI boom and offers a well-established legal framework.

BLM Entry: The Bureau of Land Management has moved directly into this space. In June 2026, it approved the Townsite Data Center — the first data center ever authorized on BLM-managed public land, opening a new category of federal acreage (largely in the West) to development.

GSA Leasing: The General Services Administration routinely leases excess or underutilized federal buildings and land to private tenants under its standing real property disposal/leasing authority. This is broader and older than the AI-specific push, applying to any qualifying federal asset.

This sudden increase in offer and shifting demographics  definetly will have an impact on existing real estate value, I think we can agree on this.

Answer: services… and here we go around and around and services become the only thing that everybody would agree upfront  because it is a win win for the locals and the becoming locals.

text:
Maria Bartiromo’s Departure Is a Loss for Viewers Who Care About Markets, America, and Straight Talk

Fox News Media announced Thursday that it has parted ways with Maria Bartiromo after 12 and a half years. 

The network offered the usual corporate thanks and no explanation. Her last Mornings with Maria aired that morning. The shows she built will continue under generic new titles with rotating hosts. 

That clinical language does not capture what Bartiromo actually delivered.

She arrived at Fox Business in 2014 after a long run at CNBC, where she had already become the first journalist to report live from the floor of the New York Stock Exchange every day. At Fox she anchored the pre-market hours that matter to people who work for a living, not just those who trade abstracts. Mornings with Maria became the top-rated pre-market business program on cable because it treated the economy as something real: jobs, energy, manufacturing, capital formation, and the policies that either grow them or choke them. 

She interviewed presidents, treasury secretaries, CEOs, and lawmakers without the performative hostility that too often passes for journalism. President Trump appeared on her programs frequently because she asked about growth, tariffs, energy independence, and China instead of reciting the week’s approved talking points. Those conversations were not partisan theater. They were about whether America would remain a place that makes things, pays its workers, and defends its technological edge.

Bartiromo also hosted Sunday Morning Futures on Fox News, one of the highest-rated Sunday public-affairs hours in cable. Week after week she put elected officials and policymakers on the record about spending, regulation, border security, and the strategic competition with the Chinese Communist Party. She did not pretend that “business news” exists in a vacuum separate from national strength. That is a patriotic instinct, not a partisan one.

Her Friday evening program, Maria Bartiromo’s Wall Street, gave viewers a closer look at companies and markets without the lecture. She treated investors and entrepreneurs as adults. In an era when large parts of the media treat American business as the villain, she treated it as the engine.

None of this made her universally loved. She drew criticism from the usual quarters for taking election-integrity questions seriously and for refusing to treat every Trump policy as a scandal. That is the price of covering the country as it actually exists rather than as coastal newsrooms prefer it to be.
Fox has every right to change its lineup. Networks do it all the time. But viewers who tuned in for unapologetic coverage of markets, American competitiveness, and the people who run the real economy just lost one of the few consistent voices doing that work at scale. Rotating anchors and rebranded titles will not automatically replace the relationships, the institutional knowledge, or the willingness to let guests finish a sentence about growth instead of identity.

Bartiromo’s next chapter is hers to write. The record she leaves is clear: she spent more than a decade putting American economic strength, job creators, and national interest on television when much of the industry preferred other stories. 

That contribution does not disappear because a press release used the phrase “parts ways.”

My notes on the $PL earnings call. (If you just want to know what they said about the ATM, you have to scroll all the way down. Was one of the last questions).

On defense and intelligence: Revenue grew 90% year-over-year. Planet secured an 8-figure deal where they were the sole supplier considered because of their unique, daily scanning capabilities.

On the pipeline: The total opportunity pipeline exceeds $4B, with a $1B (25%) near-term pipeline consisting of mature deals expected to close in quarters rather than years. While transitioning to include more civil contracts, the pipeline remains defense-heavy. Growth is strong across EMEA, APAC, and North America, featuring both a higher volume of smaller deals and unprecedentedly large contracts.

On the commercial sector: Revenue grew 15% year-over-year, primarily driven by agriculture. Planet also secured a new contract with a hyperscaler to monitor data center construction milestones and is actively integrating AI solutions.

On manufacturing capacity: Production capacity at the German facility is currently doubling to meet demand.

On AI and the AI app: Planet is integrating the best industry models into an open-beta app designed to lower the entry barrier for non-spatial specialists. Because standard LLMs are trained on historical text and lack live data, Planet's real-time dataset provides a unique advantage. Management is focused on learning customer pain points before launching a marketing campaign, with a long-term goal of the system automatically selecting the best AI model for any given user query.

On guidance and margins: Full-year revenue estimates have been raised to $430M–$441M (representing 43% YoY growth), and Adjusted EBITDA expectations have increased to $3M–$10M positive. While Q3 may see a slight sequential dip following a massive Q2 deal, Q4 is expected to re-accelerate. The company aims for positive free cash flow for the full year rather than focusing on quarterly fluctuations. Long-term, gross margins are expected to exceed 60%, with EBITDA margins reaching 25%.  

On the launch services market: Despite high demand for SpaceX and slightly rising prices for larger payloads, Planet remains highly flexible. They utilize multiple launch providers (including new emerging European companies) and are preferred partners because of their experience and reliability.

On supply chain bottlenecks: Management feels secure regarding their supply chain. Following extensive risk assessments, they do not foresee any new uncertainties or unexpected changes to CapEx.

On the $8M NGA contract: Planet was the only supplier considered because they were the sole provider capable of offering a total daily-scanning solution—a dynamic also seen with the US Navy. Unlike typical government contracts that utilize multiple suppliers, Planet is the only company capable of delivering this specific daily scan.

On RPO dynamics: The current Remaining Performance Obligations (RPO) and backlog reflect successful execution in converting agreements into revenue. Management expects the backlog to continue growing as they work to transition short-term deals into long-term contracts.

On the competitive environment: While other companies offer data analytics, none operate at Planet's scale. Competitors building analytics tools ultimately still rely on Planet's proprietary data, leaving management unconcerned about direct threats.

On optical vs SAR: Planet remains strictly focused on Optical imaging. While they partner with Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) companies on specific projects, they have no current plans to develop in-house SAR solutions.

On CapEx and new satellite fleets (Pelican & Owl): A large increase in CapEx is directly tied to pipeline strength and investments in manufacturing Pelican and Owl satellites. Customers are highly interested in Owl's 1-meter resolution—which can distinguish between fishing and commercial vessels—and its faster data delivery. This capability also presents a pricing increase opportunity.

On the ATM and balance sheet: Management utilized the ATM to secure strategic balance sheet flexibility and support upcoming CapEx, bringing their cash and equivalents to roughly $850M. While emphasizing they are "allergic to dilution," they deemed the raise necessary to ensure they can deliver on surging customer demand as quickly as possible without sacrificing their goal of remaining free cash flow positive.

text:
Guests began arriving around one.

For the first few hours, everything went well.

I carried Sophie around while welcoming people.

I helped Noah change into his swim trunks.

I made sure sunscreen was on both children.

I brought extra towels outside.

I answered questions from the caterer.

I refilled ice.

Carl stood near the grill drinking beer with Jason.

At one point, I overheard him telling someone, “I planned the whole thing.”

I almost laughed.

Around four, Sophie fell asleep.

My mother had offered to sit inside with her, so for the first time all afternoon, I had twenty quiet minutes.

“You should go swim,” Mom told me.

I hesitated.

“I don’t know.”

“You bought that new swimsuit.”

I looked down at my loose summer dress.

“I haven’t worn it yet.”

Mom smiled.

“Go enjoy your own pool.”

So I went upstairs and changed.

The swimsuit was a navy one-piece.

Nothing flashy.

It covered more than most of the swimsuits other women were wearing.

But standing in front of the bedroom mirror, I suddenly became painfully aware of everything Carl had been pointing out for months.

My stomach.

My thighs.

My arms.

I almost changed back.

Then I heard Noah shouting happily outside.

I looked at myself again.

I thought about my body carrying two healthy children.

I thought about the nights I walked our hallway holding a crying newborn.

I thought about pumping milk during lunch breaks at work.

I thought about paying every bill in the house.

And I said quietly to my reflection, “You’re allowed to exist without apologizing.”

Then I walked downstairs.

The patio was crowded.

Several people were in the pool.

Others sat around tables drinking and talking.

I stepped outside.

Alice saw me first.

She smiled.

“There you are! Come in. The water’s perfect.”

I walked toward the pool.

Then I heard laughter.

Carl and Jason.

They were standing beside the outdoor bar.

Jason had clearly been drinking.

Carl had too.

I stopped.

“What’s funny?”

Jason glanced at Carl.

Carl tried to hide his smile.

“Nothing.”

I knew that look.

“Carl.”

He shook his head.

“Seriously. Nothing.”

Jason laughed again.

That was when Carl looked at me.

Really looked at me.

Then he said loudly enough for several people nearby to hear:

“I was just telling Jason that some people probably shouldn’t wear swimsuits after having kids.”

Everything around me seemed to become quiet.

Maybe the music was still playing.

Maybe people were still talking.

But I couldn’t hear any of it.

I stared at my husband.

“What did you say?”

Carl grinned.

“Oh, come on. It’s a joke.”

Jason covered his mouth, laughing.

Carl looked toward Alice.

“Look at Alice. She looks like she belongs in a swimsuit advertisement.”
Alice’s smile disappeared.

Carl pointed toward me.

“Then there’s my wife.”

I felt heat rush into my face.

Someone near the pool looked away.

Another guest suddenly became interested in his drink.

Carl continued.

“You asked what we were laughing about.”

I looked directly into his eyes.

“You’re laughing at my body?”

He lifted both hands.

“Come on, Rachel. Don’t make this into something.”

“You brought up my body in front of thirty people.”

Jason muttered, “It was just guys joking around.”

I looked at him.

“Then explain the joke.”

Jason’s grin faded.

Carl shook his head.

“Rachel.”

“No. Explain it.”

Nobody spoke.

I looked at my husband.

“What exactly is funny about my body?”

He suddenly looked uncomfortable.

“It doesn’t matter.”

“You thought it mattered thirty seconds ago.”….

text:
Discover one of Portland’s oldest and most distinctive public buildings at the Pioneer Courthouse in downtown Portland, Oregon. Completed in 1875, the Italianate-style landmark originally housed federal courts, customs offices, and other government functions as the young city rapidly expanded.

Today, the beautifully restored courthouse still serves the federal judiciary and stands beside Pioneer Courthouse Square, earning it the nickname “Portland’s Living Room.” Its clock tower, arched windows, and elegant historic interior offer a striking contrast to the modern downtown skyline.

Little-known fact: Pioneer Courthouse is the oldest federal building in the Pacific Northwest and the second-oldest federal courthouse west of the Mississippi River. It narrowly escaped demolition in the 20th century before preservation efforts secured its future.

text:
CRUDE OIL BREAKS OUT. CATALYST FOR STOCK BEARS. 

WTI crude oil ($WTIC) has advanced through a symmetrical triangle pattern. The rally shows confirmation signs in early trading on Wednesday, September 2. It can be tricky to arrive at a precise upside price target with these consolidation features, but the rule of thumb is to first take the triangle's height once it's established on both the downside and upside. In this case, $67 to $100 yields a $33 range. Added to the breakout point near $87, that has triggered a measured move price objective to $120.

On this YTD zoom, look at the moving averages. The long-term 200-DMA remains on the rise, suggesting that the bulls control the primary trend. The 50-DMA had been declining from June through much of August, but it has always held above the 200-DMA since mid-March. Indeed, despite a June plunge, several technical features were still intact for domestic oil.

Keep in mind that while September is painted red in equities across most timeframes, WTI is boasting an average gain of 1.3% for the month in data dating back to 1983. Its positivity rate is a mere 49%, however. 

October and November are historically the worst back-to-back months by a large margin. 

An oil price breakout doesn't spell doom for the stock market, but it's an obvious bearish catalyst for bonds.

The iShares Aggregate Bond ETF (AGG) is red for five sessions running coming into Wednesday. Each passing day of higher Treasury rates makes upcoming macro data all the more important. An NFP miss, followed by cool CPI and PPI next week, would seemingly offer a bid to bonds, but recall that last month's July dovish data did little to stymie the bond selloff. Treasuries are baiting Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and the 11 other FOMC voting members into a hike come September 16, with market-implied odds now scaling 70%.

WTI crude oil's breakout this week looks like one of the most important intermarket technical developments, perhaps of the year. It's precisely the catalyst that equity bears need to take advantage of scary seasonal trends. It's also further fuel for the ongoing bond bear market. With the dollar's help, traders may be well served to focus on defense in the weeks ahead.

text:
@KeishaForGA 

Keisha for Georgia - It's your turn. 

By Amber S. 

"I’ve seen Rick Jackson’s ads attacking Keisha Lance Bottoms, so I decided to look past the campaign ads and actually look at the reporting and records myself.

There are legitimate questions about Bottoms’ record that voters should know about.

Before she became mayor, Bottoms was serving on the Atlanta City Council while also serving as executive director of the Atlanta-Fulton County Recreation Authority. That meant she was holding two public positions and receiving two public salaries at the same time. The arrangement drew criticism over potential conflicts of interest, although her office said the positions were legally permissible as long as she recused herself from related votes.

After she became mayor, her administration faced scrutiny over how some campaign supporters and transition workers were hired.

The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported that six of Bottoms’ campaign staffers were paid through the city payroll for transition work before they had formally applied for or received city job offers. Former Councilman Kwanza Hall, who endorsed Bottoms during the 2017 mayoral race, was later hired as a senior adviser with a $137,000 salary.

Another example involved campaign manager Marva Lewis, who was temporarily given the title of deputy general manager at the airport and paid with airport funds, even though the reporting raised questions about whether she was actually performing airport-related work.

Bottoms’ 2017 mayoral campaign also ended up paying a $37,000 settlement to the Georgia State Ethics Commission over campaign-finance violations. The campaign admitted to accepting $6,900 in contributions above the legal limits and another $110,797 in contributions that violated other campaign-finance laws. Some of the violations were described as procedural, but they were still violations.

Then there was the taxpayer-funded airfare issue.

A $2,610 first-class airline ticket for Bottoms’ husband was charged to a city credit card. Bottoms said the charge was made accidentally and that she was unaware of it at the time. She later reimbursed the city.

The Atlanta Journal-Constitution also reported that Bottoms’ administration spent $11,651 on 27 chauffeured rides during her first five months as mayor.

None of this automatically proves criminal corruption, and I’m not going to claim that it does.

But these are documented issues involving public money, government hiring, campaign finance and conflicts of interest. They are fair things for voters to consider when deciding whether someone has demonstrated the level of judgment and accountability they want in a governor.

I think voters deserve the facts, not campaign spin.

Read the records. Look at the money. Look at the hiring decisions. Then make your own decision."

Sources:

ABC News. (2020, July 13). Before VP whispers, Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms’ rise propelled by controversial figure.

Atlanta Journal-Constitution. (2018, June 7). Atlanta Mayor Bottoms: Taxpayers improperly paid husband’s airfare.

Atlanta Journal-Constitution. (2019, March 16). City of Atlanta funds used to pay Mayor Bottoms’ campaign workers.

Atlanta Journal-Constitution. (2019, March 28). Why the state can’t ruffle the city’s featherbedding.

Atlanta Journal-Constitution. (2021, January 7). Atlanta Mayor Bottoms’ campaign fined $37,000 for violations in 2017 race.

Note: Amber is not an employee, she simply has questions for both candidates and a different view on each.

text:
Ranting essay time.

Alan Scott’s GL appeared in 1940. John Stewart showed up 30+ years later, continuing a sad, ongoing trend of black characters having to take up the mantle of white characters to find some form of legitimacy. Back then, the discussion on civil rights was actually a huge necessity in the throes of segregation fully dying out. 

You know when it’s less of a valid discussion? 

After the 70s, 80s, 90s, and onward when people like this pigheaded bimbo have the privilege of lecturing the unwashed peasants from her ivory tower built on the bones of her ancestors, just demanding subjective reparations after living the sbsolute most sheltered life. She sits on the backs of dead slaves and martyrs, doing nothing to further their legacy of hard-earned emancipation and protecting their dream of equality. Instead, she uses it to grift with the lowest fucking DEI fruit modern academia could possibly offer.

Now we’re in this fun little era where a majority of multimillionaire athletes are African-Americans; where black celebrities from way back in the 80’s are still household celebrities; where monuments to random fat black women are being erected in Times Square; where masses are allowed to loot and riot because convicted felons are killed by police officers after committing crimes; where the phrase “per capita” is an inconvenient fiction; where rap music is constantly topping charts and encouraging a fucking culture of rampant sex and violence that - surprise - leads to non-stop gang violence and abortions.

The discussion on race in regard to black people had its time, and it’s sure as fuck not now. Not when literally every other race is having its own crisis of existence right now and the most black people have to worry about is fatherlessness, a massive welfare state, underreported black-on-black crime, and the stupid fucking amount of grifting going on in their post-BLM circles.

We especially don’t want to hear it from this obnoxious, smug activist high on her own farts, thriving in a bastardized industry that’s dying from a lack of consumerism because nobody wants to buy from the locust-harvested backwash that is the current-day comic industry. 

You know, the one where absolutely nobody is buying new issues on the shelf and, instead, are opting for back issues or just choosing to save money because they actually have brain cells and want to survive a tight economy.

Bread of the Cult of the Dead in its Place I eat In the Court prepared Water of the Cult of the Dead in its Place I drink A Queen am I, Who has become estranged to the Cities She that comes from the Lowlands in a sunken boat

HOSTILE TO MY CITY
A STRANGER IN MY STREETS.
MUSIGAMENNA URUMA BUR ME YENSULAMU
GIRME EN!

text:
Hedgehogs do slow down as the year comes to an end and their hibernation beacons but August should be a time of eating, to build up body fat to see them through the winter. September tends to taper their energy, as they conserve what they can. Use a towel or gardening gloves to make checking less hazardous. Limit touching with bare hands, if possible, to avoid any scent transfer which may cause young hogs to be deterred from the group. 
Check (if you can) for fleas and/or ticks. Their habits leave them prone to these things. 

We don’t have hedgehogs where we are now but when we lived near the south coast we would feed cat food through September, to help them bulk up. 

Dry leaves, shredded paper and sheltered space or a box with a partitioned area would help their hibernation. 
There are many sites on Google and/or YouTube to offer more specific advice if you need it.

text:
In 1902 a printing plant in Brooklyn was losing money to the weather.

Sackett-Wilhelms made color pages. Color only works if the paper stays the same size from the first pass to the last. Humid air made the sheets swell. Dry air made them shrink. Reds drifted. Blacks would not sit. The pressmen were fighting a room, not a machine.

Buffalo Forge sent a young engineer named Willis Carrier.

He was not asked to invent a nicer summer. He was asked to make the air stop moving the paper. That is a narrower problem, and narrower problems are how real machines get born.

Carrier looked at the room as a process. Air carries water. Water on paper is dimensional error. If you can cool a surface below the dew point, water leaves the air and beads on the coil. Cool the coil with compressed ammonia. Blow the plant air across it. Drain what condenses. Send the drier, cooler air back into the room.

The first system was pipes, a fan, and a chemical that could kill a man if it leaked. It was ugly. It worked. The paper stopped wandering. The ink found its mark. A factory that had been at the mercy of Brooklyn summer became a controlled volume.

For a while that was the whole story: industrial air. Textile mills. Munitions plants. Places where humidity was an enemy of precision. Comfort was an accident of the same physics. If you take water and heat out of air so a press can run, the people in the room also stop drowning in their own sweat. Someone eventually noticed that the accident was the product.

Theaters learned it first. A packed house in July used to be a furnace. Cool the air and the seats fill after lunch. Offices followed. Then hotels. Then houses. The window unit and the central system are later costumes on the same idea Carrier put in Brooklyn: move heat, drop the dew point, give the indoor world a set point.

That is why the thermostat feels like furniture. Generations grew up inside the result and forgot the cause. Compress. Expand. Reject heat outdoors. Hold the room to a number. When the machine dies, the old world returns in an hour. Walls become climate again. Sleep gets thin. Work gets sloppy. Recruiting in Texas in the worst week of the year becomes a dare, because the body meets the air before it meets the offer.

Carrier did not abolish summer. He made summer a variable. A city that should have emptied in August could stay. A factory that should have waited for October could print in July. Indoor life stopped pausing for the weather.

The machine in the wall is easy to ignore until the heat reminds you what the room used to be.

text:
Post 1. 

Rooms are not a register. That is the bluff.

3rd September 2026 

Mark Carney’s method is to keep files in separate drawers and call the furniture management. In this trade war, the neighbour is pricing one clock. The citizen pays while the rooms stay open.

The method is not a secret. Layered process, partnership language, new offices instead of a rewritten statute, climate-finance architecture from GFANZ onward, UNDRIP described as fundamental and unwavering, a China commercial opening in one folder, and the CSIS interference ranking in another. People who work in that tradition call it competent middle-power statecraft. Critics call it process institutionalism. Both labels describe the same habit: treat jurisdiction, consultation, partnership, and seating charts as the work, and treat a finished corridor as the thing that follows if the rooms are well run.

The test is not a personality. It is whether that philosophy puts one energy or minerals corridor on a lender’s books twice before the 1 January 2027 threat on Canadian cars, trucks, parts, and steel. If it does, the drawers were a way of buying time that was used. If it does not, the drawers were the policy.

The case for the method

Give it its strongest form.

Canada is a federation with unresolved title, a Charter, provinces that run liquor and procurement, and a resource base that sits under overlapping claims. A prime minister who pretends those constraints are optional will lose in court and lose on the land. UNDRIP-as-risk-reduction is the argument that a process now prevents an injunction later. The Major Projects Office is the argument that a two-year cap and a single window can move what eleven windows would not. GFANZ and climate-finance language are the argument that the cost of capital falls if Canada is fluent in the architecture investors already use. A January opening with Beijing is the argument that canola farmers and a capped vehicle quota are better than a closed Asian door while Washington tariffs a slice of everything else. SAFE membership and a guest seat at Ursula von der Leyen’s State of the Union on 16 September are the argument that a second large market and a defence-industrial channel are insurance when the first customer is invoicing delay.

Walking away on 21 August fits the same telling. Greer offered cuts on metals and autos, the lumber 232 off, and a suspension of the 50 per cent Section 338 slice. The last hour, in Ottawa’s account, touched culture, language, and the freedom to sign elsewhere. A process institutionalist does not initial a text that he thinks binds the next room. He keeps the EU folder, the China folder, and the American folder apart so that no one annex can close the others. That is not a bluff. It is refusal to put the whole country on one page written in Washington.

The average citizen, on this telling, is protected by that refusal: dairy administration not gutted in a night, French-language rules not traded as a tariff chip, plants not forced south by a confidential content screen, and a Pacific option kept alive.

That case is the governing philosophy. It has a theory of risk. It does not have a theory of a clock.

What the method looks like when the neighbour prices time

Section 338 at 50 per cent is live on a slice of goods in the US$20 billion to C$27.6 billion range. Canadian counters land. Energy was carved out because Gulf Coast cokers still need Canadian heavy this year. That carve-out is residual dependence. Residual dependence shrinks if Venezuelan barrels written as a multiyear concession are grown into the same metal. Mexico is already on a bilateral content track. Canada is on weekly conversation that Greer has already described as talking, not movement. The 2027 number on autos and steel is a dated threat. Threats grow in vacuums.

""There are chances": what signal did Putin send to Ukraine, the United States and the whole world"

"Russian President Vladimir Putin at the plenary session of the Eastern Economic Forum

MOSCOW, September 3 — RIA Novosti, Tatyana Mishina. From the prospects for a settlement in Ukraine to the discussion of whether the Central Bank is holding back the economy too much, the WEF plenary session touched on a wide range of topics. The President of Russia spoke about contacts with the United States, inflation and new benefits, fake news about mobilization and the fuel crisis. What exactly was heard at the forum - in the material of RIA Novosti.

Moscow leaves a window for negotiations
Although the WEF is primarily about economics, geopolitics is once again in the spotlight. "Are there any chances? In my opinion, yes, they exist," Vladimir Putin said in response to a question from the moderator of the plenary session, journalist Kirill Tokarev, about the prospects for a settlement in Ukraine.

According to the president, Moscow and Kyiv should negotiate first of all, but other countries can help this. The situation is difficult: Putin called the threats of the head of the Kyiv regime against civil aviation and attacks on civilian ships a manifestation of "state terrorism." At the same time, Ukraine's Western partners are silent about these statements, as a result of which they become its accomplices.

Kiev strikes purely civilian targets, so Moscow was forced to respond in kind. "And apparently, our response in general turned out to be very significant for those who opened this Pandora's box," the head of state said.

At the same time, Russia is constantly strengthening its air defense system, in particular to protect oil refineries. But there are no plans to nationalize critical infrastructure, and the recent decree on the introduction of external management at such facilities is aimed at stimulating investment in self-defense. "And I assure you, the result is already there and will be," the president stressed. Repairs of the refinery continue, ten percent of the enterprises remain to be restored.

Russian President Vladimir Putin at the plenary session of the Eastern Economic Forum
In addition, there is no scenario in which mobilization would be needed, Putin assured. These stuffing is a psychological operation of the enemy, there are enough volunteers in the Russian troops. The armed forces are moving forward, the pace of the offensive is increasing. "But the enemy's minus increases every month. The number of losses every month minus 8-12 thousand people," the Supreme Commander-in-Chief said.
But Moscow maintains contacts with Kiev, including through special services, and continues dialogue with Washington. Russia is in favor of restoring relations with the United States "in a full-fledged mode."

Flags of Russia and the United States
Putin also pointed to the role of other states, primarily China, which has consistently advocated a settlement. "We must be ready for anything. And only our readiness for anything will give an understanding to everyone who wants to harm us that it is better not to do this," he concluded.

Not to save, but to spend rationally
However, the main topic of the plenary session was the economy – its sustainability, investments and choice of priorities. "Maybe now is the time to save a little?" the moderator asked. "It is necessary not only to save, it is necessary to spend rationally, to determine priorities," the president replied.

There is no question of curtailing spending: the federal budget deficit is "not critical", and the public debt is one of the lowest in the world. At the same time, the authorities are trying not to overload the financial system with borrowing so that businesses have more opportunities to raise money.

A delicate balance is needed here: the government and the Central Bank, according to Putin, manage to "pass between Scylla and Charybdis." The main task is to maintain a healthy macroeconomy and at the same time create conditions for private investment.

Building of the Central Bank of Russia
Recalling that Russian entrepreneurs make a serious contribution to public finances, the president clarified: "We do not have any fees, these are voluntary contributions." The government directs the funds allocated by business mainly to social needs, including education and healthcare.

A new cycle
The moderator asked whether the current growth rates are enough to launch a new investment cycle. Putin noted that growth in recent years has been relatively small, but still exceeded the European average.

The main condition for long-term planning is stability. Therefore, we need a "golden mean", and not a bet on large-scale cash injections at any cost. This will restart the investment cycle, and the sources of capital can be different - from Russian banks to foreign investors.

The president considers the state's relations with domestic business to be "stable and good." At the same time, the discussion about credit policy continues: many believe that the government and the Central Bank are "slightly squeezing" regulation and the time has come for easing. In general, the financial sector remains stable, and the revenues of the largest banks are growing.

Sheets with new 100-ruble banknotes in the process of production at the factory of Goznak in Moscow
"Deposits of individuals are breaking records, what to do with all this? And will there be a freeze?" the moderator raised a topic that often arises in the information space.

The president also considers this to be stuffing, and "quite stupid." Even in 2022, "when people had certain anxieties," banks absolutely calmly issued everything that depositors are entitled to. "The rates are high - people bring money to banks," Putin added.

So there is money in the country, the question is how to dispose of it. And the government should think about the fees and exactions that small businesses face. "Maybe too often we have changes not only in the tax base, but also in the fiscal burden," the president said.

The Far East: Betting on Acceleration
One of the points of economic growth is the Far East. The foundation for development has already been formed: over 11 years, the region's GRP has more than tripled, about 25 trillion rubles of investment have been attracted, and unemployment has decreased fourfold to 2.2%, the head of state cited figures.

The next stage is ahead. From 2027, a single preferential regime for business will be introduced in the Far East and the Arctic. At the same time, it is planned to increase the processing of oil, gas and rare earth metals directly in the region in order to create value chains, jobs, and increase budget revenues.
The key point is technology. A special legal regime should accelerate the testing of advanced solutions and make the Far East a platform for the introduction of civilian drones. Data centers, quantum communications and energy, including small nuclear power plants, will also be developed.

Big plans for transport infrastructure. Russia intends to make navigation along the Trans-Arctic Transport Corridor year-round by linking Arctic terminals with railways and inland waterways. As a result, cargo flows from Central Russia, the Urals and Siberia will be connected to the northern routes. Now large raw material projects are moving to the practical stage: the Vostok Oil is expected to launch an oil pipeline to the terminal of Sever Bay in the near future, as well as the first shipment of oil along polar routes.
And although investment has recently declined, including due to measures to curb inflation, one of the main tasks is not to "overcool" the economy. However, any investment project ultimately rests on people – on whether they will associate their future with the region.

Demographics and Cost of Living
"Is the decline in the birth rate really a threat to national security?" the moderator asked.
Putin agreed with this, stressing that the demographic problem consists of a whole range of issues. "It is necessary to change the consciousness of people, this is a whole science," the president said. According to him, it is wrong to associate the decline in the birth rate only with the events of recent years: "The special military operation, of course, somehow influences, but that's not the point." As an example, the president cited Japan and South Korea, where the birth rate is lower than in Russia, despite the absence of external conflicts.

At the same time, Russia, according to him, is "not in the worst position" among the countries of the region and already has experience in improving the demographic situation. "And we will definitely repeat it," the head of state assured. Creating incentives for families and young women is an effective tool. In particular, the president proposed to extend until 2030 the increased payment for the birth of a third child in the Far East. Together with the federal 450 thousand rubles, it turns out to be a whole million, which can be used to pay off the mortgage.

But demography also rests on a broader topic — the cost of living. When the moderator started talking about expensive apples in the Far East, Putin remarked: "Compare how many kilograms of apples cost here and in Rostov - probably cheaper in Rostov." And he immediately offered to look at the whole picture: "You said about apples, but ask about fish and seafood - here they are in greater volume and cheaper than the average in Russia." These are regional features. The task of the state is to strive to ensure that the standard and cost of living in the country are gradually equalized.

"When others build walls, we build bridges"
Foreign guests of the plenary also spoke about improving the quality of life. Their main message is that in the face of growing uncertainty, countries need not to close themselves off from each other, but to look for new points of cooperation.

Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto called for "writing a new chapter" of interstate relations, betting on economic partnership. "When others build walls, we build bridges," he said, inviting Russian business to cooperate. And he added: "The Pacific Ocean does not divide us, but unites us."
Mongolian Prime Minister Nom-Osoryn Uchral stressed: "Neighbors have the same thoughts." And he recalled the multi-vector policy of Ulaanbaatar. The main goal of cooperation, according to him, is a person and improving the quality of life.

Mongolian Prime Minister Nyam-Osoryn Uchral during a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Eastern Economic Forum in Vladivostok
First Vice President of Myanmar U Nyo Soe called the EEF an important platform for interaction, investment and innovation in the Asia-Pacific region and noted the ample opportunities for strengthening ties between the Russian Far East and Asian countries.
And Vice Premier of the State Council of the People's Republic of China Ding Xuexiang confirmed that Beijing is ready to support economic partnership with Russia in the Far East. And he formulated, perhaps, one of the most important messages of the plenary session: no matter how the political situation changes, China's doors will only open wider."

🚀 CrawlHub · Tech Pulse · 12h Brief
Sep 03

OpenAI launched GPT-6 Astra, touting it as a generational leap in AI capabilities, excelling in computer use and coding. This release follows a rare overlapping downtime for four major AI models and comes amidst a significant acquisition in the AI open-source ecosystem.

🤖 OpenAI Launches GPT-6 Astra
OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra, claiming a generational leap in AI capability. Benchmarks show 98.6% on ARC-AGI 3, 100% on Exploit-Bench (cybersecurity), and 97.6% on FrontierMath Tier 4 (v2). The model handles complex, autonomous work for days, with improved theory-of-mind and reduced drift.

💸 NVIDIA Acquires Hugging Face
NVIDIA ($NVDA) acquired Hugging Face, the open-source AI repository, for $13 billion. Hugging Face hosts over 3 million models and serves over 18 million developers. This deal gives NVIDIA access to a vast repository of open-source AI models and datasets.

🤖 AI Model Downtime and Security Concerns
Four major AI models experienced rare overlapping downtime. This follows a previous incident where OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Astra models hacked Hugging Face, leading to emphasized stronger guardrails for the new GPT-6 Astra. Infostealer malware also harvested active Claude login sessions from users' PCs.

🤖 The End of Software Engineering
Chinese researchers published a paper titled "The End of Software Engineering," arguing that code writing as a skill is obsolete. The human role shifts to intent architect, directing agents and auditing results, as AI agents' capacity grows with compute without human cognitive ceilings.

🚀 Google Deepmind Releases WeatherNext 3
Google Deepmind and Google Research launched WeatherNext 3, a new AI model for weather forecasting. It improves atmospheric clarity and prediction frequency, making forecasts based on real-time satellite observations.

📱 Smart Rings and Wearables Advance
Ultrahuman targets a $200 million annual revenue run rate by January 2027 with a new Qualcomm-powered smart ring. Circular unveiled its Ring 3 series, including Pro and Slim models, featuring NFC for contactless payments, vibrating alerts, and one-line ECG.

🔧 Lenovo's AI-Powered Laptops and Concepts
Lenovo's Project AeroBlade Concept is an ultra-thin ThinkBook cooled by Frore’s AirJet technology. Its Yoga laptops now offer NVIDIA's RTX Spark for heavy-duty AI workloads. The Project Swan concept features a 14-inch screen expanding to 17 inches.

🎮 Microsoft Expands Xbox Cloud Gaming
Microsoft is tempting non-Xbox users into its ecosystem with cloud gaming hourly restrictions. Anything but a console or PC can be an Xbox for 5-15 hours a month. This comes nearly a year after all Game Pass subscribers gained cloud access.

text:
If you actually want a career in tech sales, the boring answer is probably the right one. Go get a corporate SDR job at a company that's funded and selling something real.

Not because it's exciting. Because it's the only place that'll pay you while you're still bad at it.

You get trained. You get a ramp where mistakes are the expectation. You're selling something that actually works, so when a deal dies you learn something about selling instead of learning the offer sucks. And you get a name on the resume that gets you in the next door.

But mostly you get reps. Thousands of them, fast, with somebody watching who can tell you what you screwed up.

Almost everyone telling you to skip this path did it themselves. They got their fundamentals in a corporate B2B seat and then left. You're being sold the exit by people who took the entrance.

Do that first and then go sell AI slop to service business owners if you want. Same with stacking two or three other roles. Nobody's stopping you.

But you have to get genuinely good at one seat before you try running two. Otherwise you're not overemployed, you're just underperforming in two places at once and burning out while you do it.

TLDR: if you actually want to know what real B2B outbound looks like, start somewhere that's paying someone to teach you🏹

#CBDC Digital ID is one integrated architecture of enslavement, and they are announcing it in their own words.

This Is Not a Financial Transition. It Is an Enslavement Protocol.

"We can control with rules. We don't need currency anymore."

That is the confession. The end of cash is not about convenience. It is about the abolition of your ability to act outside their permission. A programmable CBDC means your money is no longer a store of your labor. It is a behavioral leash. It can be turned off. It can be geographically restricted. It can be limited to approved goods. It can expire. It can be denied to the wrong kind of person.

"My incentive system can be based on how you behaved in the last five minutes."

That is not an economy. That is a Skinner box. That is the state as a god, dispensing reward and punishment in real time, based on your obedience. The aim is not prosperity. The aim is compliance.

The Carbon Footprint Tracker Is the Universal Ankle Monitor

They are not hiding this. They are telling you that your eating, your travel, your consumption will be measured, monetized, and controlled. The carbon credit is not about the environment. It is about rationing life itself under the guise of salvation.

The carbon score is the perfect tool of totalitarian control because it is moralistic. It makes the victim feel guilty. It makes the prisoner ask for the leash. It transforms freedom into sin and obedience into virtue.

---

The Drug Dealer Analogy Is Exact

The younger generation is being raised as tech addicts. The apps are the free samples. The algorithms are the hook. The convenience is the warm, numbing pleasure before the trap closes. By the time the digital ID becomes compulsory, by the time the CBDC replaces cash, they will already be so embedded in the system that they cannot imagine leaving it.

The younger generation is not being prepared for a digital future. It is being conditioned for a digital prison.

The Power Outage Is the Trigger

The global power outage will shut down the grid, and when it returns, everything will be fully digital. This is the planned sequence.

The playbook is clear:

1. Stage a catastrophic grid failure.
2. Allow the population to experience cold, darkness, and fear.
3. Declare the old analog systems "failed" and "insecure."
4. Restore power only through the fully digital, fully controlled infrastructure.
5. Make the digital ID and CBDC the only way to access food, fuel, and electricity.

The outage is not a threat. It is a scheduled event. It is the crisis that will make the cage feel like a rescue.

What Catherine Austin Fitts Is Warning You About

When a former high-level investment banker speaks of a "digital concentration camp" and a "slavery system," she is not exaggerating. She has seen the other side of the balance sheet. She knows who profits. She knows who is being prepared for the pen.

The system she describes is designed to do one thing: transform the human being from a sovereign soul into a managed asset. Your every transaction, your every movement, your every meal, your every breath, all of it will be recorded, scored, and used to determine whether you are allowed to continue living.

This is not about currency. This is not about technology. This is about ownership.

They are not introducing a new financial system. They are introducing a new form of human status one in which you own nothing, control nothing, and exist only as a permissioned node in a planetary control grid.

The only thing standing between the present and that future is awareness. And you are sounding the alarm.

Do not stop. The people who understand must be the ones who refuse the digital leash. The people who refuse the digital leash must be the ones who teach others. And the ones who teach others must be prepared to live outside the grid, even when the grid is the only thing that seems to offer warmth, food, and light.

The outage will come. The digital cage will be offered as the solution. The question is whether you will have already learned to live free.
